60-70% for coil springs. Peak capacity utilisation is targeted around Q2-Q3FY28, with asset turnover expected at 2.5-2.75x.
Customer Qualification & Competitive Advantage
• New OEM customer onboarding typically takes 12-24 months, involving technical audits, plant visits, sample development,
testing and customer validation. Following qualification, Gala typically receives 20-25% of the customer's business. Key
competitive advantages include technical capability, process stability, stringent quality standards and long-standing customer
relationships. Critical processes such as heat treatment and shot peening are 100% in-house, supporting consistent spring
performance.
Renewable Energy & New Applications
• Renewable Energy contributes 35-38% of sales and remains a key growth driver, with management seeing strong demand from
India and Europe despite a slowdown in the US post-FY25/26. Gala's wallet share with major renewable OEMs remains <10%,
providing significant headroom. The company supplies fasteners and disc springs for wind, hydro, electrolysers and gas
turbines. Electrolyser commercial scaling is expected beyond FY30, following commercial orders secured after a pilot with L&T.
Industrial, Railways & Mobility
• Industrial, Renewable Energy and Railways are expected to drive growth over the next 2-3 years. Railway applications include
wedge-lock washers, coil springs and specialised fasteners for high-speed trains, metros and private rolling-stock
manufacturers. Automotive contributes 20% of revenue, with 65% of automotive sales linked to heavy commercial vehicles and
tractors. Brake and seatbelt-retractor applications are largely ICE/EV agnostic, limiting near-term EV transition risk.
Exports & Revenue Visibility
• Exports contribute 36-38% of sales and management expects the mix to remain broadly stable. OEMs provide annual demand
forecasts, while firm POs are generally received 12-16 weeks ahead of dispatch. Gala has firm visibility for one quarter of
dispatches and broader demand visibility for one year. Export and domestic margin profiles are broadly similar, while INR
depreciation supports export competitiveness.
Working Capital
• Working capital remains an important area of focus, with the overall cycle at 175 days, comprising inventory of 120 days,
receivables of 90-94 days and payables of 20-30 days. Receivables have increased by 10-15 days due to longer export transit
times and some customer collection delays. KPMG has been appointed for working-capital optimisation, with management
targeting a 15-20% reduction over the next 9-12 months.
Capex & Expansion
• Chennai Phase 1 has been completed, while Phase 2 involves INR 150 mn of additional capex and is targeted for completion by
March 2027. Minor line-balancing capex at Wada is also expected to be completed during the current fiscal year. Gala has
signed an MOU for additional land at Wada, subject to legal due diligence. Remaining cash is earmarked for land acquisition and
potential inorganic opportunities.
Automation & Inorganic Growth
• Gala has invested in automation, semi-automation and IoT for 6 years, with the objective of improving quality consistency,
reducing manual dependency and increasing productivity. Inorganic opportunities will focus on precision engineering,
complementary products, customer synergies and businesses with critical technical approvals. Aerospace and Defence remain
potential mid-to-long-term opportunities rather than near-term priorities.

Ganesh Consumer Products Ltd
Business
• Founded in 1936, Ganesh is the oldest and largest consumer staples brand in East India. It leads in wheat-based products and
Sattu across East India and is among the top two in gram-based products.
• The portfolio covers 44 product categories and more than 250 SKUs. Whole wheat Atta is ~32-33% of sales, value-added flours
(Suji, Maida, Besan, Sattu, Dalia) ~55-60%, and emerging products (spices, instant mixes, ethnic flours) the rest.
• Revenue comes from B2C (branded products, SKUs from 10 g to 10 kg) and B2B (sale of by-products and co-products). B2C is
the focus and has grown at a ~12% CAGR over 4 years.
• West Bengal is ~92-93% of sales. Motilal Oswal PE invested INR 1,000 mn in 2016 (INR 600 mn primary, INR 400 mn
secondary), and the stock listed in September 2025.
• FY26 revenue was ~INR 8.7 bn. Revenue grew at a ~12.5% CAGR and EBITDA at ~15% over 4 years. FY26 EBITDA margin was
9.8% and PAT margin ~4.8%.
Guidance
• EBITDA margin is guided at 10-11% on a conservative basis (Q1FY27: 11.2%).
• Management expects the demand slowdown to normalise in 1-2 quarters and is targeting double-digit revenue growth over 3-
4 years.
• Revenue potential from existing capacity is INR 13-14 bn, targeted in 3-4 years. ROCE is 18-20% today at ~56-57% utilisation
and could reach ~42-43% at full utilisation if margins hold.
• Priorities for the next 2-3 years: raising core-category utilisation from ~56-57% to 80-85%, increasing the share of sales outside
West Bengal from ~7-8% to ~15%, entering new adjacent categories (ethnic snacks and packaged sweets), and raising spice
margins to industry levels.
Growth Headwinds
• Emami entered in Q2FY26 with aggressive pricing, which hurt Q3FY26. Management says this has now eased and Nielsen
shows market share improving.
• West Bengal policy change: the new government stopped giving wheat to local millers for ration Atta and now supplies wheat
directly through ration shops. The displaced millers sell small unregistered packs of Atta and Maida at 15-20% below Ganesh.
Management expects their limited working capital to constrain them as wheat inflates by 4-5% a year.
• Higher LPG prices cut Atta and Maida consumption, since rotis use more LPG than rice, and also hit HoReCa demand in Q1.
Direct HoReCa billing is only ~1.5% of B2C.
• Sattu and Suji have grown over Q1-Q2, which management sees as green shoots.
Capacity and Capex
• Atta was at 70% utilisation before the Agra Atta section was commissioned in FY26. Suji runs at 55-60%, and spices are low
because the category is new.
• Narrower UP-Bihar wheat price gaps under OMSS have made shipping from UP less viable. The company is shifting to small,
low-capex Atta plants in Bihar and the Northeast (land acquired in Assam), with Atta as the carrier product and other products
reprocessed locally. Commissioning will take ~2 years.
• A new Besan and Sattu plant in West Bengal, funded by INR 450 mn of IPO proceeds, will bring outsourced volumes in-house
for better margin and consistent quality.
• A snacks and sweets plant is planned near Kolkata.
New Categories
• Spices were launched in 2024 and generated ~INR 380 mn revenue last year, growing ~20%. Margins are currently kept low to
gain penetration and are being raised each year toward industry levels within a couple of years.
• Ethnic snacks were piloted through a contract manufacturer with decent feedback. Management does not plan to enter
competitive snacks such as chips.
• Ethnic snacks and 2-3 packaged sweets are targeted for Q3/Q4FY27. They carry higher ASPs.
• Value-added products command a 35-40% premium to unorganised players.
Distribution and Channels
• The network has more than 30 C&F agents, more than 1,000 distributors, ~0.30-0.35 mn retailers (Nielsen) and more than 1
mn consumer touchpoints.
• E-commerce is ~14% of B2C sales and brick-and-mortar modern trade ~7.3%.
• Products reach Kolkata within ~15 days of manufacture and other districts in 20-25 days.
• Sales outside West Bengal are growing ~15-20% on a small base. Distribution in Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and the Northeast is
being expanded without waiting for the new plants.
• C&F stock is visible in SAP, while distributor stock is tracked manually. A DMS rollout across distributors is underway.

Ganesh Infraworld Ltd
Business
Ganesh Infraworld is a Kolkata-based infrastructure contractor working in 8 states. It started as a partnership in 2017 and became a
public company in June 2024.
It works in water infrastructure, civil and electrical infrastructure (buildings, roads, railways) and civic utilities. Mining is done
through Tycoon Mines, a 60% subsidiary; the other 40% is held by Tycoon's previous promoters.
FY26 consolidated revenue grew ~55% to INR 8,350 mn, EBITDA more than doubled to ~INR 1,050 mn and PAT rose ~90% to ~INR
760 mn.
Q4 was the seventh straight quarter of sequential revenue growth, with revenue of ~INR 2,290 mn and PAT of ~INR 250 mn.
Q1FY27 PAT was ~INR 300 mn (+103%). Standalone revenue was ~INR 2,000 mn and consolidated ~INR 3,700-3,800 mn.
Total assets rose to ~INR 11.5 bn from INR 2.65 bn.
Guidance
FY27 standalone revenue is guided at ~INR 9-10 bn, with a PAT margin of ~8.5-9%. Consolidated revenue is guided at ~INR 18-20 bn,
with a PAT margin of ~8%.
Management expects quarter-on-quarter growth to continue and targets an order book of more than 3x revenue.
Direct orders, rather than subcontracts, should be 70%+ of the order book within 3 years.
Order Book and Bids
The consolidated order book is ~INR 45 bn (INR 43 bn in March). Mining accounts for ~INR 30 bn, all confirmed, for Coal India and
Mahanadi Coalfields, to be executed over 2-3 years.
The standalone order book is ~INR 15 bn: water ~INR 4.5 bn, civil infrastructure ~INR 8-9 bn and civic utilities ~INR 1-2 bn.
New wins include an ~INR 4.5 bn mining order from Central Coalfields over five years and an ~INR 1 bn rail EPC subcontract
(Vikramshila-Katareah) won by Tycoon.
The bid book is ~INR 90 bn: ~INR 40 bn in the subsidiary, with ~50% expected to convert, and ~INR 50 bn standalone, with ~25-30%
expected to convert.
In water, the company is bidding mainly under AMRUT, Namami Gange and irrigation schemes, and is cautious on Jal Jeevan
Mission. It says it has no pending Jal Jeevan receivables.
Mining (Tycoon Mines)
Mining EBITDA margin is ~12-13%. Tycoon has a gross block of more than INR 4 bn, so no further capex is needed.
Work is end-to-end, from removing overburden to coal extraction. Bills are raised monthly and paid within ~20 days, with 5%
retention.
Coal India has absorbed fuel cost increases, so there has been no margin hit, only a cash flow effect.
The largest contract (Kandoi, at the Nigahi mine) runs 7 years, with 3 elapsed. It bills ~INR 450 mn a month, peaking at ~INR 520-530
mn, and management sees a high chance of renewal.
Balance Sheet
Standalone debt is ~INR 1.6 bn (INR 1.2 bn fund-based and INR 400 mn non-fund-based) against net worth of ~INR 2.5 bn. Subsidiary
debt is ~INR 2.6 bn against ~INR 2.5 bn of net worth, so debt-to-equity is ~1x in both.
The reported 1.22x debt-to-equity is distorted because the subsidiary's P&L was consolidated for only one day in FY26 while its full
balance sheet was included.
The subsidiary repays ~INR 100 mn a month in loan instalments, which should reduce finance costs. Warrants worth ~INR 510 mn
are being issued, and no other large fundraise is expected.
Receivable days are ~60-70 for mining, ~70-90 for water and ~80-90 for civil, or ~85-90 days consolidated. Operating cash flow was
negative and is expected to turn positive by year-end.
The top 5 customers are ~70% of revenue: J&K water department, WAPCOS, Welspun Enterprises, Apar Industries and BUIDCO
(Bihar urban development). Concentration follows a few large orders rather than many clients.

Outlook: Management targets FY27 revenue of INR 5-5.5 bn, a 35-49% jump from ~INR 3.7 bn in FY26, and INR 10 bn by FY30.
EBITDA margin is guided at 9-9.5% in FY27, 10%+ in FY28 and 13%+ over the long term. ROCE and ROE, currently compressed, are

Recent Performance: Revenue has historically ranged between INR 3.3 bn and INR 3.8 bn. EBITDA margin is currently 8-9%, with

cumulative revenue over 10 years. Trial orders are under way, and commercial revenue recognition starts in FY28.
Domestic Market & Share Gains: India's welding consumables market is worth INR 120-130 bn and is growing at a 6-8% CAGR.

share from 6-7% to about 12% in 3-4 years, helped by a structural shift toward organised, quality-compliant suppliers.

October 2026, and the commercial IT park project launches in FY27.
Portfolio Expansion: The company is adding flux-cored wire and submerged arc (SAW) fluxes to complete its consumables
portfolio. Equipment shipments from China were delayed by 1-2 months because of visa issues, but they are progressing.
Welding Equipment Entry: The company currently trades welding equipment on a small scale. It plans to enter equipment
manufacturing in FY28/FY29, probably through acquisitions, where margins are 12-14%.
Exports: Exports account for more than 10% of sales, across the Middle East, Eastern Europe and Southeast Asia. They earn higher
margins, and the company's stainless steel products are priced competitively against Chinese supply.
Promoter Pledge: About 46% of promoter shares are pledged against an INR 400 mn personal loan. Management plans to release
the pledge gradually over the next 3-4 years.
Working Capital: Working capital days have stretched because the company built strategic raw material buffers during recent
geopolitical uncertainty. Inventory days should return to normal by end-FY27 without any increase in credit limits.
Long-Term Potential: The specialty mix shift, a nuclear opportunity worth INR 50-60 bn over a decade and organised-market share
gains support the path to INR 10 bn of revenue by FY30 at margins of 13%+. The INR 4 bn from the Thane land monetisation
strengthens the balance sheet further.

Genus Power Infrastructures Ltd
Genus Power's outlook is anchored on a visible electricity smart meter pipeline of ~36.1 mn awarded meters (expandable to ~40-
42.5 mn via the 30% incremental provision), with ~10 mn meters targeted for installation in FY27 and all AMISP projects now
revenue generating, which should drive receivable reduction and operational cash flow positivity by end-FY27 or Q1FY28. Gas
metering is the next growth engine, expected to scale ~8-10x in FY27 with ~INR 350 mn already won in Q1 and a ~INR 350-360 bn
industry opportunity over 5-6 years, while water metering could emerge as an even larger segment in 3-4 years. Margins are
guided at ~18% EBITDA despite currency and crude-linked cost pressures, supported by prudent pricing, in-house moulding, and
deep supplier relationships. Management remains disciplined on pricing, prioritising bottom-line over top-line amid aggressive
competitive bidding, and with a strong AA- credit profile and self-liquidating working capital, Genus is well-positioned to convert
its large order book into sustainable, cash-generating growth.
Business Overview and Strategic Positioning
Genus Power Infrastructures operates across electricity, water, and gas metering, with electricity being the most advanced
segment in India and globally. The company has been awarded ~36.1 mn smart meters under RDSS/AMISP tenders, with ~15 mn
installed as of 30 June and ~21 mn pending. Contracts include a provision for up to 30% incremental meters at the same price,
implying the order book could expand to ~40-42.5 mn meters. Management consciously prioritises bottom-line over top-line and
is willing to sit out aggressively priced tenders.
Electricity Smart Meter Rollout and Run-Rate
Q1FY27 installation stood at ~2.3 mn meters, translating to ~30,000 meters/day, though monsoon slowed the pace. Production in
Q1 was ~4 mn meters, against annual capacity of 18+ mn, with the flexibility to ramp up or down without significant capex. The
FY27 installation target is ~10 mn meters, and the company believes it is on track. All AMISP projects have achieved Operation Go
Live status and are revenue generating. Industry-wide installation is running at ~3-3.5 mn meters/month, expected to rise from
next financial year. Uttar Pradesh is moving slowly until the elections, but there has been no order cancellation. West Bengal (~10
mn meters), Haryana (~5-6 mn), and Tamil Nadu (~5 mn) are key upcoming opportunities; Telangana is still in process.
Gas and Water Meter Opportunity
Gas metering is opening up with the government mandating CGDs to convert domestic connections to PNG with smart gas meters.
This year tenders of ~4.5-5 mn meters (primarily non-smart) are expected, with smart gas meter specifications likely finalised by
end-FY27 and large-scale tenders from FY28. Industry opportunity is ~INR 350-360 bn over 5-6 years; Genus targets ~20-25%
share. Gas revenue is expected to be ~8-10x last year's ~INR 120-130 mn, with ~INR 350 mn already won in Q1FY27. Water
metering is nascent but could become larger than electricity over 3-4 years, with global financing interest emerging.
Order Book and Revenue Visibility
The order book as of 30 June stood at ~INR 240 bn, primarily from own AMISP projects. With the 30% incremental provision, the
effective book could rise to ~40-42.5 mn meters. Management expects this to be a revenue-generating, not decorative, order
book. O&M revenue baseline of ~INR 8-9 bn annually is expected once the installed base stabilises, growing with new service
connections.
Margins and Raw Material Outlook
EBITDA margin guidance of ~18% (reduced from ~20%) is maintained despite currency depreciation, higher crude-linked
transportation costs, and geopolitical volatility. Key raw materials include chips, relays, batteries, PCBs, and in-house moulding
(new facility near Kotputli, Rajasthan). Deep supplier relationships and end-to-end manufacturing give confidence on margin
sustainability. Capex is modest; depreciation is ~INR 500-550 mn, with only ~INR 500-700 mn of annual capex expected going
forward.
Working Capital and Cash Flow
Negative operating cash flow (~INR 5 bn in FY26) is due to three self-liquidating components: inventory (~INR 13.5 bn, peaked as
meters were built ahead of revenue conversion), receivables (~INR 14.85-15 bn, due to installation outpacing billing), and contract
assets (~INR 8.7 bn, awaiting SAT certification). All projects are now revenue generating, SAT tests are catching up (Q1FY27 SAT
exceeded installations), and the company expects to be operationally cash flow positive by end-FY27 or Q1FY28. Receivables are
expected to decline significantly over the next 6-7 months. Genus is rated AA- (Stable) by CRISIL, and AMISP projects are rated AA-
by ICRA, enabling low-cost debt.
Competitive Intensity and Pricing Discipline
A recent Kerala tender saw L1 pricing ~50% below Genus's quote, with newer players aggressively bidding. Management views
this as unsustainable given 10-year warranty and 12-13 year product life requirements, plus long-term O&M obligations. DISCOMs
have previously suffered service quality issues from L1-driven low pricing and have since become more cautious. Genus is
comfortable waiting for right-priced opportunities, with gas and water providing large future growth avenues. Domestic sourcing
is already high (Category 1 supplier), with willingness to increase local procurement including displays.

rooftop and, most recently, utility-scale BESS. Q1FY27 revenue grew ~71% YoY to ~INR 5.05 bn on 109 MW of decentralised capacity
(~24,000 systems) installed in the quarter. The order book stood at ~INR 5.5 bn as of 30 June 2026; post-Q1, the company has
secured a further ~INR 4.5 bn of rooftop orders, taking the cumulative order book to over ~INR 10 bn, against which management
sees ~INR 15 bn of FY27 revenue visibility. Management reiterated its double-digit PAT margin guidance (not EBITDA or gross
margin), with pump and rooftop carrying broadly similar margins (within ~1%). Growth drivers include the T6/T7 pump tenders
(~100,000 pumps each, ~INR 45 bn combined value, of which GK expects a ~14-15% share) and PM Kusum 2.0, expected to be
floated in Q3FY27. The company remains asset-light (contract manufacturing, no backward integration) and recently entered BESS
with a 150 MW/300 MWh utility-scale order win. Key monitorables are PM Kusum 2.0 tender timing and pricing, order-book
conversion into revenue in H2FY27, geographic diversification beyond Maharashtra, receivables/cash-conversion trends, and the
BESS manufacturing decision.
Business Model & Positioning
• GK Energy was incorporated in 2008, initially as a product-trading and consultancy business, including work on product-testing
guidelines that later became BIS standards.
• The company began solar pump implementation in 2014-15, followed by solar rooftop and other energy products, with major
pump volumes starting in 2018-19 as government adoption picked up.
• Under Maharashtra's Atal Scheme, GK installed over 1,200 of the ~8,000 pumps deployed, and was subsequently a vendor under
the state's Mukhyamantri Saur Krishi Pump Yojana.
• Following the Central Government's PM Kusum scheme from 2019, GK became the largest implementer in Maharashtra and is
now the second-largest implementer nationally under PM Kusum.
• The company's USP is decentralised, megawatt-scale-equivalent implementation delivered through thousands of individual
systems; Q1FY27 saw 109 MW installed across ~24,000 systems.
• GK recently entered battery energy storage systems (BESS) as a natural extension of its decentralised renewable energy model,
securing a 150 MW/300 MWh utility-scale order.
Order Book & Revenue Guidance
• Q1FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) revenue grew ~71% YoY to ~INR 5.05 bn, with the order book at ~INR 5.41-5.5 bn as of 30
June.
• Since then, the company has secured ~INR 4.5 bn of further rooftop orders, taking the combined outstanding order book to over
~INR 10 bn.
• Management sees ~INR 15 bn of FY27 revenue visibility based on the current order book, noting that H1 has historically
contributed only ~30-40% of full-year revenue, with the balance weighted to H2.
• When pressed on an earlier stated ambition to double turnover to ~INR 30 bn in FY27, management did not explicitly reconfirm
the figure, instead pointing to this H1/H2 seasonality and citing continuous order inflow.
• As of the same period last year (September 2025), the order book stood at ~INR 6-6.5 bn, indicating a year-on-year
improvement in booked orders.
Solar Pump Business – Realisations & Tenders
• Average pump realisation is currently ~INR 0.2 mn, having declined with scale as procurement and manufacturing costs have
come down; management said margins have been maintained despite the lower realisation.
• Underlying demand remains strong from both government and farmer/beneficiary perspectives, given the scheme's subsidy-
linked economics.
• The T6 and T7 tenders (~100,000 pumps each, ~INR 45 bn combined value) are in the pipeline: T6 has already been bid, with an
order expected shortly, while T7's tender has been floated and bidding is in process.

• Based on past trends, management expects to win ~14-15% of the T6/T7 volumes, implying ~30,000 pumps.
• Scheme implementation timelines have been reduced from 120 days to 60 days from NTP issuance, with LOA typically following

Solar Rooftop & Segment Mix
• Rooftop currently contributes an estimated 25-30% of revenue, with the balance from pumps; management expects rooftop's
revenue share to keep rising, moving toward a roughly 40:60 to 50:50 mix with pumps by FY30/31.
• Rooftop and pump businesses carry broadly similar (blended) margins, within ~1% of each other, and are viewed as a natural

• A recently announced Smart Rooftop order for 100,000 systems, valued at ~INR 4.5 bn, is currently under implementation.
PM Kusum 2.0 & Tender Pipeline
• PM Kusum 2.0 is expected to be floated in Q3FY27 (management has consistently guided to Q3 since its March con-call); pricing
under the new scheme will depend on the specifications ultimately notified.
• Management expects competitive intensity under PM Kusum 2.0 to be broadly similar to the recent Maharashtra (Magel Tyala)
tenders, with largely the same set of players.
• Every state has submitted its implementation intent for PM Kusum 2.0, with empanelment to follow once volumes are finalised;
management expects industry-level tender volumes of up to ~700,000 pumps to be announced under the scheme.
Geographic Diversification
• Maharashtra has historically accounted for ~60-65% of GK's pan-India implementation; management expects this concentration
to reduce as PM Kusum 2.0 rolls out implementation in other states.
• Madhya Pradesh has already delivered 2,000+ pump orders for the company; Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh are also flagged as
key focus markets given large addressable demand from marginal landholders (MP alone targets ~3 mn pump installations).
• Haryana is viewed as a smaller opportunity given its size and existing coverage; Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan and UP are
expected to remain the four largest markets going forward.
BESS – New Growth Vertical
• The 150 MW/300 MWh BESS order (utility scale) was announced only once secured, consistent with management's stated
preference to announce results rather than intentions.
• Management has not disclosed a decision on setting up in-house BESS manufacturing versus remaining EPC-focused; internal
discussions are ongoing, with any confirmed outcome to be disclosed via exchange filings.
Margins & Business Model
• Guidance is consistently framed around a double-digit PAT margin rather than EBITDA or gross margin.
• The company is asset-light: it owns its manufacturing network but relies on contract manufacturing rather than in-house
production, and has not announced any backward integration plans.
• The business model is B2C in nature: the farmer selects the vendor and contributes their share upfront to the state
implementing agency, while GK receives 100% of its payment from the agency rather than from the farmer directly.
Working Capital & Receivables
• Receivable days are targeted at ~140-150 days on an annualised basis (as of March), broadly in line with the company's cash
conversion cycle of ~3-4 months, which management described as consistent with industry practice.
• Management indicated ongoing efforts to improve working capital but no material near-term change to the cash conversion
cycle.
Balance Sheet & Funding
• There are no immediate plans for equity dilution post-IPO; near-term funding requirements, if any, are expected to be met
through debt.
• Management would consider raising additional equity only if longer-term funding needs warrant it.
Other Items
• The company is also executing a small, continuous flow of private-sector orders (particularly in rooftop) that are typically not
individually announced given their scale.
• Revenue and receivables remain concentrated among a limited number of government nodal/implementing agencies, though
management notes this reflects the scheme-driven, subsidy-linked nature of the business rather than customer-specific risk.

Globus Spirits Ltd
Strong Consumer-Led Growth & Improving Earnings Mix
• Globus Spirits is targeting a structural shift in its business mix, with consumer revenue expected to increase from ~40%
currently to 50% by FY29, supported by growth in IMFL and country liquor. The consumer segment is already contributing a
disproportionately higher share of EBITDA, while the company expects the increasing contribution from higher-margin
consumer products to improve the overall earnings profile and operating leverage.
UP Emerging as a Key Growth Driver
• The newly established UP business is scaling rapidly, with country liquor volumes increasing to ~210,000-215,000 cases per

increasingly important contributor to consumer growth, with its share of IMFL revenue already reaching ~15%.
IMFL Expansion with Significant Margin Upside
• The IMFL business is progressing towards breakeven in FY27-FY28, after which management expects meaningful margin

Integrated Manufacturing Supports Bulk Business Economics
• Globus operates around 334 mn litres of installed distillation capacity across six plants, with flexible facilities capable of
producing both ethanol and ENA using multiple feedstocks including rice, maize and molasses. Bulk EBITDA is expected to
remain within INR 5-6.5 per litre on an annualised basis, although quarterly margins remain seasonal due to raw material
availability and ethanol allocation. Management expects consumer growth to gradually increase captive consumption of
ENA/alcohol and reduce dependence on bulk sales, improving the overall profitability mix.

• The company has already utilised the INR 2 bn raised through the QIP, including repayment of INR 1.55 bn of long-term debt,
which is expected to generate interest savings of around INR 60 mn for the balance of the year and ~INR 120 mn annually. The
remaining INR 450 mn is earmarked for the consumer business, including brand development and expansion into new states.
Management expects debt reduction, higher consumer contribution and improving IMFL profitability to provide further
support to cash generation and returns.

Glottis Ltd
Outlook: Glottis is targeting around 30% revenue growth in FY27 and expects to maintain a similar growth trajectory over the next
2-3 years, supported by expansion across India, Malaysia, project cargo and new verticals such as chemicals, pharma and
automobiles. Renewable-related logistics should remain a key growth driver over the next 2-3 years, while the planned 1,000-
container addition and fleet expansion should improve customer retention and margins. Management expects margins to recover
to FY25 levels during FY27, with container deployment potentially adding 2-3 percentage points to margins. Near-term challenges
remain elevated freight volatility, container availability and geopolitical disruptions, particularly through Q3FY27.
Business & Customer Base
• Glottis is a multimodal transport operator, with core operations across ocean freight, air freight and local transportation.
• The company has diversified into minerals, timber, agro, home appliances and engineering products, and is expanding into
automobiles and defence.
• Customer base increased from 1,500 to 2,071 in FY26, adding 163+ customers during the year.
• Around 70-75% of customers are long-term/sticky, while spot customers provide opportunities for better margins.
Revenue Growth
• Management indicated that FY27 revenue is expected to be around INR 9.5 bn, implying roughly 30% growth.
• Management is targeting around 30% CAGR over the next 2-3 years.
• Growth is expected to come from new geographies, Malaysia, project cargo, expansion of sales offices and new verticals.
• North and West India have become important growth regions, with increasing contribution from chemical and pharma
customers.
Renewable Diversification
• Renewable energy remains an important vertical, but management is actively diversifying towards chemicals, pharma and
automobiles.
• Renewable-related cargo is expected to remain strong for the next 2-3 years, driven by solar manufacturing, battery storage
and cell-line capex.
• The company handles imports of solar cells, aluminium frames, glass and other raw materials from Southeast Asia.
• Management expects additional opportunities from upcoming cell and wafer manufacturing capacity in India.

container supply.
• Management expects the asset addition to support both revenue growth and margin improvement.
Malaysia Expansion

Godavari Biorefineries Ltd
Outlook: The company is positioning biochemicals as a key medium-term growth driver, supported by rising demand for bio-based
alternatives, established customer relationships and improving price competitiveness against fossil-based products. The targeted
quarterly biochemical revenue run-rate of INR 2.4 bn from Q3FY28 provides a potential earnings catalyst, while additional ethanol
fungibility could improve feedstock flexibility and product-mix optimisation. However, near-term consolidated profitability will
remain exposed to sugar seasonality, feedstock costs, government ethanol allocation policies and commodity realisations. The
pace of biochemical capacity utilisation, execution of the proposed expansion and the commercialisation timeline of the
pharmaceutical pipeline will be key monitorables.
Biochemicals – Growth and Realisations
• Biochemicals remain a key growth driver, with revenue targeted at INR 2.4 bn per quarter from Q3FY28, implying an
annualised run-rate of ~INR 9.6 bn.
• The company is witnessing stronger demand for specialty biochemicals as the price parity between bio-based and fossil-based
chemicals narrows, supporting higher capacity utilisation.
• Speciality chemicals continue to command a premium over conventional alternatives, with the company maintaining existing
premiums despite volatility in crude-linked petrochemical prices.
• Investments in downstream biochemicals are translating into revenue growth, supported by customer relationships and
expanding production capabilities.
• The company has over 100,000 TPA of bio-based chemical capacity, with utilisation varying across products depending on
demand and prevailing market economics.
Ethanol – Capacity Expansion and Flexibility
• The company commissioned a 200 KLPD grain-based distillery in Q1FY27 to diversify feedstock sourcing and reduce
dependence on sugarcane-based feedstock.
• Management is evaluating an additional 160 KLPD of fungible capacity, which would allow greater flexibility between grain-
and sugar-based ethanol production depending on feedstock availability and relative economics.
• Ethanol production allocation is driven by relative realisations, with ~80% of output supplied to OMCs and the balance catering
to pharma, ENA, industrial alcohol and captive biochemical requirements.
• Ethanol margins from grain-based operations are estimated at ~10%, although profitability remains sensitive to grain
procurement costs and fluctuations in feedstock prices.
• The company currently diverts ~30-32% of its sugar towards ethanol production, with the actual allocation dependent on
government policies, OMC tenders and the relative profitability of sugar and ethanol.
Integrated Business Model – Sugar, Ethanol and Chemicals
• The integrated sugar, ethanol and biochemical model provides flexibility to optimise product allocation based on prevailing
sugar prices, ethanol realisations and feedstock availability.
• The ability to switch between sugar, ethanol and downstream chemicals provides a strategic advantage in managing
commodity price volatility and improving profitability.
• The company is evaluating further fungibility investments to strengthen its ability to optimise production across different
feedstocks and end markets.
• Sugar profitability remains seasonal, with earnings typically concentrated in Q4 as crushing activity progresses in Karnataka,
while Q1 and Q2 generally experience weaker performance.
Sugar Business – Seasonality and Inventory
• Sugar operations remain subject to government-imposed monthly sales quotas, which restrict the pace of inventory
liquidation and extend the working capital cycle.
• The finished-goods inventory for chemicals is generally maintained at 7-10 days, while sugar inventory levels are largely
determined by production volumes and government sales allocations.
• ~20% of sugar sales are routed through the branded consumer business, with the Jivana brand generating INR 1.29 bn of
revenue in FY25.
• Sugar profitability in the upcoming season will depend on rainfall, sugarcane availability, recovery rates, cane prices and
government policies governing ethanol diversion.
Exports and Global Demand
• Export demand across Europe, North America and East Asia remains broadly stable, with management reporting no material
change in demand from key international customers.
• The company provides product-level carbon footprint data to customers, supporting its positioning in markets where
sustainability credentials are increasingly important.
• Management believes its bio-based products offer greater price stability than fossil-based alternatives amid geopolitical
disruptions and volatility in crude-linked chemical prices.

Godawari Power & Ispat Ltd
Business
• The company is based in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, and is integrated across iron ore mining, pelletisation, sponge iron, steel billets
and value-added downstream products.
• Captive power comes from waste heat, coal, biomass and solar. Power is 100% consumed internally, with no commercial sales.
Captive generation costs INR 3.5 per unit against ~INR 6 for grid power.
Mining: The Key Bottleneck
• Environmental approval was received in February to expand iron ore mining capacity from 2.35 MTPA to 6 MTPA.
• Mining is constrained by delays in tree-cutting approval and dumping space for ore overburden. Management expects the
approval in the next 1-3 months, after which the beneficiation plant will also come up.
• The target is full-capacity mining by the exit of this financial year. After that, iron ore for pelletisation will be fully met in-
house, and management expects the full-year impact in FY28.
• FY27 will see more than 50% of iron ore bought from the market. Earlier it was ~20-25%, and last year ~70% was captive.
Management will not guide on the exact percentage.
• A mining contractor is already lined up for equipment and infrastructure.
Pellets
• The new pellet plant is natural-gas based. Earlier plants use coal gas.
• It was shut for ~30-45 days (shutdown from the first week of July) because the economics turned unviable. It restarted as
pellet prices rose.
• Based on management's indicated production of 150,000 tonnes per month and a selling price of ~INR 8,500 per tonne at the
time, the 45-day shutdown implies a loss of ~225,000 tonnes, or ~INR 1.9 bn of revenue. The impact falls in Q2, and
depreciation continues; management says the interest cost impact is minimal.
• Natural gas was chosen because a pipeline was available and for the environmental angle. Management said it was not for
better product quality.
• Gas availability is not an issue, though it comes at a slightly higher cost. Unit economics remain comfortable.
• Because of Middle East-related supply issues, a second coal gasifier will be added at the new plant. It will take about 6-9
months.
Guidance and Margins
• Q3 and Q4 margins will be slightly lower than the earlier year, mainly because of the new pellet plant and heavier market
purchase of iron ore.
• Margins can expand beyond FY26 levels once the dumping ground approval and beneficiation plant are in place.
• Whether FY27 EBITDA margin falls below 20% depends on volume and mix. Selling prices of value-added downstream
products have improved considerably over the last 1-1.5 months.
• FY27 revenue will not be lower than last year and should be better, helped by the new pellet plant.
• The guidance in the investor presentation will be revised before the next investor call, to reflect the shutdown and margin
impact.
Battery Energy Storage (BESS)
• The 20 GWh project (single line, ~INR 14 bn) is located in the AURIC industrial area, Maharashtra.
• Equipment is tied up, with shipment in November-December and arrival at site around February. Civil work is just starting,
with foundations planned to be ready before equipment arrives, and the building is prefab.
• Commissioning is targeted by March-end, with production in Q1FY28. Management would not commit to one or two months
either way.
• Raw material is tied up under 5-year agreements. Sales will be 100% to third parties.
• Marketing has started and a team is in place. The company will bid for BESS supply and EPC tenders (government bodies and
C&I customers) and is still debating the developer model. No orders yet, but management expects to secure some over the
next 1-2 quarters. Delivery is assumed from July 2027.
• Pricing: ~INR 8.5 mn per MWh including BMS and PCS. Management also quoted a price of ~USD 52,000 per MWh, noting that
prices have risen rather than fallen.
• At full capacity, potential turnover is close to INR 180 bn, reached over 3-4 years, at 6-8% EBITDA margin (INR 12-14 bn
EBITDA).
• For FY28, with 9-10 months of operation, initial estimates are ~7-8 GWh of output, roughly 35-40% of capacity.
Cold Rolling Mill (CRM) Complex
• The capacity is 0.7 MTPA. The location was moved from Chhattisgarh to Maharashtra (Auric belt) because of approval delays.
• Land has been allotted. The lease deed and initial approvals are pending, and the project needs at least a year from start of
construction to commissioning.

Outlook: Goel Construction is transitioning from a civil-focused industrial contractor to a general contractor model by integrating
mechanical works into its service offerings. The company maintains a debt-free status with a consistent 10-11% EBITDA margin
and targets sustainable revenue growth of approximately 30% over the next few years.
Business Performance & Financials
• Revenue & Margins: The company reported revenue of ~INR 6.5 bn last year, with a stable EBITDA margin of 10-11%.
• Order Book: ~INR 13 bn as of March.
• Financial Health: The company is debt-free and operates with minimal working capital requirements due to its focus on private

• Growth Strategy: Targeting ~30% sustainable growth for the next 2-3 years.
Operational Capabilities
• Core Expertise: Specialised in high-complexity industrial civil construction, including cement plants, thermal power plants, and

Project Execution & Terms
• Timelines: Cement plants typically take 10-12 months for 80-90% billing, while thermal power plants take approximately 24
months.

Risks & Other Matters
• Market Pressures: Monitoring fuel cost increases resulting from the West Asia crisis, though the current impact is not yet
significant.

associated with that sector.
• Shareholder Returns: There are no immediate plans for buybacks or dividends as funds are prioritised for scaling, though a
policy may be developed if funds cannot be meaningfully deployed.

will add 25% to total processing capacity. At full ramp-up, the new capacity can generate about INR 60 bn of additional
revenue, with a payback period of 3.5 years. The roll-out is phased through September 2027, and the first lines at Gandhidham
and Haldia are targeted internally for March 2027.
• Modernisation: The programme also upgrades older units: Gandhidham (built in 2003) and Haldia (built in 2009 and acquired
through NCLT). The aim is to reduce processing losses and improve yields.
• Biodiesel: The 300 TPD biodiesel plant has been fully operational since April. Its entire output is exported to the EU under EOU
status, benefiting from the EU's 7% blending mandate. The segment holds ISCC EU sustainability certification and earns EBITDA
margins of 3-6%.
• Edible Oils: About 80% (±5%) of raw material is imported, mainly crude palm, soya and sunflower oil from Indonesia, Malaysia,
Brazil and Argentina.
• Castor & Mustard: Castor oil and derivatives generate a stable INR 10 bn (±10%) of annual revenue. India supplies 80% of the
world's castor, and 80% of India's crop is grown in Gujarat. Seasonal domestic mustard crushing adds INR 2-3 bn a year.
• B2C Branded Push: Branded products currently make up 6% of revenue. Management aims to raise this share to 20-25%
within 3-5 years, which would support a better mix and higher margins.
• Solar Cost Savings: A 16.5 MW solar project now meets about 70% of the Gandhidham plant's power needs. Solar installations
are being extended to Mangalore and Krishnapatnam. The target is for 55-60% of total electricity consumption to come from
solar by March 2027, and the solar projects have a payback of 3.0 years.
• Risk Management: The company fully hedges both commodity price risk and forex risk. It works on a 90-day back-to-back
contract framework and takes no unhedged speculative positions. Recent cuts in edible oil import duty are passed straight
through to customers without any inventory loss, because customs duty is applied when the sale or contract is executed.
• Return Profile: ROCE has stayed above 30% for the past two years. This reflects low acquisition and gross block costs and
shared utilities across plant locations.
• Promoter Pledge: Promoter shares are pledged only to the working capital consortium lenders to secure operating credit
lines, not to raise external debt.
• Backward & Forward Integration: The company is expanding into palm plantations in Andhra Pradesh, near the
Krishnapatnam plant. It is also moving into higher-margin oleochemicals.
• Long-Term Potential: The 25% capacity addition, worth about INR 60 bn of revenue potential, and growing exports give the
company a clear path for scale. Higher-margin biodiesel, the shift toward B2C products and solar cost savings support margin
improvement. A fully hedged model and ROCE above 30% underpin the quality of returns.

GPT Healthcare Ltd
Outlook: GPT Healthcare is targeting a strong financial trajectory with an expected revenue CAGR of 15-17% over the next 4-5
years. The company's overall EBITDA margins are projected to stabilise around 21%, supported by its mature hospital assets which
consistently generate ~25% EBITDA margins. Under its current operational footprint, the existing hospital network holds a peak
annual revenue capacity of ~INR 8.0 bn. The business remains uniquely positioned to capture long-term structural demand across
Eastern India, an underserved healthcare market that currently has only 14 beds per 10,000 population compared to the national
average of 40-45 beds.
Growth Strategy
Operating under its flagship "ILS Hospitals" brand, the group is aggressively scaling its network to reach 1,000 beds over the next
couple of years. To achieve this capacity expansion, management is following a disciplined growth rate of adding 10-12% bed
capacity annually, which translates to roughly 150 beds added every 18 months. This measured pace allows the company to
pursue long-term geographic expansion without overstretching its management bandwidth or operational cash flows.
Financial Performance & Balance Sheet
The company maintains a highly conservative balance sheet characterised by a debt-to-equity ratio below 0.1x, with management
committing to a strict internal leverage ceiling of 0.5x for any future debt. Operating cash flow conversion remains exceptionally
strong at above 80%, backed by cash reserves of ~INR 500 mn. All upcoming capacity expansion will be funded through internal
accruals and debt, ensuring no equity dilution for shareholders. Additionally, the company maintains a consistent dividend policy,
paying out ~30% of PAT annually.
Pricing & ARPOB Strategy
GPT Healthcare intentionally maintains its network ARPOB at ~INR 40,000-42,000, which is roughly 30% below major corporate
chains like Apollo Hospitals, in order to keep quality healthcare affordable for its core middle-to-upper-income demographic.
Management expects ARPOB to expand at an annual rate of 6-7%, driven by routine price inflation and an evolving, higher-
complexity case mix. The payer profile remains low-risk, with cash and private insurance accounting for 90-95% of total revenue,
while government schemes and corporate tie-ups contribute only 5-7%.
Working Capital & Governance
Actual trade payable days are 41-44 days; management clarified that external screeners overstate this metric due to formula
errors that mistakenly include independent doctor consultant payouts in the denominator. On the governance front, the company
operates with an independent board structure audited by BSR & Co.
Network Expansion & Capex Structure
The company currently operates ~750 beds across five hospitals located in Salt Lake, Dum Dum, Howrah, Raipur and Agartala. A
sixth hospital in Jamshedpur is scheduled to open in March/April 2027. Management is actively evaluating new greenfield sites
and acquisition opportunities in Cuttack, Siliguri, Guwahati, Varanasi and a replacement site in Ranchi. In terms of capital intensity,
fully owned greenfield assets require ~INR 10 mn per bed in capex, whereas leased locations like Raipur and Jamshedpur operate
on an asset-light model requiring significantly lower capital outlay.
Operational Performance & Utilisation
Overall network occupancy currently stands at ~50% against a realistic operational ceiling of ~75%, following a successful
reduction in average length of stay (ALOS) to under three days. Looking ahead, mature units in Dum Dum and Salt Lake are
expected to reach ~70% occupancy in upcoming quarters, Agartala is targeted at ~60%, and Howrah at ~55%. The newer Raipur
facility is operating at 20-22% occupancy and is targeted to reach 30% monthly utilisation by March 2027 to achieve breakeven,
aided by major corporate tie-ups with Coal India and SAIL. The upcoming Jamshedpur unit is targeted to achieve 70% occupancy
within five years of launching, delivering 22-23% EBITDA margins.
Specialty Mix & Clinical Capabilities
Revenue generation is well-diversified, with the top 10 specialties accounting for ~80% of revenue, ensuring no dependence on
individual "star doctors". The group is actively upscaling its clinical capabilities by introducing orthopaedic robotics at Howrah,
expanding CTVS/bypass and gastrointestinal procedures at Salt Lake, and setting up radiation oncology in Agartala. Demonstrating
its high-end tertiary capability, the year-old Raipur hospital successfully executed both liver and kidney transplants within its first
year of operation.
Talent Procurement & Medical Tourism
Doctor attrition remains very low at under 10%, supported by ethical practices and advanced clinical infrastructure, while nursing
and paramedical talent is directly supplied by GPT's captive nursing college in Agartala. In accordance with regulatory guidelines,
independent doctor consultants are not eligible for ESOPs. Medical value tourism contributes less than 5% of total revenue; while
the Agartala facility derives ~10% of its patient volume from Bangladesh due to border proximity (which has stabilised after visa
disruptions), the primary Kolkata units focus almost exclusively on a local neighbourhood catchment radius of 3-4 km.

Business Model & Positioning
• Greaves Cotton has a 167-year history, with engine manufacturing dating back to 1939; it is popularly known as a three-wheeler
diesel engine maker, though diesel three-wheeler engines account for only ~16% of consolidated FY26 turnover (~24% of the
core business).
• Management frames the business in two parts: a "core business" (engineering: energy, mobility and industrial solutions)
requiring routine working capital and capex, and an "investing business" (Greaves Electric Mobility/Ampere and Greaves
Finance) funded by cash from the core.
• Consolidated FY26 turnover was over INR 25 bn, with EBITDA of ~INR 3.8 bn; international business has grown from 9% to 13%
of core business and is targeted to reach ~18-20% by FY30.
• The engine mix shift is notable: engines contributed 80% of business in FY26, falling to 51% in H1 (across applications including
three-wheelers, gensets, firefighting and construction equipment), as other businesses have grown faster.
• Net worth stood at INR 16.2 bn in March 2026; of this, ~INR 7.2 bn is deployed in the core business (INR 3.4 bn in fixed
assets/working capital, INR 3.8 bn in the Excel Controlinkage and Greaves Technologies acquisitions), generating INR 3.83 bn
EBITDA and INR 3.7 bn PBT, implying core ROCE of over 50%.
• The remaining ~INR 9 bn comprises ~INR 4.5 bn invested in Greaves Electric Mobility and Greaves Finance, and ~INR 4.5 bn of
cash (as of March 2026) since deployed across these entities and the Excel acquisition.
• The company is debt-free (as of March 2026) with an AA- credit rating, giving headroom for further borrowing (INR 5-7 bn) if
required for capital deployment.
Core Business: Growth Guidance & Capital Allocation
• Management has guided to 16-20% core-business revenue growth for FY27-FY30 with EBITDA margins maintained at 13-15%
and capex of only INR 5-7 bn, since land/building capex is largely already in place.
• Using a rule-of-72-style illustration, management estimates core EBITDA could roughly double from ~INR 4 bn (FY27E) to ~INR 8
bn by FY30, implying a cumulative four-year EBITDA pool of ~INR 25 bn.
• After capex, working capital and tax, management estimates ~50% of EBITDA is convertible to cash (~INR 12.5 bn over four
years), which together with the existing INR 4.5 bn cash and debt headroom gives a deployable pool of ~INR 20-25 bn for
inorganic growth, subject to board and shareholder decisions.
• Guidance figures are for organic growth; inorganic growth would be incremental.

GSP Crop Sciences Ltd
GSP Crop Sciences operates an integrated agrochemical model across technical manufacturing, formulations and R&D, with revenue
split of ~25% from technicals and ~75% from formulations, and a channel mix of ~40% domestic B2B, ~40% domestic B2C and ~20%

to pass through the channel. Management expects H2 exports to be stronger given Brazil's opposite agricultural season. The key
factors to monitor are rainfall and demand recovery, cost pass-through in B2C, the share of patented products, progress in Brazil
and the H2 export recovery.
Business Model & Revenue Mix
• The company operates across technical manufacturing, formulations and R&D.
• Revenue is split ~25% from technicals and ~75% from formulations.
• The sales mix stands at approximately 40% domestic B2B, 40% domestic B2C and 20% exports.

Patented Portfolio
• Patented products contribute around 20% of the top line.
• The company focuses on developing differentiated combinations using molecules that have recently gone off-patent.
• It holds 100+ patents, of which 18-20 have been commercialised, with another 100+ patents in the pipeline.
• The strategy focuses on building higher-value products rather than competing solely on generic molecules.
Domestic Distribution
• The domestic B2C business remains a key growth channel.
• The network spans 20 states, 24 CNF locations and 6,000+ dealers.

Exports & Brazil Opportunity

• Management expects H2 to be stronger, given Brazil's opposite agricultural season.
Demand Environment & Margins
• Domestic agrochemical demand has remained broadly flattish, with erratic rainfall impacting crop-level demand across regions.
• Raw material inflation and rupee depreciation have pressured B2C margins.
• B2C price increases can take 3-6 months to pass through the distribution channel.
• B2B pricing is more responsive, allowing quicker pass-through of cost increases.
• Rainfall-led demand recovery and normalisation of input costs will remain key monitorables.

GV Electricals Ltd
Outlook: FY27 revenue is guided at INR 1,800-2,000 mn, up 15-27% from INR 1,570 mn in FY26. Over the next 2-3 years (FY28-
FY29), management expects EBITDA margin to expand from 10.9% to 15-16% and PAT margin to rise to 9-10%, driven by higher-
margin data centre and specialised infrastructure work.
Company Background: Founded in 1985 by Mr Anil Raj, GV Electricals is a 40-year-old power distribution and electrical services
company. The current management took over in 2012: Chairman Javed Akhtar, Managing Director Sunil Vatsa and CEO Furqan
Akhtar. Since then, turnover has grown about 26x, from INR 60 mn to INR 1,570 mn in FY26.
Business Verticals: The company operates in four areas:
• Network O&M: The core recurring business, covering grid stability, complaint handling and reduction of transmission and
distribution (T&D) losses.
• Electrical infrastructure (EPC): Specialised work including new connections, power lines, underground cabling, pillar boxes and
substations up to 400 kV.
• Meter Management Group (MMG): Installation, billing and maintenance of smart meters.
• Data centres (emerging): Electrical infrastructure and O&M services for hyperscale data centres.
O&M Revenue Base: O&M revenue grew from INR 840 mn in FY24 to INR 1,040 mn in FY25 and INR 1,200 mn in FY26, about 76%
of total revenue. Monthly recurring billing makes this revenue highly predictable, and it held up even during COVID-19.
Smart Metering: MMG revenue was INR 11.6 mn in FY25 and INR 12.0 mn in FY26. Public resistance to smart meters has slowed
the rollout, but the company is expanding into new discom circles in Odisha and Ajmer.
Order Book & Pipeline: The order book stood at INR 5,530 mn as of June, about 3.5x FY26 revenue, executable over three years.
About 70% is O&M and 30% is electrical infrastructure and metering. A further INR 3,000+ Mn of orders is close to finalisation, and
the company is bidding for active tenders worth more than INR 10,000 mn.
Client Franchise: Repeat business accounts for 88.29% of revenue. The anchor clients are major private discoms Tata Power (a
partner since 1996) and Adani Electricity. Other clients include CESC, Hiranandani Yotta, ABB, Siemens and BPCL.
Data Centre Opportunity: The company has partnered with Schneider Electric to bid for major data centre projects. It has bid for
the Reliance Jamnagar project, which has an estimated annual O&M value of INR 89 mn and EPC/installation scope of INR 300-400
mn per floor. It is also in talks with TCS about a 1.2 GW power infrastructure project in Pune/Jharkhand.
Geographic Expansion: The company is entering South India through the Hubli and Belgaum clusters in Karnataka. It is also taking
part in upcoming discom tenders across several zones in Uttar Pradesh.
Competitive Moats: Its strengths include a pan-India presence, in-house software for call centres and meter billing, and end-to-
end complaint resolution. Strict tender qualification criteria on manpower and fleet size also keep smaller local contractors out.
Debt Reduction: Debt was INR 140 mn before the IPO. The company is using IPO proceeds to cut it to INR 30-40 mn.
Working Capital Efficiency: About 90% of monthly O&M bills from major private discoms are collected by the 7th or 8th of the
following month. Because of this, the O&M business needs only one month of working capital, and the current balance sheet can
support up to INR 10,000 mn of O&M order execution. Trade receivables rise temporarily at year-end because discoms bill
February and March together.
Workforce: The company has about 4,000 employees. Revenue per employee is about INR 0.4 mn and should rise as EPC and data
centre revenue grows.
Long-Term Potential: A recurring O&M base with strong collections, an order book of 3.5x revenue and a pipeline of more than
INR 10,000 mn give the company good revenue visibility. Entry into data centres with Schneider Electric, together with a shift
toward higher-margin EPC work, supports the expected margin expansion to 15-16% EBITDA.

Hariom Pipe Industries Ltd
Hariom Pipe Industries is entering its next phase from a position of greater scale, stronger integration and improved financial
discipline, though FY27 will be partly constrained by the ~110-day Perundurai shutdown that cannot be recovered. Volumes are
expected to be broadly flat year-on-year, while revenue should rise on better realisations and absolute EBITDA is guided ~10%

The Gadchiroli greenfield project in Maharashtra (INR 30 bn MOU, ~300+ acres, 136 acres under preliminary agreement) remains a

Perundurai Disruption and Q1FY27 Impact
The Perundurai unit was shut for ~110 days due to a pollution control closure notice effective 31 March 2026, with power
disconnected from 4 April 2026. Operations resumed only from 14 July 2026. This led to Q1FY27 volumes of 63,084 MT versus
81,742 MT in Q4FY26, and Q1FY27 revenue of INR 4,291.8 mn versus INR 4,609.6 mn in Q1FY26.
FY27 Volume and Revenue Guidance
Full-year volumes are expected to be broadly similar to last year given the irrecoverable 110-day loss. Revenue is expected to be
higher than last year on stronger sales realisations, though the ~25% growth target is not achievable on flat volumes. Absolute
EBITDA is guided at ~10% higher than FY26 standalone EBITDA of INR 2,094.2 mn, driven entirely by product mix rather than
volume.
Blended EBITDA and Product Mix Economics
FY26 blended EBITDA per tonne was INR 7,258, comprising INR 8,251 per tonne from MS tubes (integrated induction furnace
route, 93,249 MT sold, EBITDA INR 769.4 mn) and INR 7,008 per tonne from galvanised and value-added products (183,794 MT
sold, revenue INR 11.59 bn, EBITDA INR 1,288 mn). FY27 blended EBITDA per tonne is expected at ~INR 7,500. Higher MS tube and
OEM product volumes lift margins, while HRPO, CRFH coil and pipe sales dilute them since raw material is externally procured.
Growth Drivers and Strategic Rationale
Growth will come from improving utilisation of existing capacity across three units, increasing high-value product contribution,
expanding the OEM and customer franchise, and driving operational efficiencies into cash flow. Management emphasised that as
Hariom produces more of its own primary steel, profitability and per-tonne EBITDA will rise. The company targets a ~INR 100 bn
top line in ~5-7 years from FY27, to be achieved through phased capex rather than a single large outlay.
Maharashtra (Gadchiroli) Greenfield Expansion
The project requires ~300+ acres, with MIDC issuing the notification for Hariom. Preliminary agreements cover 136 acres, but land
will be acquired by MIDC from villagers, farmers, tribals and the forest department before allocation to Hariom. This is a long-term
phased project, not completable in one to two years. The MOU with the Maharashtra government is for INR 30 bn. Hariom is also
evaluating a parallel brownfield or greenfield expansion in the interim, with disclosure to stock exchanges at the appropriate time.
Capex and Balance Sheet
FY27 capex is guided at INR 600-700 mn, including the Anantapur unit pipeline, with no volume addition expected in the current
year from these projects; full volumes would come ~18 months after project commencement. Total long-term and short-term
borrowings stand at INR 4.21 bn. The quarterly finance cost run-rate is ~INR 150-160 mn. The next credit rating review is due in
FY27, with the current rating already completed.
Solar Power Venture
Hariom is developing a 60 MW AC project under the PM-KUSUM scheme (Component C) with a 25-year fixed PPA at INR 2.96 per
unit and central government capital subsidy. Total investment so far is ~INR 1 bn, including a bank term loan from SBI, with a
payback of ~13-14 years against a 20-year loan tenure. Expected annual fixed revenue is INR 320-330 mn with EBITDA margin
above 94% and negligible operational risk. Revenue recognition begins from Q2FY27. This is positioned as an ESG, carbon credit
and green steel enabler rather than a diversification into power.
Green Steel and ESG Positioning
Management expects that if steel is certified as green steel, realisations could rise from ~INR 55,000 per tonne to INR 85,000 to
90,000 per tonne with identical chemical and physical composition. The differentiator would be lower carbon emissions per tonne
of finished steel and renewable energy usage. The solar project supports this framework along with energy efficiency, recycling,
water reuse, safety and governance.

HFCL Ltd
Outlook: HFCL is poised for a structural multi-year growth cycle driven by hyperscaler and data centre demand, with optical fibre
capacity expanding to 43 mn fibre kilometres and cable capacity to 62 mn fibre kilometres by July 2028, alongside 600 tonnes of
preform capacity by October 2028. Revenue growth guidance has been raised to a minimum of 60% for FY27, with ~50%+ growth
considered sustainable, supported by a ~INR 280 bn order book and improving margins (23.25% EBITDA in Q1FY27 versus 16.7% in
FY26). The defence segment offers a second growth pillar, targeting ~INR 40-50 bn by FY30, while data centre interconnect is set
to rise to 18-20% of the OFC segment next year. With firm global demand, sustained pricing, no tariff impact, and ~INR 25 bn
capex underway, HFCL appears well-positioned to capitalise on a long runway of opportunities through FY29 and beyond.
Capacity Expansion Roadmap
• HFCL is undertaking a major capacity buildout across the optical fibre value chain. Optical fibre capacity stands at 28 mn fibre
kilometres, expanding to 34 mn by December 2026 and 43 mn by July 2028. Optical fibre cable capacity is currently 39 mn
fibre kilometres, rising to 43 mn by December 2026 and 62 mn by July 2028. The company is also setting up 600 tonnes of
preform capacity at a capex of ~INR 12.5 bn, operational by October 2028. This will meet ~50% of captive preform
requirements, with the balance continuing to be outsourced from Japanese suppliers Sumitomo and Shin-Etsu.
Demand-Supply Dynamics
• Global annual optical fibre cable demand stands at ~750 mn fibre kilometres against supply of ~600-625 mn fibre kilometres.
The shortage is primarily driven by preform availability constraints. Demand is split across hyperscaler data centres at ~400-
450 mn fibre kilometres, telcos at ~200 mn fibre kilometres, and defence applications (drones) at ~100 mn fibre kilometres.
Demand is expected to reach ~900 mn fibre kilometres by FY29, with the shortage expected to persist. Unlike previous cycles
tied to the 2G, 3G and 4G rollouts, this cycle is structural and driven by hyperscalers and data centres, with a runway of at least
seven to eight years.
Pricing Trends
• Optical fibre prices have risen sharply. D2 fibre for telcos has moved from ~USD 4-5 per fibre kilometre to ~USD 13-14 per fibre
kilometre. A2 fibre for hyperscalers has moved from ~USD 7-8 per fibre kilometre to ~USD 25 per fibre kilometre. Pricing is
expected to sustain given the structural demand shift. Telcos have held back capex for the past one to one-and-a-half years
expecting price softening, but with prices sustaining, large telcos globally have begun inquiries. The next phase of demand is
expected from telcos densifying networks, 6G rollout by FY29, and defence applications.
Geographic Demand Shift
• Current demand is predominantly from US hyperscalers. This is expected to shift to Europe, Southeast Asia, the Middle East,
and Asia including India. India has announced significant data centre capex, with cable requirements expected to begin in one
to one-and-a-half years. Fibre, cable and data centre interconnect constitute ~5% of total data centre capex, split 50-50
between cable and data centre interconnect products.
Defence Segment Growth
• HFCL has developed land-based defence products including electronic fuses, thermal weapon sights, radars, and multimode
hand grenades under a DRDO technology tie-up. The company acquired an aerospace company manufacturing fuel tanks and
pylons for fighter jets, with a confirmed export order book of ~INR 16 bn at acquisition, now ~INR 20.5 bn. Defence revenue
was ~INR 770 mn last year, with aspirations of ~INR 5 bn this year, ~INR 15 bn next year, and ~INR 40-50 bn by FY30. A defence
tender financial bid is likely to open in February 2027. The board has approved ~INR 2.75 bn of capex for ammunition facilities.
Financial Performance and Guidance
• HFCL reported turnover of INR 49.49 bn in FY26, and Q1FY27 revenue was INR 19.15 bn. FY27 growth guidance was revised
from 20% to 40%, and now to a minimum of 60% over FY26. EBITDA margin was 16.7% in FY26, improving to 23.25% in
Q1FY27; this is seen as sustainable, with further quarterly improvement expected. The operating margin for the OFC,
interconnect and telecom networking segment is ~30%, and preform backward integration is expected to improve segment
margins by ~2-3 percentage points to ~32-33%. Blended EBITDA is lower due to EPC losses of ~INR 800-900 mn per quarter,
which are likely to continue for one to two more quarters.
Order Book
• The total order book stands at ~INR 280 bn. Optical fibre cable and data centre interconnect account for ~INR 190 bn, telecom
and networking products ~INR 78 bn, defence electronics ~INR 3 bn, and EPC including O&M ~INR 35 bn. The ~INR 20 bn
aerospace export order book is not included, as the acquisition is underway, with consolidation expected by Q4FY27. Two
large OFC orders are long-term in nature, with prices revisited annually, while the remainder are short-term (2-6 months). Last
quarter alone saw ~INR 40 bn of orders.

Hindustan Zinc Ltd
Hindustan Zinc, India's benchmark integrated zinc-lead-silver producer, delivered record FY26 performance with EBITDA crossing
INR 220 bn and revenue crossing INR 400 bn for the first time. For FY27, the company targets mined metal of 1,150 KTPA, refined
metal of 1,100 KTPA and silver of 680 tonnes at a cost of production of USD 975-1,000/t; at conservative prices (zinc USD 3,000-
3,200/t, lead USD 1,900-2,000/t, silver USD 60-65/oz), FY27 EBITDA could reach ~INR 280-290 bn. Q1FY27 cost was USD 850/t, aided
by sulphuric acid prices (USD 970/t excluding this). Growth will come from the Phase 1 expansion of refined metal capacity from
1,144 KTPA to 1,400 KTPA by Q2FY29 (250 KTPA at Debari) and an INR 40 bn tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha (10
MTPA feed, commissioning Q4FY28), with a significant production jump from FY30. The company remains net cash (~INR 55 bn)
while paying dividends and expects to sustain costs around USD 1,000/t. The key factors to monitor are project execution and ramp-
up, zinc and silver prices, hedging, the renewable power transition, the royalty outcome on 2030 lease renewals, the silver
demerger and critical mineral exploration.
FY26 Performance & FY27 Guidance
• FY26 was a record year operationally and financially, with EBITDA crossing INR 220 bn and revenue crossing INR 400 bn for the
first time.
• FY27 targets: mined metal production of 1,150 KTPA, refined metal of 1,100 KTPA and silver of 680 tonnes, at a cost of
production of USD 975-1,000/t.
• At conservative assumptions of zinc LME USD 3,000-3,200/t, lead USD 1,900-2,000/t and silver USD 60-65/oz, FY27 EBITDA is
expected at ~INR 280-290 bn.
• The company has paid INR 11 per share in dividends so far this year and expects to remain net cash despite capex and dividends;
cash stood at ~INR 55 bn.
• Over FY27-29, the focus will be on achieving existing smelting capacity of ~1,150 KTPA, with a significant production jump from
FY30.
Cost of Production
• Q1FY27 cost of production was USD 850/t, mainly due to sulphuric acid price benefits; excluding the YoY sulphuric acid benefit,
cost would have been USD 970/t, close to guidance.
• Management expects to sustain costs around USD 1,000/t even after expansion, which it considers the most sustainable level.
• Renewable power share is expected to rise from ~22% (August 2026) to ~35% by FY27-end and ~70% by FY28-end (supported by
a 530 MW round-the-clock RE agreement), with the remaining ~30% from existing thermal plants. Moving to 70% RE is expected
to save ~USD 20-25/t in cost of production.
• After reaching 70% RE, freed-up thermal capacity will support the new smelter capacity from FY30; the long-term goal is 100%
RE and net zero by 2050.
Growth Projects
• Phase 1 of the overall 2 mn tonne refined metal expansion, approved in June 2025, will raise capacity from 1,144 KTPA to 1,400
KTPA, with the 250 KTPA integrated smelter at Debari to be commissioned in Q2FY29. Mine development is progressing in
parallel across mines to support the incremental smelter requirement.
• The tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha, with an investment of ~INR 40 bn and commissioning in Q4FY28, will process
10 mn tonnes of tailings annually (tailings contain ~2% zinc and ~25 ppm silver), producing zinc concentrate with ~20-25 ppm
silver as raw material security for smelters.
• Only the Century mine in Australia has attempted a similar process globally; the technology is being adapted for HZL's
mineralogy. Being new technology, ramp-up may take longer than the usual 1-2 quarters.
• Silver from the tailings concentrate will be recovered via the smelter's fumer plant. R&D is underway on whether germanium
and antimony present in ore can be extracted, but quantities may be too small for viable technology.

• Production from both projects may begin partly in FY29, but conservatively a significant jump should be considered from FY30.
Critical Minerals & Diversification
• HZL has won four critical mineral blocks (including tungsten, potash, rare earths and a recently won yttrium block in Karnataka),
with exploration to be completed by FY29-30.
• Based on exploration results, the company will decide which blocks are commercially viable; greenfield projects typically take 7-
8 years to production, implying output around FY33-34, as HZL aims to become a multi-metal company.
• There are no new zinc-silver mines available in India or globally; the exploration team evaluates government auctions selectively
rather than chasing a bid-to-win ratio.
• Annual exploration spend is modest at ~INR 1-2 bn, and all mines are operating at almost 100% utilisation.
Hedging
• Hedging is purely for risk management, to secure EBITDA margins for part of production, not for treasury income.
• The group policy caps hedging at 20% of the next 12 months' rolling production (e.g., 20% of ~880 KT zinc), irrespective of price
levels; hedging below the cap is a management call.
• Currently ~7-9% of zinc and silver production is hedged. Silver at USD 60-65/oz is not seen as a hedging opportunity, while zinc
at ~USD 4,000/t is being considered for further hedging (potentially up to 10-12%). Silver was hedged when prices were above
USD 100/oz.
Mining Leases & Royalty
• Mining leases for Rampura Agucha, Zawar and Rajpura Dariba expire in 2030, while the remaining leases run until 2048.
Management sees no risk of non-renewal.
• The key risk is a higher royalty: HZL currently pays ~14-15% of revenue as royalty. In a worst case where royalty doubles to
~30%, EBITDA margin could fall from 55-60% to 40-45%, still well above global underground miners' 25-30%, with volume
growth cushioning the impact.
• Management cited the precedent of Cairn's PSC renewal for 10 years with 10% additional profit share, without an auction.
Silver Demerger, Ore Profile & Other Initiatives
• The proposed silver business demerger aims to unlock value, as the stock is seen as undervalued; it would create a pure-play
listed silver company. Timing is under discussion with the government and subject to board approval. It is too early to say where
the critical minerals business would sit.
• Zinc contributes ~50% of EBITDA and silver ~45%; management highlighted that the share price tends to track silver more than
zinc despite zinc at ~USD 4,000/t.
• Ore grade is ~7% (5.5% zinc, 1.5% lead) with ~6.5% ore-to-metal recovery (~80% zinc, ~20% lead). Silver is mainly a by-product of
the lead concentrate (95-100 ppm silver).
• Hindustan Zinc Alloys produced 11-12 KT last year from a 30 KT plant, supplying tailor-made alloys to auto manufacturers as
they begin using galvanised steel in some car parts.
• The Zinc Park industrial park (with partners such as CMR Green Technologies) is at a nascent, 4-5 year horizon stage with
Rajasthan government support. Battery-electric vehicles (including 100 battery-swapping trucks and 10 electric bulkers at
Debari) are being deployed in phases across mines as part of the net-zero roadmap.

Business and Financials
• The company has moved from a flour-focused business to a broader FMCG one under the Hari Om Atta and Spices brand.
Products include fresh chakki atta, healthy flours, spices, rice, pulses and edible oils.

broker as intermediary.

• Operating cash flow has been negative because of receivables, which management attributes to its focus on sales growth. It
was about -INR 61.8 mn in FY25, and management expects an improvement this year.
Listing
• The company listed on the SME platform in 2024 and plans to migrate to the main board after three years (May 2027); ~80% of
the eligibility criteria are already met.

• Merchants using multiple Identixweb applications are considered more likely to remain with the company due to the broader
solution set.
• Bundled pricing is being used to encourage customers to adopt additional applications.
Cross-Sell Potential
• Management does not currently track or disclose a formal cross-sell attach rate across its 14,000+ merchants.
• Merchant product combinations vary depending on individual business requirements.
• In certain cases, merchants can use three products while being charged for two, supporting deeper product penetration.
Platform Risk
• Shopify's continued expansion of native functionality remains a key competitive consideration.
• Wholesale Hero faces greater platform-level exposure as Shopify continues developing its own B2B capabilities.
• Management has moderated incremental investment in Wholesale Hero until Shopify's B2B offering becomes more stable.
• Stellar has lower dependency risk due to its broader delivery-related ecosystem, including payment, shipping and rate-
management products.
Customer Acquisition
• The Shopify App Store remains the primary installation channel for the company's public applications.
• Management likens the Shopify App Store to the Google Play Store and Apple App Store as the mandatory distribution
marketplace for Shopify applications.
• The company supplements marketplace discovery with SEO, social media and e-commerce marketing.
• Management did not disclose a specific CAC/LTV ratio.
Main Board Migration Plan
• Management indicated plans to transition from the BSE SME platform to the main board in approximately two years.
• The company also highlighted the rapid growth of its subsidiary, Munim ERP Pvt Ltd.
• Specific details regarding free float, institutional participation and the transition process were not disclosed due to applicable
regulatory requirements.
Growth Outlook
• Management indicated that FY27-FY28 growth should remain broadly similar to FY26, without providing specific numerical
guidance.
• Standalone growth assumptions include existing fixed-value service projects and continued growth in product installations.
• Munim ERP is expected to benefit from its expanding business, a new Bangalore branch and recurring/renewal revenue.
