India Homes Ltd
India Homes (formerly India Steel Works) is a turnaround story in its early innings: a legacy steel manufacturer that has resolved its
debt, pivoted to Mumbai-focused real estate redevelopment and is assembling a pipeline with a combined GDV of ~INR 50 bn
across Khopoli, Chembur, Matunga and Vadala. The group has two decades of execution experience in Mumbai redevelopment and
is adopting an asset-light JV/share-swap model to bring group-held land banks into the listed entity without heavy capital outflows.
Revenue recognition begins in FY28 at the earliest, making this a pre-revenue, optionality-driven thesis for now.
Debt Resolution & Transformation
• The company repaid Kotak Bank in full (September 2025) and reached a settlement with JC Flowers (March 2026). The balance
payments to JC Flowers are due by the end of December 2026 and will be funded through an e-auction of plant and machinery
(mjunction appointed; the auction is expected around Diwali).
• The company has been renamed from India Steel Works to India Homes. FY26 marks the decisive shift from stainless steel
manufacturing to real estate redevelopment.
• Brought-forward losses on the balance sheet provide a tax shield for future profits.
Project Pipeline
• Waterfall Enclaves (Khopoli): Erstwhile factory land, developed in a JV with Lloyd's Realty. GDV is INR 30+ bn; India Homes
receives a 20% revenue share plus 40% of profit, with expected revenue to India Homes of INR 6-8 bn. It is a mixed development
(plotted, residential and commercial). Land use conversion is pending (6-8 months), with revenue from FY28/FY29 and full
execution over 5-6 years in phases.
• Duke's Court (Chembur): An SRA redevelopment on 4,200 sq m of land with 139 tenements and GDV of ~INR 10 bn. The LOI
from SRA is at the final stage, and the company is in talks with a Category A builder as a partner. India Homes' share is INR 2-2.5
bn.
• King's Court (Matunga): A redevelopment adjacent to the completed Aden Court project, with GDV of INR 3-4 bn. It is currently
held in group entity Level Enterprises, and AGM approval has been received for India Homes to become the majority
stakeholder via a share swap.
• India Court (Vadala West): A smaller redevelopment near the railway/monorail station, with GDV of ~INR 1.5 bn. MHADA
permissions have been received and tenants have agreed. It is fully owned by India Homes.
• Total identified pipeline GDV is ~INR 50 bn. Additional land banks include Vadala East (150,000 sq ft of additional FSI, GDV of INR
7-7.5 bn), the Vadala West cluster (GDV of ~INR 10 bn) and Sewri (details not disclosed).
Business Model & Capital Strategy
• Asset-Light Model: Share swaps and JDAs are preferred over conveyance, avoiding stamp duty of 5-6% and heavy capital outlay.
Projects are brought into India Homes either via majority share purchase of group entities or via JDAs.
• Redevelopment offers structurally higher margins than the erstwhile steel business. Cost discipline from factory operations is
being applied to construction.
• No equity dilution is planned. Promoter holding is ~35-36%, with plans to increase it by converting promoter advances into
shares through a rights issue.
• Minimal cash outflow is expected until revenue commences. Active discussions are underway on 5-6 additional projects
(Santacruz, Bandra West and further projects in Matunga).
Completed Projects (Group Track Record)
• The Link (Andheri; 100,000 sq ft; 2007; commercial and residential), MG Greens (Vadala East; 150,000 sq ft; fully sold out) and
Aden Court (Matunga Five Gardens; 125,000 sq ft; designed by Hafeez Contractor and executed by Ahluwalia).
Guidance
• Revenue will begin in FY28 at the earliest. The company has offered to share detailed financial projections for one-, two-, three-
and five-year periods separately.
• Khopoli land use conversion is expected within 6-8 months. Closure of the JC Flowers settlement and the plant e-auction by
December 2026 will fully clean up the balance sheet.

Indian Phosphate Ltd
Outlook: Indian Phosphate operates two verticals: chemicals (~85% of revenue) and phosphate fertilisers (~15%), with
manufacturing in Udaipur, Rajasthan and Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu. The chemical segment is anchored by LABSA 90%, an anionic
surfactant supplied to detergent and FMCG companies on a B2B cost-plus model. The fertiliser segment produces single super
phosphate (SSP) under the Ankur SSP brand, distributed across 14+ states and expanding to 18.
Integrated Value Chain
• The company has secured its supply chain from source to finished product. For chemicals, it has a long-term sulphur tie-up,
captive sulphuric acid production at Cuddalore, and LABSA output across two plants (450 tonnes per day combined). For
fertilisers, a rock phosphate mine in Madhya Pradesh provides backward integration. Forward integration into magnesium
sulphate and NPK complex fertilisers is being explored.
Capacity Ramp-Up Underway
• The Cuddalore sulphuric acid plant became operational in FY26 using IPO proceeds, and the LABSA plant there has recently
started. The company targets 80-85% utilisation at its chemical plants and is ramping up fertiliser utilisation from the current
~65%. Global DAP supply disruptions (prices moving from ~USD 600 to USD 1,000 per tonne) are creating strong replacement
demand for domestically manufactured SSP.
ICD Logistics Venture
• Indian Phosphate holds a controlling stake in an ICD and multimodal logistics project near Jaipur on the Dedicated Freight
Corridor. Total capex is ~INR 2.9 bn, with ~INR 350-450 mn to be funded by Indian Phosphate through internal accruals. The
project has an 18-month execution timeline and will not require any equity dilution.
FY26 Financial Performance
• Consolidated revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 10.72 bn. EBITDA more than doubled to INR 452 mn, and PAT rose over 3x to INR
236 mn. EBITDA margin improved from 2.4% to 4.2%, and PAT margin from 0.8% to 2.2%. Standalone PAT of INR 214 mn was
the highest in the company's history. The company has no term debt; all borrowings are for working capital (D/E of 0.37x).
Guidance
• Q1FY27 standalone revenue came in at INR 4.36 bn (+81% YoY, +43% QoQ), signalling strong momentum. The company
expects a significant improvement in both revenue and EBITDA in FY27, driven by the ramp-up of the Cuddalore plants and the
commencement of fertiliser import distribution. The ICD and NPK projects are expected to contribute from FY28 onwards. No
specific margin guidance was given due to the volatility of crude-oil-linked raw materials.
View
• Indian Phosphate offers an integrated chemicals and fertilisers play with structural tailwinds from DAP substitution and Make
in India. At ~8x trailing P/E on a revenue base exceeding INR 10 bn, the valuation is undemanding. However, thin EBITDA
margins (~4%) and high raw material intensity are structural features of this business. The ICD project and NPK capacity
expansion could be medium-term catalysts if executed on schedule.

IndiQube Spaces Ltd
Outlook: IndiQube is positioned as a large-scale, enterprise-focused flex workspace provider with a dominant presence in South
India. The company aims to sustain revenue growth of 25-30% over the next few years, with EBITDA margins of 12-21%. Its
strategy focuses on curated supply across Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities, specifically targeting Global Capability Centres (GCCs), which
currently drive 53% of revenue.
Business Model & Product Lines
• GROW: The core plug-and-play workspace model, contributing 83% of total revenue.
• Value-Added Services: These contribute 17% of revenue and comprise:
◦ DesignQube: Interior fit-out as a service.
◦ IndiCare: Facility and asset maintenance for office and retail spaces.
◦ Eco: Sustainability arm focusing on green certifications and solar power.
◦ MyQube: Overarching technology layer with over 1.5 mn downloads in the last year.
Operational Metrics & Financials
• Portfolio Scale: ~137 properties across 17 cities, totalling 10.6 mn sq ft.
• Occupancy: Portfolio occupancy ranges from 80-85%, with steady-state occupancy (centres >12 months old) at 85-90%.
• Unit Economics:
◦ Capex: Standard cost of INR 1,650 per sq ft, with a recovery period of 36 months.
◦ Realisation: Average revenue of INR 200 per sq ft.
◦ Breakeven: Centres typically reach operational breakeven at 55-60% occupancy within 6 months.
◦ Profitability: EBITDA margins are 12-21%, EBIT margins are 12-13%, and PAT margins are 8-9%.
Supply & Client Strategy
• Supply Strategy: Uses a mix of renovated old properties in CBDs, campus environments in peripheries, and floors within tech
parks.
• Client Profile: Focused on large-size, long-stay enterprises; 90% of occupancy comes from clients with >100 seats.
• Client Mix: GCCs (53%), Indian enterprises (30%) and unicorns/start-ups (24%).
• Competitive Edge: Differentiates through a "hub-and-spoke" model and deep talent landscape insights to proactively source
supply in budding micro-markets.
Strategic Advantages & Risks
• Lease Structure: Employs a straight lease model over managed aggregation to provide stability for landlords and better
economics for clients.
• Lock-in Dynamics: Landlords are locked in for 15-20 years, while IndiQube maintains flexibility with a 38-month lock-in.
• Market Position: The largest player in South India, leveraging the high density of GCCs in Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad.
• AI/IT Impact: While demand from traditional Indian IT services has slowed, demand from GCCs across various sectors (e.g.,
healthcare) remains intact.

Indo Borax & Chemicals Ltd
Outlook: Indo Borax & Chemicals has entered a transformational era following a formal change in control on 23 January, with
Zenrock Chemicals Holding acquiring a controlling stake and taking over as the new promoter group. Zenrock initially secured a
50.8% stake in the company and currently holds ~39% equity following the completion of a mandatory open offer. The transaction
marks a shift toward institutionalised, professional management designed to scale the legacy chemical business into a broader
specialty chemicals platform.
Professional Leadership Team
To execute its growth vision, the incoming promoter group has onboarded a full professional leadership team. The team is led by
Managing Director & CEO Suresh Kalra, who brings nearly 28 years of global chemical sector and MNC leadership experience.
Other senior appointments include a new Chief Commercial Officer & CHRO (Kamesh Joshi), a Chief Financial Officer with
extensive pharmaceutical industry experience at Lupin, and experienced functional heads overseeing plant operations and global
supply chain management.
Promoter Continuity & Transition Assurance
To safeguard core institutional knowledge and prevent operational disruption, the incoming management structured a 36-month
formal consultancy agreement with the founding promoters. The outgoing promoter family will actively assist the executive team
with research and development, key client relationships, and raw material procurement. Furthermore, the founding promoters
retain 50% of their personal shareholding (reclassified under the non-promoter category), signalling strong alignment with the
company's long-term value creation strategy.
Monopoly in Pharma/IP-Grade Boric Acid
The company holds a unique strategic moat as the sole domestic manufacturer of pharma/IP-grade boric acid in India, backed by
mandatory BIS certification. IP-grade products command premium pricing, generating 8-10% higher realisations than standard
technical grades. Currently accounting for 6-8% of revenue, this high-margin segment supplies critical excipients to
pharmaceutical manufacturers, consumer personal care brands, cosmetics makers and specialised industrial lubricant producers.
Technical-Grade Boric Acid
Technical-grade boric acid is the foundation of Indo Borax's operations, accounting for ~80% of total sales volume. It is a key input
for ramming mass and refractory materials used in steel manufacturing and induction furnaces, and a core raw material for the
glass, fibre optic and ceramics industries.
Agricultural Micronutrient Growth (DOT)
Indo Borax manufactures disodium octaborate tetrahydrate (DOT), an essential soil micronutrient used to correct boron
deficiencies in agricultural crops. DOT currently contributes 7-8% of total revenue. The Indian market for DOT is estimated at
~10,000 tonnes annually, and domestic demand relies heavily on imports (~8,500 tonnes a year). Indo Borax produced 900 tonnes
last year and is ramping up production to 1,400-1,700 tonnes this fiscal year, against installed capacity of 4,000 tonnes, to
substitute imports.
Organic Debottlenecking & Capacity Utilisation
The Pithampur facility has installed capacity of 20,000 tonnes per annum. Having produced ~15,000 tonnes in FY25, management
is executing an organic debottlenecking programme to increase output to 17,500-18,000 tonnes by FY27. This aims to raise
capacity utilisation to 90-95% without major capex, driving operating leverage and margin expansion.
Downstream Expansion into Boron Oxide
As part of Phase 1 of its downstream expansion roadmap, Indo Borax has initiated capex to set up local manufacturing of boron
oxide. India currently relies entirely on imported boron oxide. This value-added derivative commands 2.5-3x the price realisation
of standard boric acid. The project has a 12-18 month commercialisation timeline, with capacity utilisation planned at 30-40% in
FY28 and 100% in FY29, alongside future captive boric acid expansion.
Product Pipeline & Future Derivative Phases
Beyond Boron Oxide, management is evaluating Phase 2 and Phase 3 downstream development programmes centred on zinc
borate, a fire-retardant additive widely used in plastics, polymers, textiles, and coatings. Technical feasibility, process chemistry,
and market entry strategies are currently undergoing detailed evaluation by internal commercial and technical teams.

Strategic Acquisition of Kronox Lab Sciences
In a major inorganic expansion move, Indo Borax acquired a 64.26% controlling stake in Kronox Lab Sciences Ltd, a publicly listed
specialty chemicals manufacturer. Kronox adds a high-margin product portfolio of 185 high-purity chemical products supplying
pharmaceutical excipients, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), laboratory reagents, biotech applications, and nutraceuticals.
The transaction was funded through a combination of internal cash reserves, liquidation of liquid mutual funds, non-core asset
sales, and external acquisition finance.
Manufacturing Scaling & Dahej Capex Programme
To support Kronox Lab Sciences' medium-term growth trajectory, management has formally approved an INR 1.1 bn capex plan.
The capex will be deployed on newly acquired land at the industrial hub in Dahej, Gujarat, establishing state-of-the-art
infrastructure to significantly expand Kronox's manufacturing capacity and global client footprint.
Capital Discipline & Non-Core Real Estate Monetisation
Under new leadership, Indo Borax is enforcing strict capital allocation discipline by liquidating historical non-core real estate
assets, including commercial office premises and residential apartments. Proceeds are being recycled directly into high-return
chemical manufacturing operations. The remaining legacy office spaces are slated for sale, which will end the historical rental
income stream and focus the revenue model on core chemical manufacturing.
Corporate Restructuring & Balance Sheet Streamlining
To reduce administrative overhead and optimise capital structure efficiency, the board of directors approved the formal
amalgamation of its wholly owned subsidiary, Indo Borax Infrastructure Pvt Ltd. The merger consolidates balance sheet resources,
simplifies corporate compliance, and concentrates management focus entirely on chemical operations.
Historical & Q1 Performance Benchmarks
Under the outgoing management, Indo Borax delivered FY25 revenue of ~INR 1.75 bn and PAT of INR 425 mn. Demonstrating early
momentum under the new leadership, the company reported Q1 revenue of ~INR 700 mn and EBITDA of INR 198 mn.
Near-Term Guidance (FY26 & FY27)
For FY26, consolidated revenue is projected at ~INR 2.15 bn, with a PAT target of INR 500 mn. For FY27, revenue guidance is INR
2.5-2.65 bn, supported by higher debottlenecked volumes and an improved product mix.
Medium-Term Growth Targets (Standalone Units)
Over a 2-3 year horizon, management targets scaling standalone Indo Borax revenue to ~INR 4 bn through high capacity utilisation
and boron oxide commercialisation. Kronox Lab Sciences, on a standalone basis, is targeted to grow from a baseline revenue of
~INR 1 bn to INR 4+ bn over the medium term as the new Dahej facility comes online.
Long-Term Vision (Consolidated FY30 Guidance)
Combining organic volume expansion, high-value downstream derivatives and the full commercial ramp-up of Kronox Lab
Sciences, management has outlined a consolidated FY30 group revenue target of INR 7.5-9 bn.
Raw Material Dynamics & Global Sourcing
Because India lacks commercially viable natural boron ore deposits, raw material availability is a critical operational factor. Indo
Borax mitigates supply chain risks through multi-year supply contracts with major global miners in Turkey (primary supply source),
backed by secondary supply channels across North and South America to ensure uninterrupted plant operations.
Structural Protection from Chinese Imports
Indo Borax is naturally insulated from Chinese low-cost competition or dumping risks. Chinese chemical manufacturers also lack
native commercial boron ore reserves and rely on imports from the same global mining hubs in Turkey and South America.
Consequently, Chinese producers enjoy no raw material cost advantage, creating a balanced competitive environment in the
domestic Indian market.
High Entry Barriers & Industry Protection
The business is protected by strong structural entry barriers. Unorganised downstream users of ramming mass and industrial
borates are unable to backward-integrate due to the complex refining chemistry required for crude ore, highly restricted global
raw material supply networks, stringent BIS and regulatory compliance and capital-intensive working capital cycles.

Indo Count Industries Ltd
Business
• Indo Count has been a home textiles (bed linen) maker since 2006, with integrated spinning and weaving. It is the world's
largest bed linen producer, with capacity of 153 mn metres.
• Exports go to 50+ countries, and the US is ~70% of exports. India holds ~60% of the US cotton bedsheet market, Pakistan ~20-
22% and China ~8%. Indo Count's share is ~20-22%.
• The top 10 customers are ~70% of revenue. Purchase orders run quarterly or half-yearly under 1-2 year agreements. Working
capital is ~100-120 days.
Indo Count 2.0 and the New Businesses
• Brands: Wamsutta (a US brand from 1846) was acquired in April 2024 and launched in D2C in July 2025, with more channels to
follow. Three licensed brands, including Fieldcrest, sit alongside it. The brand business is profitable and its working capital is
similar to the core's.
• Utility bedding (pillows and quilts): two US plants were acquired in September-October 2024, and a North Carolina greenfield
plant started in January 2026. Capacity is now 31 mn pillows and 1.5 mn quilts, up from 13 mn pillows.
• New business revenue was INR 2.85 bn in FY25 and INR 7.92 bn in FY26. Q1FY27 was INR 3.87 bn, and FY27 is targeted at INR
15 bn.
Targets
• Management targets doubling revenue from INR 40 bn (FY25) to INR 80 bn by CY28. This comprises INR 55 bn from the core
and INR 25 bn (~USD 275 mn) from new businesses, split between ~USD 100 mn from brands and ~USD 175 mn from utility
bedding.
• EBITDA margin targets for CY28 are 15% for the core, 15% for utility and 16-17% for brands.
• FY27 guidance is revenue of INR 55 bn at an EBITDA margin of ~13%.
• Core volumes were ~105-106 mn metres in FY25 and 94 mn metres in FY26 (tariff-hit). FY27 guidance is 105-110 mn metres,
and the CY28 aim is 140-145 mn metres (90-95% utilisation).
• Q1 core volume was flat YoY at ~25-26 mn metres; management noted that quarterly volumes fluctuate and that it is on track
for the full year.
• Realisation has been flat at ~INR 365 per metre since FY24, because last year's tariff was shared with customers. Management
focuses on profitability rather than realisation.
Capex
• No growth capex is needed for the INR 80 bn target. FY27 capex is ~INR 2.5 bn, spread over 12-18 months: INR 700-800 mn for
maintenance, ~INR 850-900 mn for a zero-liquid-discharge facility at the Bhilad plant and ~INR 800-850 mn for spinning unit
expansion and modernisation.
• No acquisitions are planned.
US Tariffs and Export Incentives
• Management says it lost no customer or order when tariffs hit 50% last year. The first 25% was not shared since competitor
countries were at 18-20%. The additional 25% Russia-oil penalty was shared on a case-by-case basis.
• Management does not know whether a new tariff will come and says it will deal with it then.
• Government export incentives (~8-10% of value, depending on the product) run until 30 September. Management is confident
of a ~5-year extension, since these schemes refund embedded taxes so that taxes are not exported.
UK and EU FTAs
• The UK FTA has been in force since 15 July. Indo Count has an office in Manchester and already ships to the UK.
• Indian exporters previously faced a 10-12% duty disadvantage in the EU, and a level playing field should lift orders. Customer
meetings and inquiries have doubled, and benefits should show with a lag of 3-4 quarters.
• Management suggested the FTAs will be a big part of volume growth from ~105 mn metres to ~140 mn metres over 2-3 years.
• The rest of the world accounts for ~30% of exports and is expected to grow ~20% this year.
Vapi-Area Flood
• The Bhilad plant has capacity of ~45 mn metres, about a third of the total.
• It flooded on 22-23 July, restarted partially around 10-12 August and is now back to normal. Some processing was shifted to
Kolhapur.
• Management expects no major annual impact. Inventory, plant and machinery and loss of profit are insured, and the claim is
being filed.
Demand and Costs
• US demand is good, with no inventory glut or undercutting seen, and Chinese suppliers are not strong in this category.
• Yarn prices are higher on Chinese demand. Management plans inventory for two quarters and sees no supply issue.
• The company's sustainability index score rose from 45 to 78 out of 100 in two years, and it says it is well placed for EU rules.
• Management declined to give cost breakdowns, product-level realisation, competitor comparisons or customer names, and
pointed to the annual report and investor deck.

Indo Gulf Crop Sciences Ltd

Capacity Expansion & Capex

Plant Nutrition & Biologicals

Margin Expansion
Plant nutrition and biologicals generate ~53-60% gross margins in B2C versus ~30-34% for crop protection. Their contribution has
increased from ~7% of sales in FY22 to ~10% in FY26 and is targeted at ~15-16% over the next ~3 years, supporting overall margin
improvement.
B2C Expansion & Distribution
Indo Gulf has ~7,000-8,000 B2C channel partners, with AGPL supporting distribution expansion. AGPL has expanded from 5-6
states into Odisha and Chhattisgarh, while the company is strengthening its presence across South and Central India.

Infollion Research Services Ltd
Business and Financials
• Infollion is an expert network founded in 2009 and listed on the NSE. Clients include investment funds, consulting and research
firms, and large corporates.
• Its edge is a research team of ~250 people, organised by sector, that maps industries and finds the right expert rather than just
searching for titles.
• FY26 revenue was INR 1,003 mn (+29.8% YoY), EBITDA was INR 147 mn and PAT was INR 127 mn.
• Revenue has grown from INR 340 mn in FY23, a ~43.5% CAGR to FY26.
• The company is debt-free with ~INR 435 mn of cash. Operating cash flow was ~INR 105 mn, and DSO improved from 83 to 67
days.
• The network has 136,000 experts and delivered 20,700+ calls in FY26 across 55+ sectors. More than one-third of business was
delivered through experts based outside India.
• Over 80% of revenue comes from pre-panelled experts, and ~15% of the panel is active in a year. Management says the active
set keeps rotating.
• Over 95% of clients are repeat clients, and the top 10 have been clients for 10-12+ years.
Demand Trend
• In March, management cited a ~25% dip in volumes. Stress persists but has eased since March, and there were signs of
recovery in September, though management is unsure whether this will hold.
• Management attributes the slowdown to the macro environment for consulting, research and funds, not one cause.
• On AI, management accepts it has hurt shallow, industry-overview calls. It says 92-95% of calls are deep domain and cannot be
replaced by AI because the knowledge is undocumented.
• Management said it did lose some business to AI, but sees itself as less exposed because it operates at the premium end.
• Transcript subscriptions are offered selectively. Management does not see much value in them, and says deep-domain
transcripts would be very costly.
Growth Levers
• Hooka (corporate L&D): Expert-led training. It added 40 logos last year and crossed INR 10 mn of revenue in FY26. The plan is
to move to full-stack managed training services.
• US and MENA: each crossed INR 10 mn in FY26 (~1% each). The US team is ~50 people on US shifts, and there is a permanent
resource in Germany.
• Management plans a permanent presence in the US, Europe and Dubai once it becomes viable.
• Third Eye: a new product in which domain experts validate AI outputs, plus AI integrations and APIs.
• No revenue targets for 3-5 years or US and MENA market sizing were shared. Segment-wise margins were also not disclosed,
since growth takes priority over margin in new territories.
Margins and Capital Allocation
• Management says it kept margins steady and is reinvesting operating leverage in better expert payouts. It also cited some
promotional calls for clients, and pointed to the annual report for details.
• Cash of INR 435 mn sits in liquid funds earning 6-7% and is earmarked for M&A. A small strategic investment has also been
made.
• There are no dividend or buyback plans at present.
Model and Competition
• Experts are paid per project at honorariums they choose, with no fixed commitments. The panel is invitation-only, with an
average of 25+ years of experience.
• Compliance includes NDAs and tool-based sign-offs. Infollion staff do not join client-expert calls, which limits
disintermediation. Clients and experts rate each other.
• Competitors are the global networks Third Bridge, AlphaSights and GLG, plus the homegrown InsightAlpha and others.
• Management estimates it is the largest homegrown player, with the next three combined smaller in revenue. It does not
consider Kavi a peer.
• Marketing relies mostly on client referrals, with some international visits and events.

Outlook: Management expects operating EBITDA margins to stay broadly stable at the current 16% this year. It targets raising

Financial Performance: Annual merchandise sales are about INR 2,000 mn, and revenue grew by more than 30%. Operating

paid a dividend, but management plans to set a dividend policy as the business scales.
Long-Term Potential: Rising online and infant wear contributions, an EBO network with attractive store economics and expansion
into North and South India give the company several growth levers. Existing capacity can support about 2x the current revenue.
Bringing working capital down from its high level of about 384 days (receivables plus inventory) will be the key monitorable for
cash flow.

IRM Energy Ltd
Outlook: The company is targeting 10-15% YoY volume growth, supported by continued CNG expansion in Banaskantha and rapid
ramp-up in Namakkal-Trichy. Management is targeting 27-28% gross margins and minimum EBITDA of INR 7 per SCM, while
keeping spot sourcing low through long-term contracts. Key monitorables include the pace of CNG/PNG penetration in Namakkal-
Trichy, utilisation of the planned INR 2.5 bn capex, industrial volume recovery at Fatehgarh Sahib following regulatory
implementation, and the sustainability of margins after the Q1 one-off benefit.
Gas Sourcing & Margin
• ~67% of the gas sourcing portfolio comprises domestic gas and HPHT gas, which carry government-determined ceiling prices
and provide greater cost visibility.
• Commercial and industrial volumes are largely sourced through long-term contracts with GAIL, IOCL, HPCL, RIL and BP, linked
to benchmarks such as Brent and Henry Hub.
• Spot-market sourcing remained below 1% and was <0.5% in Q1FY27, supporting margin stability and limiting exposure to spot
LNG volatility.
• Q1FY27 gross margin stood at 32%; however, the company is targeting a more sustainable 27-28% gross margin going forward.
• Selling prices are adjusted based on gas-cost movements, competition and alternate-fuel pricing to protect margins.
Volume Growth
• The company expects overall volume growth of 10-15% YoY, with incremental volumes primarily driven by Banaskantha and
the ramp-up of Tiruchirappalli and Namakkal.
• Tiruchirappalli and Namakkal volumes have increased sharply, with Q1FY27 gas sales at ~6 mmscm versus ~2.84 mmscm in
Q1FY26.
• Management expects volumes in these newer GAs to continue ramping up as the CNG ecosystem and infrastructure mature.
• Namakkal and Tiruchirappalli are expected to become meaningful growth contributors over the next 2-3 years.
Namakkal-Trichy Ramp-up
• The company has established 48-49 CNG stations across Namakkal and Tiruchirappalli, providing the infrastructure required
for volume expansion.
• State transport buses are increasingly shifting from diesel to CNG, supporting the initial volume ramp-up.
• Around 90% of LPG/other-fuel three-wheelers targeted under the company's initiatives have been converted to CNG.
• Four-wheeler penetration remains at an early stage but is improving as station density and consumer confidence increase.
• Further growth is expected as pipeline infrastructure expands and PNG commercial/domestic connections are added.
Geographic Potential
• Banaskantha: The GA is mature but continues to deliver ~10-15% CNG volume growth, supported by agricultural activity, local
mobility and increasing CNG vehicle penetration.
• Fatehgarh Sahib: Industrial volumes are currently around 200,000 SCM/day; further upside could emerge from
implementation of NGT-related pollution-control measures.
• Diu & Gir Somnath: CNG volumes are supported by tourism and seasonal traffic, while conversion of commercial customers to
PNG is providing additional growth.
• Namakkal-Trichy: Considered the key emerging growth engine, with significant headroom for CNG as well as future PNG
penetration.
Capex & Infrastructure
• FY27 capex is planned at ~INR 2.5 bn, including ~INR 1.5 bn towards Namakkal and Trichy, with the balance allocated across
other GAs.
• Capex will primarily focus on CNG stations and pipeline network expansion.
• In mature GAs such as Banaskantha, investments will focus on bringing high-volume stations online to improve station
economics and reduce RTKM costs.
• In Namakkal and Trichy, the priority is network expansion to build CNG availability and accelerate ecosystem adoption.
• A CNG station typically takes 2-3 years to reach full utilisation, depending on the maturity of the underlying market.
Strategic Initiatives
• Organic growth remains the primary focus, particularly through the untapped potential in Namakkal and Trichy and continued
CNG growth in Banaskantha.
• Management remains open to acquisitions, but only where valuation and regulatory economics are favourable; no concrete
acquisition has been announced.
• IRM Energy is already present in LNG and LCNG, including LNG dispensing for long-haul trucks and LCNG stations in Trichy,
Namakkal and Vairavanth.
• The company is also evaluating e-mobility and other green-energy opportunities, including integration of solar power with
CNG stations.
• Capital allocation will remain focused on opportunities offering attractive returns relative to the existing CGD business.

CBG Economics
• Under the CBG mechanism, GAIL acts as the nodal intermediary, purchasing CBG from producers and supplying it to CGD
companies.
• The additional cost paid to CBG producers is normalised across the domestic gas portfolio, resulting in only a modest increase
in the effective domestic gas cost for CGD players.
• Management indicated that CBG remains economically beneficial for CGD companies under the current structure.
Margin Outlook

circumstances.
• Management does not expect Q1-level margins to sustain and is targeting 27-28% gross margin going forward.

anticipated volume ramp-up.

currently under evaluation.
Customer Mix

• As pipeline infrastructure expands, management expects PNG commercial and domestic volumes to gradually increase.
• The company expects the customer mix in newer GAs to diversify over time, similar to the transition observed in Diu & Gir

Jainik Power Cables Ltd
Outlook: Jainik Power Cables is poised for a structural transformation from a wire rod commodity supplier into an integrated,
higher-margin cables and conductors platform. With a firm order book exceeding INR 1 bn, L1/L2 positions in Haryana tenders and
vendor approvals across five states, the company enters FY27 with visible revenue momentum. Management expects PAT margins
of 4-5% in FY27, expanding to 6-7% from FY28 as cable volumes scale, alongside annual top-line growth of at least 20%. The
product mix is set to shift decisively, with cables and conductors rising to 20-30% of revenue in FY27 and over 50% by FY28. Peak
revenue capacity of INR 7.5 bn at the Sonipat plant, targeted utilisation of 85% by FY28, an INR 450 mn working capital raise and a
planned INR 500-600 mn CCV line for HT cables once revenue crosses INR 6 bn underpin the next phase of growth, with copper
and export markets in Africa and the Middle East offering long-term optionality.
Revenue Growth
• Management targets sustainable annual top-line growth of at least 20% over the coming years.
Margin Guidance
• Management anticipates PAT margins of 4-5% in FY27 as cable and conductor order execution accelerates in the second half.
From FY28 onwards, PAT margins are projected at 6-7% as higher-margin cable volumes scale. Legacy wire rod trading yielded
EBITDA margins of 4.5-5%, while the new cables and conductors business achieves EBITDA margins of 9-10%.
Order Book
• The company has a firm order book exceeding INR 1 bn. In Haryana utility procurement, it emerged as L1 in two tenders and
L2 in a third, with a cumulative value exceeding INR 250 mn.
Backward Integration
• Jainik operates a fully backward-integrated model across the aluminium electrical value chain, sourcing and importing
aluminium scrap and ingots, converting them into wire rods, and processing those rods internally into finished cables and
conductors. This delivers a 3-5% cost advantage over non-integrated regional competitors. While standalone cable producers
operate at around 6% margins, Jainik captures value at multiple processing steps to achieve overall margins of approximately
8%.
Product Portfolio
• The company produces aluminium wire rods, aluminium wire, aluminium conductors, LT power cables, aerial bunched cables,
HT cables and medium-voltage covered conductors. Captive consumption of internal wire rods transforms the business from a
commodity supplier into an integrated electrical products platform.
Quality and Certifications
• Jainik operates a permanent NABL-accredited laboratory on-site. It is ISO-certified and holds multiple BIS certifications,
including IS 398 Parts 2, 4 and 6, IS 7098 Part 1 and IS 14255.
Clients and Vendors
• The client base spans discoms, EPC contractors, infrastructure firms and institutional buyers. Key clients and pipeline partners
include Adani Energy, Raghava Construction, Diamond Power, Andhra Pradesh discoms and MP discoms. Inquiries have come
from Vikran Engineering, Ashoka Buildcon and Gold Bridge. Vendor registrations are secured in Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra,
Chhattisgarh, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, with approvals underway for Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Power Grid. Qualification
timelines range from 10 days in Madhya Pradesh to over six months for railway approvals. Power Grid qualification requires a
proven supply track record of at least 1,000 kilometres of cable to state discoms.
Exports
• Jainik has received official inquiries for aluminium cables and conductors from African countries. Management views African
and Middle Eastern markets as crucial long-term growth vectors driven by power infrastructure development and
electrification demands.
Peak Potential and Utilisation
• The Sonipat plant operates on 2 acres of owned industrial land plus 1 acre of leased space. At full infrastructure utilisation,
peak potential revenue capacity is INR 7.5 bn, achieved by capturing INR 4 bn of internal wire rod production and processing it
into finished cables and conductors. Management targets plant capacity utilisation of ~85% by FY28.
Product Mix Transition
• In FY27, cables and conductors are expected to generate 20-30% of total revenue as order execution commences in the second
half. By FY28, they are targeted to exceed 50% of total revenue, replacing standalone wire rod sales as the primary revenue
contributor.

Future Expansion
• The company plans to invest INR 500-600 mn in a continuous catenary vulcanisation (CCV) line for HT cables once total

threshold, Jainik intends to evaluate entering the copper segment for copper wires, conductors, and LT and HT cables.
Capital Allocation

allocated towards operational working capital, not plant capex.
Geographic Expansion
• Historically, 90-100% of revenue came from Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Tight margins on raw
wire rods and high transportation costs previously restricted distribution. Higher-margin finished cables allow the company to
absorb freight costs and expand pan-India into western and southern states.
Partnerships
• Jainik has established a strategic alliance with Saaga Industries, a cable manufacturer, to supply wire rods and utilise spare
manufacturing capacity for conductor production.
Growth Drivers and Demand
• Demand is propelled by government initiatives in power distribution, smart cities, and national highway infrastructure.
Management foresees strong industry demand over the next decade exceeding available national manufacturing capacity,
even as major industrial groups enter the sector.
Raw Materials and Hedging
• To protect against aluminium price volatility on global exchanges, Jainik maintains a fixed baseline inventory and executes
simultaneous back-to-back buying and selling or hedges positions on the LME and MCX. Raw material price fluctuations affect
working capital requirements rather than eroding profit margins.

Capex & Funding

• Capex is expected to be funded primarily through internal reserves, although debt funding could also be considered.

Working Capital & Receivables

• Private customers generally offer easier/faster execution and communication and can place larger orders.

Jeena Seekho Life Care Ltd
Jeena Sikho Lifecare Ltd
Outlook: Management is targeting INR 30,000 mn revenue over the next 3-5 years, supported by expansion across Ayurveda
products, hospitals, clinics, wellness centres, virtual OPD and preventive healthcare. The company aims to build a 360-degree
healthcare ecosystem, with growth driven by increasing bed capacity, direct-to-consumer product sales, health-insurance
penetration, college-hospital partnerships and repeat/referral-led customer acquisition.
Products & Margins
• FY25 revenue was indicated at INR 8 bn, comprising INR 4.15 bn from products and INR 3.25 bn from services. Product gross
margins have remained ~90%, with management expecting sustainable margins in the 85-90% range. Historically,
manufacturing was largely outsourced with company-led quality control; the company is now moving towards dedicated
manufacturing capacity, with an exclusive facility expected to commence operations shortly and plans to gradually shift
production across seven locations.
Direct Distribution & E-Commerce
• Management is currently de-emphasising the traditional distributor/OTC model due to high channel costs, estimated at 60-65%
of product economics after distributor, retailer, C&F and advertising margins. The focus is shifting towards owned centres,
hospitals, e-commerce and direct online sales. Management highlighted sales of 95,000 units of Pure Yakrit Pliha and 70,000
units of sea buckthorn juice during the previous month, with direct sales providing materially higher margins and better control
over product authenticity.
Hospital & Bed Expansion
• The company had 2,400 operational beds as of Q1, with management targeting 3,000-3,500 beds by year-end and a longer-term
ambition of 7,000-10,000 beds. Q1 occupancy was 61%, with management preferring a sustainable 60% occupancy level rather
than maximising utilisation at the expense of service quality. Average revenue per occupied bed (ARPOB) was indicated at INR
8,300 for the last quarter.
College-Hospital Model
• The college-hospital partnership model is a key component of the expansion strategy. Ayurveda colleges are required to
maintain 100-bed teaching hospitals, many of which have historically operated with low patient utilisation. Jeena Sikho has
taken over three such facilities across Mohali, Vrindavan and Mehkar, with management stating that these centres are
operating at high utilisation. The model also provides access to trained manpower and reduces capital intensity. Management
indicated that capex can decline from INR 0.3-0.4 mn per bed under the conventional model to INR 0.1-0.15 mn per bed under
this model, with 20 additional opportunities reportedly in the pipeline.
Insurance & Preventive Healthcare
• Health insurance is becoming an important growth driver, with management indicating that 26% of revenue came from health
insurance in the referenced period. Increasing acceptance of Ayurveda under insurance and government initiatives such as
Ayushman Bharat are expected to support hospital and bed expansion. Management also expects greater adoption of
preventive healthcare and Ayurveda to support long-term demand.
Customer Acquisition & Marketing
• Management highlighted a significant improvement in customer-acquisition economics, with marketing expenditure contained
at INR 600 mn despite strong revenue growth. The company attributes this to referrals, repeat purchases and patient-led brand
advocacy. The integrated model allows customers acquired through products to be converted into healthcare-service
customers and vice versa, reducing incremental acquisition costs.
Research & Clinical Development
• Research is being scaled up through a dedicated research centre, with staff hiring and equipment procurement already
underway. Management stated that the company has published 201+ research papers, with 150 papers in the pipeline.
Collaborations mentioned include IIT Ropar and Punjab University, while discussions with ILBS were also highlighted. The
company intends to strengthen clinical research, evidence generation and integration of Ayurveda with broader healthcare
ecosystems.
Luxury Wellness
• Ekam Wellness, positioned as the company's luxury wellness offering, is expected to soft-launch on 31 October. The luxury
segment is intended to complement the company's mainstream hospitals, clinics and wellness centres and provide an
additional higher-end preventive-healthcare offering.

Justo Realfintech Ltd
Outlook: Justo is transitioning from a traditional real estate mandate platform into a broader, technology-led, full-stack real estate
services company. The company currently has a strong presence in Mumbai and Pune, with 46 live mandates worth INR 6,500 mn
as of July 2026, and it has sold INR 11,500 mn of inventory across 15,650 units since inception. Management expects growth to be
driven by geographic expansion, entry into premium real estate through Chestertons, higher-margin advisory businesses and new
verticals.
Business Model & Scale
• Justo operates as a B2B, tech-enabled real estate mandate partner, providing developers with end-to-end services covering
project strategy, product positioning, pricing, marketing, sales, CRM, home loans and collections. The company has 400+
employees, 6,000+ RERA-registered channel partners and a developer network of 750+ in Pune and 500 across the rest of
Maharashtra/Mumbai. Justo's model converts developers' fixed sales and marketing costs into a variable, success-based cost
structure.
Growth Track Record
• The company has delivered a 32% revenue CAGR, 51.9% EBITDA CAGR and 52.0% PAT CAGR. As of July 2026, Justo had sold INR
11,500 mn of inventory (15,650 units) since inception. Management did not provide specific FY27/FY28 revenue guidance but
indicated expectations of robust growth, supported by expansion into faster-growing markets and segments.
Chestertons & Premium Real Estate
• Justo acquired rights in 2026 to operate Chestertons' IPC business in India, providing access to a premium segment beyond its
existing core market. While Justo currently largely operates in the INR 6-30 mn ticket-size segment, Chestertons will target
properties with minimum ticket sizes of INR 40-60 mn. Key segments include luxury residences, villas, branded residences,
plotting, second homes and weekend homes.
New Growth Verticals
• Through Chestertons, the company intends to expand into capital markets, fundraising, JV/JD transactions, commercial leasing,
hospitality, facility management, PMC and development management. Management has identified a cumulative target
addressable market of INR 1,400,000 mn across the segments it plans to address. The company expects these businesses to
contribute meaningfully to growth over the next 24 months.
Margin Expansion Strategy
• The current revenue mix is 80% through channel partners and 20% through direct sales. Management plans to increase the
share of direct customer acquisition, which would reduce the commissions paid to channel partners and support profitability. In
addition, the company is focusing on higher-margin businesses such as IPC and financial advisory to protect and potentially
improve margins.
Technology & Project Manthan
• The company is developing its proprietary technology platform, Project Manthan, covering the real estate lifecycle from lead
nurturing and pre-sales through field sales, collections and CRM. Phases 1-3 have been completed, while Phase 4 covering
collections and CRM is under development. Deep-tech and AI capabilities are expected to be integrated into the later stages,
with the complete technology stack targeted for release around January. Management has already observed some efficiency
improvement from the deployed technology, although the larger benefits are expected after full implementation.
Geographic Expansion
• Justo's current operations are concentrated in Mumbai, Pune and Nashik, with Mumbai and Pune accounting for the majority of
revenues. Over the next 12 months, the company plans to enter Gujarat/Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Hyderabad and Nagpur, while
markets including Delhi/NCR, Kolkata, Raipur, Indore and Chennai are being considered over the next 24 months. Geographic
expansion is aimed at reducing concentration in Mumbai and Pune and accessing faster-growing markets.
Receivables & Collections
• Management stated that there are no material recovery issues and considers the outstanding receivables to be good debt.
Around 73% of outstanding receivables are less than 90 days old. Management highlighted that substantial collections were
achieved during H1 and expects recoveries to remain in line with its commitments.
Seasonality
• Real estate remains a highly festive-driven business, with the majority of revenue captured during Q3 and Q4. Management
broadly indicated a 30:70 H1:H2 revenue split, making the second half particularly important for annual performance.

Kalpataru Projects International Ltd
Outlook: Kalpataru Projects International enters the remainder of FY27 with strong momentum across its core power T&D, B&F,
and oil & gas businesses, underpinned by year-to-date order inflows of ~INR 180 bn plus an L1 pipeline of ~INR 80 bn, together
representing ~INR 260 bn against a full-year guidance of INR 300+ bn, with potential for upward revision at Q2. Management
remains confident of achieving ~15% revenue growth, ~75 bps margin expansion, working capital below 90 days, and further debt
reduction, supported by better-margin orders, lower interest costs, and efficient execution. Growth visibility is reinforced by a
strong Middle East oil & gas and water pipeline, a large HVDC and GIS substation opportunity in India, a fast-growing data centre
vertical with end-to-end MEP capabilities, and the INR 1.5 bn Raipur captive rolling mill as the first step in backward integration.
With capex likely to surpass the ~INR 8 bn guidance, non-core asset monetisation progressing, and the LMG Sweden stake sale
completed, the company appears well-positioned to deliver on its full-year guidance while building a broader, higher-margin
growth platform for FY28 and beyond.
Q1FY27 Performance and Full-Year Guidance
Kalpataru Projects International reported Q1 revenue growth of ~9% to INR 63.96 bn with EBITDA margin expansion of ~30 bps.
Management reaffirmed full-year FY27 guidance of ~15% revenue growth, ~75 bps margin improvement, working capital below 90
days, significant debt reduction, and order inflow in excess of INR 300 bn. The company is on track to meet or exceed these
targets, with order inflow plus L1 already at ~INR 260 bn against the INR 300 bn guidance, leaving room for a potential upward
revision when Q2 results are announced.
Order Inflow and Tender Pipeline
Year-to-date order inflows stand at ~INR 180 bn, supplemented by an L1 pipeline of ~INR 80 bn, taking the total to ~INR 260 bn.
Management indicated a possible upward revision of the INR 300 bn guidance given strong tendering activity across power T&D,
B&F, and oil & gas. Notable wins include a ~INR 17-18 bn metal and mining processing plant order and a ~INR 40+ bn oil & gas
order in the Middle East. The tender pipeline remains robust across all three core businesses, with HVDC opportunities of ~INR
500-600 bn expected over the next three to four years.
Debt Reduction and Working Capital
Consolidated net debt declined by ~INR 19 bn to ~INR 9.17 bn in Q1FY27. Management expects further improvement in working
capital and debt metrics in Q2 and H2FY27, with no anticipated deterioration. The water segment's outstanding billed plus
unbilled receivables remain at ~INR 14-15 bn, but collection intensity has improved compared to last year, with ~INR 3.8-4 bn
collected in Q1 and similar amounts in Q2.
Oil & Gas and Middle East Expansion
The Middle East oil & gas market remains a key growth driver, with significant tender activity in Saudi Arabia and the UAE focused
on onshore greenfield and brownfield projects, gas supply, and energy security. The company is executing its legacy Aramco
project, which is ~60-65% complete and slated for completion in the next 12 months, providing confidence to scale the
international oil & gas business. A second large oil & gas order in excess of INR 40 bn was recently secured in the Middle East, with
further wins expected in H2FY27 and FY28.
Water Segment and Middle East Desalination
Water is not a new business, with prior international projects in the Maldives, Sri Lanka and Mongolia. The first Middle East water
treatment order of ~INR 3.44 bn, secured in JV with a technology partner, opens a significant desalination and water supply
opportunity over the next five to seven years. The margin profile in this segment is in line with the T&D and B&F businesses,
nearing double digits. The company is qualifying with major Middle East clients and expects to scale this vertical meaningfully
from next year.
Data Centre and B&F Opportunities
Within the B&F segment, data centres represent a growing opportunity with a civil-only addressable market of ~INR 150-200 bn,
and 3-4x that if MEP is included. The company has completed two data centres on the civil front and is currently executing one in
the Mumbai region, having developed end-to-end civil plus MEP capabilities. It has bid for two to three large data centre projects
and expects to convert at least one, worth ~INR 10-20 bn, this year. Other B&F verticals include residential, commercial, airports,
and industrial processing plants.
Backward Integration and Capex
The Raipur rolling mill, the first backward integration project, is entirely captive, with planned annual capacity of ~150,000 tonnes
(~12,500 tonnes per month) at an investment of ~INR 1.5 bn. Payback is expected in one to two years, with benefits including
lower inventory and greater flexibility in rolling billets into the required tower sections. FY27 capex guidance of ~INR 8 bn is likely
to be surpassed, with ~INR 5 bn already incurred by Q2. Capex is directed towards the rolling mill, B&F staging and fabrication, oil
& gas automatic welding and elevated metro projects.

Karbonsteel Engineering Ltd
Outlook: Management targets 20-30% annual growth, supported by the expansion of capacity from 30,000 MTPA to 54,000 MTPA.
It maintains its guidance of about 13% EBITDA margin. Of the current order book, INR 2,000-2,250 mn is expected to be executed

FY26 Performance: Total revenue was INR 3 bn. Normalised EBITDA margin held at ~13%, with realisation of ~INR 95,000 per

PAT & One-Offs: PAT fell about 26% because of non-recurring items and operational delays. These included a one-time bad debt
write-off of INR 16.5 mn after an NCLT ruling on a pre-COVID case. A 20-day outage in LPG supply from Reliance in March also
disrupted steel cutting and created an inventory backlog.
Order Book: The current order book is INR 3,000 mn, about 1x FY26 revenue. A further INR 1,500 mn of orders is in active
negotiation across refineries, power plants and bridges.
Capacity Expansion: Current capacity is 30,000 MTPA. It is being expanded to 54,000 MTPA, with full commercial benefits from
around November-December. Later phases aim to reach 70,000 MTPA from a single location.
Plant Consolidation: The smaller Khopoli facility has been merged into the main Umargam plant, which covers more than 20 acres
and 0.85-0.90 mn sq ft. Consolidation improves technological consistency and operating margins.
Automation & Cost Initiatives: The company has installed an automated beam straightening and welding machine, an automated
shot-blasting unit with 2,000 MT capacity and a German high-definition drilling and cutting machine. A 1 MW rooftop solar plant,
due by 1 December, is expected to fully offset electricity costs.
Bullet Train Bridges: The company has been pre-qualified and trained by Japanese partners to build bridge spans for the
Ahmedabad-Mumbai high-speed rail line, covering more than 30,000 MT of span projects.
Semiconductor Project: The company is in final negotiations to design and build the heavy, seismic-resistant steel structure for a
chip manufacturing unit.
Other Projects: It has supplied 40,000 MT of structural steel to ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel for its plant expansion. It also works on
refineries (IOCL Dumad and IOCL Paradip), thermal power plants, EV battery units, data centres and railway foot overbridges.
Raw Material Protection: Every client contract includes a price variation clause, so raw material price movements are passed
straight to clients.
Working Capital: The working capital cycle averages about 150 days. Steel arrives from mills 45-60 days after an order is placed,
fabrication and inspection take 60-90 days, and clients pay 30-60 days after delivery. Progressive billing on individual components
keeps cash flowing through project lifecycles of 1.5-2 years.
Balance Sheet: Debt stands at INR 600 mn against a net worth of INR 1,150 mn, a debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.5x. The company
is seeking approval to raise its borrowing limit to INR 4,000 mn, to give flexibility for expanding beyond 54,000 MTPA.
Industry Peers: Peers include Jindal Steel & Power (JSPL), Syska/Syscon and Goodluck Engineering.
Long-Term Potential: Capacity is increasing about 1.8x, and the company is entering high-specification segments such as bullet
train bridges and semiconductor plants. Combined with pass-through pricing protection, this supports the 20-30% growth target.
Further scaling to 70,000 MTPA and solar-led cost savings offer more room for growth and margin gains.

Karnika Industries Ltd
Outlook: Karnika is a vertically integrated kidswear maker running a B2B brand, Karnika, and a B2C retail brand, Kid City, on an
asset-light model that keeps fixed investment low. Growth is anchored on scaling the Kid City shop-in-shop network and licensed
character-led outlets at airports and premium malls, with the company guiding to consolidated revenue of ~INR 3.5-3.7 bn in FY27
and INR 5 bn by FY29, at an EBITDA margin of 15-18%.
Business Model
• The company keeps designing, cutting, finishing, quality checks, ironing, packaging and dispatch in-house, and outsources the
time-intensive stitching, printing and embroidery steps, keeping asset investment light.
• B2B runs under the Karnika brand through an agent, wholesaler and retailer chain, at a net margin of ~10-12%.
• B2C runs under Kid City on a direct-to-consumer basis, at a net margin of ~17-20%, with the company carrying the inventory
risk.
• The company also acts as the sole regional aggregator in Kolkata for online platforms such as Hopscotch and Bonsai and is
signing on more clients.
Kid City and Retail Strategy
• Kid City was acquired to add a ready B2C retail platform to Karnika's strong backend manufacturing, framed as a win-win on
cost and price.
• The network stands at ~75 shop-in-shop stores concentrated in Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, with expansion
planned into airports and high street malls through licensed character-based outlets.
• Around 80% of shop-in-shop stores operate on a sale or return basis and 20% on outright purchase.
Margins and Inventory
• B2B carries lower margins but no inventory risk as goods move to wholesalers, while B2C earns higher margins but holds
inventory.
• Dead or unsold Kid City stock can be cleared at cost through the established Karnika B2B channel, which the company views as
a cushion that pure retail players lack.
• White labelling is under 1%, with both B2B and shop-in-shop sales under own brands.
Competitive Position and Regions
• Against online-first players like FirstCry, the company positions itself as an offline kiosk led business in a different domain, with
a Shopify website launched only recently.
• Revenue splits roughly 55% from north and central India and 45% from south and east.
Financials, Guidance and Capacity
• Q1 revenue was around INR 740 mn at a net margin of about 12%.
• The company guided to consolidated revenue of ~INR 3.5-3.7 bn in FY27 and ~INR 5 bn by FY29, at an EBITDA margin of 15-
18%.
• There are no capacity constraints given the outsourced, asset-light model, with woven and value-added pieces taking ~90-120
days.
• Exports are limited to the Middle East with no major expansion planned for now given the war situation, while value-added
toys and accessories under licensed characters are being explored for higher margins.
• Guidance & View: The Kid City B2C and licensed character retail expansion into airports and premium malls is the main growth
and margin lever. The asset-light manufacturing model and the ability to clear unsold retail stock through the B2B channel
cushion the higher inventory risk that comes with the direct-to-consumer push.

KEC International Ltd
Outlook: KEC's outlook hinges on a transitory disruption cycle normalising from Q3FY27, with the West Asia conflict, water project
receivables, and railway and metro losses expected to fade over the next few quarters. The ~INR 410-420 bn order book plus L1,
backed by a T&D tender pipeline above INR 1,000 bn and PowerGrid capex of INR 1,100-1,300 bn, supports 12-15% revenue
growth guidance for FY27 and sustainable 12-15% growth thereafter, with T&D held at 65-70% of the mix and growing 15-20%.
Margin recovery is the key lever: FY26's 7% is unlikely to be exceeded this year, but FY28 onwards should see normalised 8-9%
consolidated margins as T&D's double-digit profitability stops being offset by losses in railways and civil. Debt reduction of at least
INR 10 bn to ~INR 55 bn by March, driven by Afghanistan, Jal Jeevan, Saudi retention, and arbitration inflows plus ~INR 2 bn of
inventory liquidation, should ease working capital to ~115 days. Cables & conductors is the main diversification story, targeted at
INR 40-50 bn turnover in three to four years with potential monetisation or strategic investment, while renewables and civil grow
at a steadier ~15-20% with lower margins.
Business Overview and Scale
KEC International is an eight-decade-old RPG Group company operating as a global EPC infrastructure major across five verticals:
power transmission and distribution (T&D), civil, railways, renewables, and cables & conductors. T&D is the largest business at
~65-70% of the mix. The company runs eight manufacturing facilities (five in India, three international), six for towers and two for
cables & conductors, and claims the world's largest tower manufacturing capacity at over 480,000 tonnes. It executes 250+
projects across ~15 countries spanning the Middle East, Africa, CIS, Far East, and the Americas through subsidiary SAE Towers.
Order Book and Pipeline Visibility
The combined order book and L1 pipeline stands at ~INR 410-420 bn, giving revenue visibility for six to eight quarters. The broader
tender pipeline exceeds INR 2,000 bn, split roughly equally between T&D and non-T&D, with T&D alone above INR 1,000 bn. Order
intake secured so far this year is over INR 75 bn plus an L1 pipeline of ~INR 80 bn, implying ~INR 150 bn of visibility against a full-
year guidance of ~INR 300 bn, with large awards expected in H2.
T&D Outlook and Growth Drivers
India T&D is seeing strong traction from renewable evacuation lines, with multiple orders from private developers and two HVDC
orders won this year. KEC is executing five HVDC projects for PowerGrid and Adani, with one more large HVDC expected during the
year and seven to eight in the overall pipeline. A notable new win was a data-centre power evacuation order, reflecting emerging
demand that benefits both T&D and civil. PowerGrid has announced capex of ~INR 1,100-1,300 bn over three years, where KEC
holds 20-25% market share. In India, KEC targets INR 80-100 bn of order intake this year within a total T&D intake target of INR
180-200 bn. The annual India T&D pipeline is seen at INR 800-1,000 bn, with an addressable market of INR 500-600 bn and KEC's
share at 15-20%.
International T&D and Regional Dynamics
The Middle East carries a ~INR 500 bn annual pipeline, but award finalisation is delayed by the conflict; KEC has conservatively
assumed only INR 30-40 bn of intake from the region this year. Saudi projects are largely insulated as towers are procured locally
under in-country value norms, and execution there is on schedule. The Americas are robust, with Brazil and Mexico factories fully
loaded for one to one-and-a-half years; the SAE order book is INR 35 bn against annual revenue of ~INR 20 bn, aided by US data-
centre and AI-driven demand. Africa is recovering post-COVID with more tenders, and SARC markets like Nepal and Bangladesh
should improve with political stability, though KEC will only take funded orders backed by EXIM India or ADB.
Margins and Segment Profitability
T&D projects earn double-digit EBITDA margins with return on capital employed above 25% and net working capital under 100
days. India and international T&D margins are now largely at par in double digits, with earlier export advantages of lower capital
cost having narrowed to ~50 bps. Cables & conductors and renewables operate at ~6-7% margins, while railways and civil are the
sources of margin pain. Consolidated FY26 margin was 7%, and management does not expect to exceed that this year, with FY28
onwards seen as the point when normalised 8-9% margins emerge as T&D's double-digit profitability stops being offset by losses
elsewhere.
Middle East Disruption and Recovery Timeline
The West Asia conflict caused a ~INR 3-4 bn revenue spillover in Q1 due to shipping lead times for imported equipment like
transformers and GIS, with Q1 seeing a complete standstill in material movement. Movement resumed in Q2 though lead times
remain elevated. KEC expects to recoup high-margin T&D revenues lost in Q1 and Q2 from Q3 onwards, making H2 growth and
margin trajectory materially better than H1. Management views the disruption as transitory and largely resolved by Q3.

Civil, Railways and Arbitration Issues
Civil has an order book plus L1 of ~INR 90 bn, with 60-70% from buildings and factories at mid-single-digit margins. Water projects
under Jal Jeevan Mission face ~INR 8 bn of stuck receivables and are being run on a cash-and-carry basis with no new orders being
pursued. Metros have been loss-making across four DMRC and CMRL projects, with two completed but awaiting PMO
inauguration and maintenance costs of INR 50-70 mn per project still being charged. Railways is being deliberately de-grown due
to power-block dependencies and weak zonal railway contract capability, with arbitration cases expected to conclude by this year
and profitability returning next year. Kavach is a modest opportunity with a tie-up with Kernex, targeting ~INR 10 bn annual
revenue.
Diversification and Capital Allocation
T&D will be maintained at 65-70% of the portfolio with 15-20% growth. Renewables, including the new wind foray and a record 1
GW of solar commissioned last year, are targeted to grow above 20% but with lower margins. Civil should grow ~15% with share at
15-20%, focused on industrial and selective residential/commercial. Cables & conductors is the key diversification lever, with the
aluminium conductor plant commissioned in March 2025 at 25,000 tonnes capacity generating INR 6-7 bn annually, plans to
double capacity, and new products like elastomeric and HTLS conductors. The business is targeted to reach INR 40-50 bn turnover
in three to four years, after which monetisation, listing, or a strategic investor may be considered. The segment's share is expected
to rise from ~10% to ~15%.
Debt Reduction and Working Capital Levers
KEC guides net debt down to ~INR 55 bn by March, a reduction of at least INR 10 bn, driven largely by one-time inflows. These
include ~INR 3 bn from Afghanistan backed by ADB letters (slipping from September to October), ~INR 7-8 bn from Jal Jeevan
water receivables, ~INR 2 bn from completion of Saudi projects with higher retention in Q3-Q4, and ~INR 2.5 bn from claims and
arbitration in transportation and metro projects. Inventory liquidation of ~INR 2 bn is also targeted, with elevated inventory due
to high steel prices and Dubai factory buffers. Working capital, currently stretched by these stuck amounts, is expected to improve
to ~115 days by year-end.
Guidance and Management Commentary
FY27 revenue growth guidance is 12-15%, though a continued Q3 war could bring it to ~10%. From next year, sustainable 12-15%
growth is seen as achievable given the order book. Management characterises the current set of issues, including the West Asia
war, water project concerns, and working capital stress, as transitory and expected to fade over the next few quarters, with
normalised margins and T&D's double-digit profitability reflecting more clearly at the consolidated level from FY28 onwards.

Khazanchi Jewellers Ltd
Business and Financials
• Khazanchi is a Chennai-based gold jewellery maker operating since 1971. B2B wholesale to jewellers across South India is the
core business and still accounts for 90-95% of revenue.
• It listed on the BSE SME platform in 2023 at INR 140 per share (valuation of ~INR 3.63 bn); its market cap is now ~INR 18 bn.
• FY26 revenue was ~INR 28 bn and PAT ~INR 890-900 mn. Q1FY27 was described as very good.
• FY26 gold volume sold was ~1,660 kg, mostly 22K. B2B volume is ~180-200 kg a month in a good season.
• No B2B client is more than 5-6% of volume.
Flagship Store (B2C)
• A 10,000 sq ft flagship opened in Chennai on 7 February 2026. Capex was ~INR 140 mn against INR 120 mn sanctioned in the
IPO.
• Inventory is ~INR 1.5-1.7 bn, funded from existing B2B stock and a higher bank limit (INR 400 mn raised to INR 1 bn).
• The store is targeted at ~INR 5 bn of annual revenue, reachable next year. After about six months, it is running at ~70-75% of
that pace, or ~INR 250-300 mn a month.
• B2C is ~10% of revenue today and is targeted at 25-30% over time.
Expansion Plan
• The plan is for two stores by 2028 and 8-10 by 2030, at a pace of 2-3 a year.
• Minimum size is 6,000-8,000 sq ft, with Chennai and South India first and locations to be announced.
• New stores are expected to reach ~70% of flagship sales.
• Funding is mainly internal accruals, with additional debt as required.
• Management targets INR 50+ bn revenue and INR 2.5+ bn PAT by FY30.
• It plans an e-commerce platform for lightweight jewellery shortly. The company has purchase and gold-savings plans (3-4
variants), and an ERP system for fast stock reorders.
B2B
• Management guides 25-30% growth for B2B, with 15-20% annual volume growth achieved since 2022. It cautioned that
volume growth is hard to achieve if prices keep spiking, and said it is confident of 15-20% volume growth if prices stabilise.
• Manufacturing is contracted pan-India, and some factories do 80%+ of their work for the company.
• Own manufacturing is planned soon for ~25% of requirements, especially hard-to-source designs.
• B2B will expand pan-India through national trade shows.
• Stock is hedged on a replacement basis: gold is replenished as it is sold.
Margins
• EBITDA margin is ~10-12% in B2C and ~6% in B2B. Blended margins are expected to improve gradually as retail scales.
Gold Price and Demand
• Conversion is ~95% at low gold prices and ~78-80% in steep rallies. Demand slows 1-2 weeks after sharp spikes and then
recovers.
• The company is cutting weights (80 g items are now 50-55 g) to hold budgets.
• Festivals are spread across all quarters in the South, and Q3 is a bit stronger with the marriage season. Bridal accounts for
~65% of jewellery sales.
Diamonds
• Natural diamond brand Vajra Diamonds by Khazanchi (IGI-certified) is pitched for bridal and everyday use, with minimalist
pieces priced from INR 3,000-12,000. Sales numbers were not given.
• Management says demand for lab-grown diamonds is very low in the South because of buyback and resale value.
• Management said diamond jewellery is now about 75% gold, so buyers still benefit from gold price appreciation. It cited the
industry's diamond share rising from 2% to 12% over 4 years and ~25% of marriage purchases going to diamonds.

Kheria Autocomp Ltd
Outlook: The company appears well positioned for sustained growth, supported by high current capacity utilisation, the upcoming
2,400-tonne capacity addition, strong customer relationships and continued demand from the Sanand-Ahmedabad automotive
cluster. Near-term growth is expected to be driven by higher-value product mix, productivity improvements and better utilisation
of existing capacity, while the new plant should provide incremental revenue from FY28 onwards. The potential shift towards sub-
assemblies, turnkey programmes and EV-linked components offers additional avenues for value-chain expansion and margin
protection. However, high customer concentration, limited near-term capacity headroom and the need to sustain its elevated 18-
19% EBITDA margin remain key monitorables.
Company Overview
• Kheria Autocomp is a plastic injection-moulding auto ancillary supplying components primarily to Tier-1 suppliers, which
further assemble and supply to OEMs.
• The company was established in 2009 and commenced production in 2011.
• Sanand, Ahmedabad remains a key automotive hub; management highlighted an industry opportunity from ~1.5 mn vehicles
currently to ~3 mn vehicles by 2030 in the region.
• The company is focused on advanced machinery, consistent quality, delivery performance and faster customer response.
Capacity Expansion
• Current capacity utilisation is high, at ~94-97%.
• The new plant will add 2,400 tonnes of capacity, with the entire IPO proceeds earmarked towards capex.
• Management indicated that project execution is progressing ahead of the timeline outlined in the RHP.
• Existing capacity is ~5,400 tonnes, while the new plant is designed to eventually reach 6,000 tonnes over the next ~3 years.
• Of the INR 650 mn project cost, >INR 250 mn has already been funded through internal accruals, and ~INR 400 mn of IPO
proceeds will be utilised towards capex.
Near-Term Growth
• The company has historically delivered ~38% growth; management remained positive on the current year's growth trajectory
but did not provide formal guidance.
• Management indicated that growth should be visible in both revenue and profitability, despite high current capacity
utilisation.
• Higher-value products and new product selection are expected to support growth from the existing facility.
• Management expects the new capacity to begin contributing from the next financial year.
Value-Chain Expansion
• The company is evaluating opportunities to move towards higher-value products and assemblies, rather than remaining
limited to individual plastic components.
• Management is in discussions with OEMs regarding opportunities to undertake higher-value/turnkey programmes, including
moulding and assembly.
• New machinery and additional vertical lines are expected to support the company's ability to serve more customers and
undertake higher-value work.
• Management does not expect to manufacture the complete vehicle product but sees scope to increase its value addition and
order-book potential.
Margin Drivers
• Management attributed its 18-19% EBITDA margin to multiple operational efficiencies rather than a single factor.
• Key drivers include selective product/customer selection, production efficiency, low rejection rates, automation, manpower
optimisation, technology, power/solar savings and logistics optimisation.
• Goods-delivery cost was reduced from INR 22 per km to INR 18 per km through operational improvements.
• Fuel cost was reduced to 2.95% and machinery repair cost to 0.65%, while freight, bank charges/convenience fees and
insurance costs also declined.
• Management highlighted very low rejection levels, with efforts to bring rejection below 5,000 PPM (~0.5%) versus an industry-
level in-house rejection rate of ~1.5-2%.
• Raw-material consumption is maintained at ~67% of revenue, which management believes is structurally better than the
broader industry.
• Management expressed confidence that 18-19% margins can be sustained, subject to operating performance.
Capacity Economics
• The INR 650 mn project is being designed beyond the initial 2,400-tonne machinery addition, with infrastructure planned to
eventually support ~6,000 tonnes of production.
• The initial 2,400-tonne addition is expected to generate approximately INR 450-500 mn of incremental revenue at full
utilisation.
• At the eventual 6,000-tonne capacity, management indicated potential revenue of approximately INR 1.3-1.4 bn from the
plant.
