Rajshree Polypack Ltd
Rajshree Polypack is a rigid food packaging manufacturer (operating since 2011) across extrusion, thermoforming and injection
moulding, with ~99% of its business from food categories such as dairy, sweets, savouries, beverages, FMCG and bakery. Q1FY27
revenue grew 24% YoY, of which 7-8% came from volumes and the balance from raw material-led price increases and product mix.
Gross margin contracted to ~38% (vs ~43% in H2FY26) due to the polymer price spike from geopolitical tensions, though EBITDA per
kg improved. Exports are soft due to the war situation and high sea freight, while domestic demand remains strong. Management
guides for 10-15% volume-led growth in topline and bottom line in FY27 (potentially 20%+ including raw material inflation).
Injection moulding capacity has reached 5,800 MTPA at 55-60% utilisation, the captive wind-solar project is on track for October
2026, and an eastern India expansion (Phase 1 capex of INR 250-300 mn) will be triggered once existing capacities near full
potential. The key factors to monitor are polymer prices and pass-through, export recovery, injection moulding utilisation, Olive Eco
Pack turnaround, working capital and the eastern India expansion.
Business Model & Positioning
• The company manufactures rigid food packaging through extrusion, thermoforming and injection moulding, catering to dairy,
sweets, savouries, beverages, FMCG, agricultural produce, bakery and confectionery; ~99% of business comes from food.
• It operates three manufacturing facilities in Daman and Gujarat, plus one injection moulding and tool manufacturing facility, and
has a joint venture, Olive Eco Pack, in Gujarat.
• Capacity stands at ~27,000 MTPA in extrusion and ~12,000 MTPA in thermoforming, with injection moulding scaled up from
1,000 MTPA to ~5,800 MTPA.
• Key customers include Amul, Hindustan Unilever, Britannia, Nestle, Tata Consumer (beverages) and Haldiram's.
• Rajshree was the first integrated manufacturer in India to produce rigid barrier sheets (installed in 2021), which extend food
shelf life and support channels such as quick commerce and exports of Indian sweets.
Q1FY27 Performance & Margins
• Q1FY27 revenue grew 24% YoY, with 7-8% from volume growth and the balance from raw material price increases (due to the
war situation) and changes in product mix.
• Gross margin declined to ~38% from ~43% in H2FY26 due to sharp polymer price spikes; however, EBITDA per kg improved, and
Q1 EBITDA margin was ~16%.
• Barrier packaging delivers the highest margins, followed by segments such as confectionery packaging; the company is working
to increase volumes from higher-margin segments.
• Management expects gross margin to recover to the 42-43% range once polymer prices return to pre-war levels.
• Compared with 21-22% margins in FY17-18, the current ~13-13.5% margin reflects a much larger revenue base and higher raw
material prices, which reduce percentage margins even at similar absolute profit levels.
Raw Material & Pricing
• Polymer prices remain volatile and elevated; the company passes on raw material price changes to customers, mostly on a
month-on-month basis.
• Customers understand the situation and absorb price increases; any margin impact is expected to be limited to a month or a
quarter and recovered thereafter, not a permanent loss.
Exports
• The company exports to 13 countries across regions including Europe, the Middle East and China; the Middle East and US are
currently affected, while other regions continue.
• Exports declined in Q1FY27 due to the geopolitical situation and high sea freight; injection moulding export volumes, which
surged ~80% in H1FY26, were flat in Q1FY27 due to the war situation.
• Most export customers are repeat customers; US customers have continued despite 50% tariffs. Strong domestic demand is
offsetting export softness.

Ramkrishna Forgings Ltd
Outlook: Ramkrishna Forgings expects 15-20% volume growth over last year, supported by strong domestic CV demand, a
recovering export market, and ramp-up in casting sales from ~26,000 tonnes to 40,000-50,000 tonnes this year and 65,000-70,000
tonnes next year. The product mix is targeted to shift from 78:22 to 70:30 auto-to-non-auto by FY28, led by railways scaling to 10%
of sales, oil and gas supplies to Caterpillar and Baker, and a PV foray expected to contribute 5-10% by FY28, while aerospace
remains 12-24 months away. Exports, which fell to ~30% of sales last year, are normalising with tariffs treated as a pass-through
and demand seen strong for the next four to six quarters. EBITDA margins are expected to sustain at 17-18% and improve with a
better export mix, while the company maintains its guidance of INR 5 bn of debt reduction this year and INR 2.5-3 bn next year,
alongside capex of INR 4.5 bn this year and ~INR 3 bn next year.
Business Overview and Capacity
Ramkrishna Forgings is a four-and-a-half-decade-old forging company with roughly 333,000 tonnes of forging capacity across 11
plants, complemented by a casting facility of ~62,000 tonnes and machining operations in Jamshedpur and Mexico. It also has a
JV, Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels, to supply 80,000 wheels per annum to Indian Railways over 20 years, with a Chennai unit
being set up with capacity of 228,000 wheels per annum. An additional ~15,000 tonnes of casting capacity is expected to
commence within a month or two.
Product Mix and Diversification Strategy
The company is primarily an auto component player, with the current mix at roughly 78% auto and 22% non-auto. Management
targets a 70:30 mix by FY28, with a longer-term ambition of 60:40. The thrust areas for diversification are railways, farm
equipment, oil and gas, and eventually aerospace, to mitigate cyclical risk from the auto-heavy portfolio.
Railway Segment
Railways currently contributes ~6-7% of total sales, with an immediate target of reaching 10%. The company expects to close this
year at ~7.5-8% and reach 10% next year, driven by bogie frame assemblies and bogie frames. Railway margins are similar to
current company levels at 17-18%, and payments are timely, with 98% received within one month of supply and 2% retained for
quality.
Aerospace and Defence
Aerospace is at a very nascent stage and will take ~12-24 months before any concrete development is announced. No defence
business exists currently, and no specific products or certifications are being disclosed at this stage.
Oil and Gas and Other Non-Auto
Significant orders have been won from Caterpillar and Baker, with supplies having started this year, which should visibly improve
oil and gas sales this year and further next year. Farm equipment and off-highway segments are making steady progress.
Export Outlook
Exports, historically ~40% of sales, fell to ~30% last year due to tariff-related disturbances and weak demand in North America and
Europe. The situation has now stabilised, with the 25% Section 232 tariff on auto components treated as a normalised position
and costs successfully passed on to customers. Export margins are better than domestic margins, and management expects
exports to remain strong for at least the next four to six quarters.
Margin Performance
EBITDA margin improved to ~17.96% in Q1FY27, driven by a better export mix, operating leverage and cost normalisation.
Management believes 17-18% is the normalised sustainable margin band and expects improvement going forward, supported by a
recovering export mix and internal improvement initiatives. Margins are expected to be largely sustained in the coming quarters.
Capacity Utilisation and Growth Guidance
Forging capacity utilisation is ~70%, with expectations of reaching 75-80% this year. The company has guided 15-20% volume
growth over last year. Last year, forging production was ~194,000 tonnes, and casting sales are expected at 40,000-50,000 tonnes
this year versus ~26,000 tonnes last year, potentially rising to 65,000-70,000 tonnes next year.
Capex and Debt Reduction
The company is undertaking ~INR 4.5 bn of capex this year and ~INR 3 bn next year, funded through long-term debt with overall
debt being fungible. It maintains a guidance of reducing INR 5 bn of debt this year and INR 2.5-3 bn next year. The March net block
plus CWIP was ~INR 37 bn, supporting ~INR 90 bn of revenue at 100% utilisation, or ~INR 72-75 bn at realistic 80-85% utilisation.
Mexico Operations
The Mexico plant is currently loss-making and is expected to break even only by Q4FY27, turning profitable next year. The
company sees good traction and growth plans in the Mexico market with multiple customers.

PV and Two-Wheeler Foray
Recent capex has been announced on the PV side, with cold forging, warm forging, and EV-related products already supplying to

Raw Material Pass-Through
In the domestic market, raw material price changes are passed on almost immediately, with at most a one-month lag for some
customers. In exports, prices are adjusted as per international indexes, which also factor in scrap and forex adjustments. The lag is
not material.
JV Wheels Business
The Titagarh JV manufactures railway wheels for Indian Railways for passenger and loco segments, while RKFL standalone
manufactures bogie frames and bogies. The two businesses are distinct, and the JV is expected to supply 30,000-35,000 wheels
this year against an initial target of 40,000, with testing expected to complete within this month and COD declared by the end of
next month.
Order Book Disclosure
The company does not have a traditional order book as business is schedule-based, with regular supply schedules received from
customers. Railway is tender-based, with wins disclosed quarterly. New orders and new customer/product wins are disclosed
periodically, but regular orders are not.

RateGain Travel Technologies Ltd
The company remains focused on profitable growth through a combination of organic expansion and acquisitions, with FY27
revenue targeted at ~INR 31,000 mn and adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.5-23.5%. MarTech is expected to remain the key growth
engine, supported by Sojern and newer AI-led offerings, while Distribution should gradually scale through the Uno platform. Over
the medium term, management is targeting 15-20% organic growth, supported by a large addressable market, increasing AI-led
productivity and continued product expansion, while free cash flow is expected to support deleveraging and create capacity for
future acquisitions.
Business Overview
• RateGain is a B2B travel technology platform serving the broader travel and hospitality ecosystem, including hotels, OTAs,
airlines, car rentals and destination management organisations (DMOs).
• The company focuses on helping customers acquire, engage and retain travellers, while expanding wallet share through an
integrated technology stack.
• Key customer segments include global hotel chains, Booking.com, Expedia, MakeMyTrip, Hertz, Avis, Singapore Airlines, Air
India, IndiGo and multiple global tourism boards.
Integrated Platform
• RateGain operates across three segments: Data-as-a-Service (DaaS), Distribution and MarTech.
• DaaS provides competitive pricing and rate intelligence to help hotels optimise revenue and pricing decisions.
• MarTech provides travel-focused advertising and performance marketing capabilities; it now contributes >81% of revenue and
is the largest business segment.
• Distribution provides connectivity between hotels and OTAs/GDS platforms, while the Uno direct stack enables direct bookings
through hotel websites.
• The company is increasingly building capabilities across the entire traveller journey, including guest acquisition, booking,
engagement and ancillary monetisation.
Growth Journey
• Revenue increased from INR 3,650 mn in FY22 to INR 18,200 mn in FY26, implying a ~49.5% CAGR over the period.
• Adjusted EBITDA margin has expanded from 7-8% at listing to >21% currently, reflecting operating leverage and profitable
growth.
• For FY27, RateGain has guided for revenue of around INR 31,000 mn and adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.5-23.5%.
• The company aspires to reach USD 1 bn revenue by FY31, implying ~27% CAGR, with organic growth targeted at 15-20% and
the balance expected from acquisitions.
AI Pricing Model
• RateGain sees a gradual shift from traditional SaaS/subscription models towards outcome-based pricing, where revenue is
linked to the value generated for customers.
• Its hotel commission product follows an outcome-based model, with RateGain earning 11-14% of direct booking value
generated through its marketing campaigns.
• This product contributes around 40% of MarTech revenue.
• The company is also evaluating similar commission-led models for the Uno direct booking platform.
• No fresh pricing pressure from customers due to AI is currently visible across the other business lines; earlier pricing
discussions have already played out.
Data Moat
• Management highlighted its 15+ years of proprietary data accumulation across DaaS and MarTech as a key competitive
advantage.
• The company has built a large data lake and proprietary know-how around travel intent, pricing intelligence and campaign
optimisation.
• RateGain believes the combination of historical data, domain expertise and customer relationships creates a meaningful entry
barrier despite faster software development through AI.
• At the same time, the company continues to use AI to accelerate product development, with development cycles reducing
from months to weeks.
Organic Growth
• Management expects FY27 organic growth of around 10-12%, based on a pro-forma combined revenue base including Sojern.
• Over the medium term, the company aspires to sustain 15-20% organic growth.
• Management indicated that the overall addressable market across its three segments is approximately USD 9 bn, versus
current revenue of >USD 300 mn.
• Free cash flow conversion is guided at around 75% of EBITDA for FY27.
• Q1FY27 free cash flow stood at approximately INR 1,350 mn.

Rathi Steel and Power Ltd
Rathi Steel and Power, incorporated in 1971 and a licensee of the Rathi brand, manufactures stainless steel products and TMT bars
at its 12.5-acre facility in Ghaziabad (NCR), with ~85,000 MTPA of steel melting capacity and 200,000 MTPA of rolling capacity.
Q1FY27 total income grew 24% to ~INR 1.93 bn, EBITDA grew 24.8% to INR 77 mn and PAT rose ~84% to INR 34.8 mn, driven by
~30% volume growth to 28,372 MT, with TMT volumes more than doubling to 18,677 MT. Rolling mill utilisation improved to ~51%
in FY26 and is targeted at 60% in FY27, while trial runs to integrate the melt shop with the TMT mill have been completed to enable
Fe 550D grade production. Interest rates with the existing lender have been reduced from 16% to ~11.5%, and carry-forward losses
of ~INR 2 bn imply no tax outgo for the next 2-3 years. Management has reiterated 20%+ revenue CAGR guidance for 3-4 years on
an FY25 base. The key factors to monitor are utilisation ramp-up, melt shop-TMT integration and Fe 550D scale-up, EBITDA margin
improvement from ~4%, melting capacity and value-added product expansion, and working capital and debt levels.
Business Overview
• The company has been in the steel industry for over five decades since its incorporation in 1971; it is a licensee of the Rathi
brand, owned by a family trust, for a nominal annual fee (indicated at up to ~INR 500 per annum).
• Manufacturing operations are located in Ghaziabad (NCR) across ~12.5 acres, with installed steel melting capacity of ~85,000
MTPA and rolling capacity of 200,000 MTPA.
• Key products are stainless steel products and TMT bars, serving construction, infrastructure, engineering and other industrial
sectors.
• The company has flexibility to allocate production between stainless steel and TMT based on demand and margins; in Q1FY27,
TMT contributed ~45-48% of revenue, with the balance largely from stainless steel.
• Management positions the company as a pure-play steel manufacturer with a business model different from brand-led peers
such as Kamdhenu.
Q1FY27 Performance
• Total income stood at ~INR 1.93 bn, up 24% YoY; EBITDA was INR 77 mn, up 24.8%; PAT rose ~84% to INR 34.8 mn.
• Total volumes grew ~30% YoY to 28,372 MT from ~21,000 MT in Q1FY26.
• TMT bar volumes more than doubled to ~18,677 MT from 8,200 MT in Q1FY26, supported by infrastructure, real estate and
construction activity in NCR.
• EBITDA margin has remained range-bound at ~4% over the last few quarters, while PAT margin improved as depreciation and
interest do not rise in proportion to volumes and there is no tax outgo.
Utilisation, Integration & Capex
• Rolling mill utilisation improved to ~51% (50-52%) in FY26, and the company targets ~60% in FY27, with stainless steel at ~one-
third and TMT at ~two-thirds of volumes.
• Trial runs integrating the steel melting shop with the TMT mill have been completed successfully; this is a strategic move to
produce higher-grade Fe 550D TMT with better realisations and quality control while mitigating fuel costs, though stabilisation
will take time.
• Melting capacity is only ~40% of rolling capacity, so full integration requires melting expansion; the company will evaluate
expansion once melting utilisation reaches 70-75%.
• The company is also evaluating additional refining equipment to grow its value-added product (VAP) portfolio, possibly ahead of
capacity expansion; capex has not been quantified but is expected to be below industry standards as it is brownfield.
• FY27 regular and modernisation capex is expected at INR 150 mn+, largely funded through internal accruals.
• With idle capacity, incremental volumes (including Fe 550D, even at margins at par with or below stainless steel) help absorb
overheads and improve overall margins.
• The company is EBITDA and PAT positive even at ~50% rolling mill utilisation.
Demand & Market Presence

Outlook: Raymond's aerospace and defence business is poised for a structural re-rating, with the order book at ~INR 59.6 bn over
ten years providing strong revenue visibility and a stated aspiration to reach ~INR 14-15 bn in aerospace revenue in the near term
from ~INR 5 bn currently. The combination of global supply chain diversification away from China, defence offset tailwinds, a
severe engine backlog, and the capital infusion from Raymond positions the company to grow at a 25% CAGR with sustainable
EBITDA margins of ~25-27% and ROCE of ~25% on a steady-state basis. The new 45-acre facility near Bangalore airport, operational
by December next year, will unlock capacity for structural assemblies and special processes, while inorganic acquisitions funded by
recent preferential raises could further accelerate capabilities into sub-assemblies and systems. Precision engineering is expected
to grow at a steadier ~12-14%, contributing meaningfully given its ~INR 17 bn base.
Business Complexity and Product Positioning
Raymond's aerospace component business spans medium to high complexity parts, with roughly 40% of its portfolio in high-
complexity components close to the engine heat zone. While the company possesses the technical capability to produce N1-level
rotating components, it has not yet received such orders, a situation common across most manufacturers. The current focus
remains on N2 and N3 complexity tiers, with a stated aspiration to move toward N1 over time. The complexity mix comprises ~17%
simple components, ~43% medium complexity and ~40% high complexity.
Defence Business Expansion
The company already supplies defence components across both aerospace and precision engineering segments, having
commenced mass production for a defence OEM in the recent quarter. The recent appointment of a senior defence executive from
BEL signals a strategic push toward moving up the value chain into assembly, sub-assembly, and system-level work. While specific
programmes remain undisclosed, management indicated that multiple initiatives are on the drawing board and further
announcements will follow in due course.
Capital Raise and Inorganic Strategy
Raymond has completed preferential fundraises, with proceeds largely earmarked for inorganic opportunities in aerospace,
defence, and precision engineering. The company is seeking acquisitions that bring incremental technology, enable migration from
complex engine parts to sub-assemblies or assemblies, or open new areas such as structural parts and systems.
Aerospace Order Book and Growth Trajectory
The current order book stands at ~INR 59.6 bn over ten years, predominantly comprising confirmed orders rather than anticipated
scope. The shift from a five-year to a ten-year disclosure reflects the long-duration nature of aerospace contracts. With revenue
running at ~INR 5 bn annually and a 25% CAGR guidance, the order book is expected to increase quarter-on-quarter. Growth is
being driven by multiple tailwinds: global supply chain diversification away from China, defence offset programmes that have
showcased India's capabilities, a significant engine backlog relative to aircraft backlog, demographic advantages with a younger
workforce, and Raymond's capital infusion enabling faster capacity expansion.
Recent Programme Win and Revenue Visibility
The indigenous fighter aircraft programme award is expected to generate early revenue within six to nine months, though
management refrained from quantifying the lifetime revenue potential at this stage. For the aerostructure order, manufacturing
will initially leverage HAL's facility due to space constraints at the existing ~3-acre Bommasandra plant. The new ~45-acre facility
near Bangalore airport is expected to be operational by December next year, with ~15 acres earmarked for special processes.
Margins on the structural order are not expected to significantly dilute the aerospace segment's overall profitability.
Margin Outlook and R&D Accounting
The aerospace segment currently reports ~22-23% EBITDA margins after writing off all R&D expenses, which management
estimates depresses margins by ~3-5 percentage points. On a steady-state basis, margins could be ~26-28%. The company has
chosen to expense R&D rather than capitalise it until the business scales to ~INR 15-20 bn in revenue. At a steady state, with
backward integration, operating leverage, and a larger base, management sees a sustainable margin of ~25-27%. The long-term
vision for aerospace remains a framework of 25% revenue growth, 25% EBITDA margin and 25% ROCE.
Capacity and Near-Term Revenue Potential
The existing Bommasandra facility can reach a peak revenue of ~INR 6.5 bn, up from ~INR 3.92 bn last year, with an additional ~INR
500-700 mn capex planned this year. The new 45-acre facility is expected to add significant capacity, with asset turns of ~1.7-2x on
plant and machinery. Management indicated a near-term revenue potential of ~INR 14-15 bn for the aerospace business, roughly
three times the current run-rate, supported by the new facility and ongoing order wins.
Precision Engineering Growth
The precision engineering segment, which includes a significant automotive component, is expected to grow at ~12-14% annually.
The business recorded ~INR 17 bn in revenue last year and is likely to approach ~INR 19 bn at the stated growth rate. While this
pace is lower than aerospace, the large base makes it a meaningful contributor to overall top-line expansion.

Business
• RBZ is an Ahmedabad-based manufacturer of antique and bridal gold jewellery that is moving into retail. It supplies national
retailers across ~70-72 cities, and the promoter, who has been in the business since the age of 17, has personally visited most
of them.
• The first retail store opened in Ahmedabad in 2021 without a legacy brand. Management says it has grown from ~INR 240 mn
to ~INR 4,000-4,800 mn in about 4 years and is still in its growth phase. A second large-format store has just opened in Surat.
• Manufacturing capacity is ~2 tonnes a year at ~50% utilisation. In value terms that capacity has grown from ~INR 14,000 mn at
IPO-era gold prices (INR 60,000-70,000 per 10 g) to ~INR 30,000 mn at ~INR 0.15 mn per 10 g, without adding kilos.
• FY26 reported revenue was INR 6,360 mn. Including ~550 kg of job work, total merchandise value was ~INR 12,500 mn.
• Retail inventory is ~20% made in-house and ~80% outsourced, with RBZ supplying designs to its vendor manufacturers. All
stores are company-owned, so RBZ funds the inventory.
Guidance
• No numerical guidance was given. Management expects bottom line to stay roughly flat in FY27 because of heavy brand
investment, while revenue keeps growing. Q1 and Q2 were positive, and Q3 and Q4 are seen as critical with new stores
opening.
• Store Pipeline: Rajkot before Diwali, and Gandhinagar and Maninagar in Q3FY27 (sites signed and interiors under way), with a
few more stores next year.
• Expansion will not be limited to Gujarat, and franchising may come later.
• Management targets capex breakeven within ~1 year per store. The Surat store is expected to match Ahmedabad's potential,
growing for 2-3 years and maturing in 3-5 years.
• Priorities for the next three years: becoming fully hedged on inventory (starting this quarter and rising each quarter), moving
inventory funding to gold metal loans (GML) and building the brand.
Retail Model and Store Economics
• Large-format stores have ~10,000 sq ft of carpet area, against ~2,500-5,000 sq ft for typical peer stores. Management says one
large store does the work of 2-3 mid-format stores.
• The Surat store is a fully display-led walk-through format: customers browse and select jewellery themselves instead of sitting
while salespeople show trays. Management says this targets Gen Z and new buyers who avoid traditional sit-down stores.
• RBZ follows a no-discount, no-bargaining, no-cash policy. Making charges are fixed at what management calls the right price,
instead of being marked up and then discounted in season as peers do.
• The range covers diamond, gold, daily wear and occasion wear in 14K, 18K and 22K. The new store leans towards studded,
lightweight, daily wear and diamond jewellery.
• Management classes a store as mature at 12-15% same-store sales growth and as growing at 20-25%, with hyper-growth in
years 1-3.
• Management said it does not focus too closely on unit economics for now, accepting some profit impact while building a brand
that can later be franchised.
• The Surat store is one of several possible locations across Surat's ~465 sq km, but the near-term priority is entering new cities
rather than adding stores within one city.
B2B
• B2B demand is still rising. National retailer customers have not raised concerns about RBZ's own stores, and management sees
no cannibalisation so far.
• B2B will stay in the occasion and bridal categories, with no plans to add other B2B products. In-house production for retail is
being piloted for other categories.
• Manufacturing expansion will be considered only once utilisation reaches ~70-75%.
• Management wants RBZ to be seen as a manufacturer-retailer with cost leadership and deep merchandise knowledge, not as a
B2B business with a few stores.
Funding and Hedging
• Equity was ~INR 3,000 mn at FY26-end and is expected to reach ~INR 3,500-3,600 mn in FY27 after brand-building spend.
• Moving from cash credit at ~8-9% to GML at ~3.5-4.5% halves the interest rate. That would let RBZ run ~2:1 debt-to-equity for
about the same interest cost as its usual 1:1. GML is a small fraction of inventory today, and the finance team is working to
raise GML sublimits.
• Management will fund inventory by value, not weight. For example, if INR 1,500 mn is budgeted for ~100 kg and gold rises
from INR 0.15 mn to INR 0.2 mn, it would deploy ~85-90 kg instead of spending ~INR 2,000 mn. Rising gold prices will not
pause expansion.
• No equity dilution is planned in the near term, and management called it a last resort. Debt, internal accruals and franchising
are the preferred routes.
• Management said that over two decades, rising gold prices have not hurt footfalls, and it treats volatility as something to
monitor rather than a major worry.

period through Valentine's Day drive the year.

into advertising and customer acquisition.

Refex Industries Ltd
Strong Growth Outlook in Coal & Ash Handling
• Refex Industries continues to strengthen its position in the coal and ash handling business, with operations across 42 power
plants and an order book of around INR 16,350 mn as of June 2026. The company currently handles ~70,000 MT per day and is
scaling towards 100,000 MT per day, supported by increasing government focus on utilisation of fly ash and legacy pond ash.
Management expects the coal and ash business to deliver around 20-25% YoY growth, with standalone PAT margin
maintained at approximately 10-12%.
Large Structural Opportunity from Legacy Ash Utilisation
• India generates around 340 mn MT of fly ash annually, while approximately 1,677 mn MT of pond/legacy ash remains
accumulated at power plants. Government regulations and ESG requirements are increasingly mandating the utilisation and
disposal of this legacy ash, creating a significant addressable opportunity. Refex is expanding beyond transportation into
integrated ash utilisation, silo O&M and end-destination management, which management expects to provide more
integrated and potentially higher-margin revenue opportunities.
Wind Business Scaling with Technology-Led Differentiation
• The wind turbine business has an initial order book of around INR 18,500 mn, of which approximately INR 16,000 mn remains
to be executed in FY27. The business currently operates at 1-2% EBITDA margin due to imported equipment and its early
stage, with margins expected to improve towards 5-6% following indigenisation. Refex plans to establish around 3 GW of
manufacturing capacity in India, involving approximately INR 4,500 mn capex, funded through a mix of debt and equity. The
company is positioning itself as a technology-led player, initially focusing on higher-capacity 5.3 MW turbines and gradual
localisation of components.
Mobility Business Pivot & Demerger to Improve Consolidated Profile
• The corporate mobility business generated ~INR 1,000 mn of revenue in FY26 but incurred a PBT loss of ~INR 350 mn due to
its asset-heavy model. Management has shifted the business towards an asset-light EV++ model, including CNG vehicles and
contract-based vehicle deployment, with revenue expected to reach around INR 1,700-1,800 mn in FY27. The demerger
process has received the required approvals and is expected to be completed by December 2026 or January 2027, which
management expects to improve the consolidated return profile by separating the mobility business.
Improving Business Mix, Returns & Integrated Growth Opportunities
• Refex is transitioning towards a more focused business mix, with legacy trading activities being phased out and coal & ash
handling becoming the core standalone business. Management indicated that the pure coal and ash business can generate
~30% ROE, while working capital remains structurally elevated at 100+ days due to advance payments to transport partners
and collection cycles of around 110-120 days from large customers. The company is also exploring ready-mix concrete (RMC)
as a forward-integration opportunity linked to its ash ecosystem, although management has not yet provided revenue or
margin guidance for this business.

RHI Magnesita India Ltd
RHI Magnesita India, part of the Austria-based RHI Magnesita group (one of the world's largest refractory producers outside China),
is India's market leader in refractories, serving mainly steel and cement, along with glass, non-ferrous metals and EPC projects.
Management targets volume growth of ~8% (2% above the ~6% steel and cement consumption CAGR) by expanding ironmaking
market share from ~13% to ~30%, scaling its 4PRO solutions model (33% of revenue, targeted at 40% in 1-2 years) and improving
cost competitiveness via product transfers to India, recycling and operational excellence. FY27 EBITDA margin is conservatively
guided at ~13% (FY26: 11.7%; Q1FY27: ~14%), as new industry capacity, including Calderys' ~240 KT plant next year, may intensify
pricing pressure. Capacity utilisation is ~67%, so no capex is needed for the next 3-4 years. Management clarified that Dalmia's ~11%
stake sale was its own portfolio decision and not a distressed sale. The key factors to monitor are margin delivery against
competitive capacity additions, raw material and FX costs, ironmaking and flow control market share, 4PRO scale-up and steel
production growth.
Business Model & Positioning
• Refractories protect customers' equipment wherever heat is required; ~12 kg of refractory is consumed per tonne of steel, and
refractories are also essential for cement, glass and non-ferrous metals.
• The company is India's market leader, with the majority of customers in steel and also cement. The group entity is based in
Austria and listed in London.
• RHI Magnesita offers an end-to-end portfolio from ironmaking to casting in steel, and alumina, basic and castables in cement,
unlike competitors with depth only in certain categories (e.g., Vesuvius in casting).
• India's steel capacity ambition of ~300 mt by 2030 (from ~169 mt) and cement capacity additions provide strong long-term
demand.
Strategy
• Outgrow the market: steel and cement consumption is expected to grow 5-6% CAGR until 2030, and the company targets ~2%
above this, i.e., ~8% volume growth over the medium term.
• Ironmaking, a key bottleneck for steel growth, is the main lever: market share has risen from ~3% to ~13% in 2-3 years without
capex, aided by the group acquisition of Seven Refractories, with an ambition to reach ~30%.
• 4PRO (performance, product, people, planet) evolved from Total Refractory Management to a consulting-led model addressing
customer productivity, sustainability and cost, including digitisation, robotics and automation, to de-commoditise refractories.
• Cost competitiveness rests on aggressive Make in India product transfers, mineral processing (reusing secondary material) and
an Operational Excellence programme to improve OEE.
• Sustainability: ~20% of recipes use recycled material; the company buys customers' used refractories (avoiding landfill), passes
on cost benefits and carbon credits, and has a dedicated recycling unit via a JV. Digitisation and technology programmes target
planning, sourcing and process automation.
4PRO Model
• 4PRO contracts range from 1 to 3 years depending on the customer and portfolio, with the company investing in working capital
and robotics.
• Product margins are flattish to slightly lower than direct product supply due to competitive pricing, but operational flexibility
(timing purchases, kiln utilisation, manpower) adds ~1-2% EBITDA.
• 4PRO is ~33% of revenue currently and is targeted at ~40% in the next 1-2 years; it is positioned as a de-commoditisation and
volume partnership tool rather than a margin enhancer.
• It also enables more trials, better product performance and investments in automation and digitisation for customer
productivity.
Dalmia Stake Sale & Acquisitions
• The Dalmia acquisition in 2023 was at ~INR 632/share (implying ~INR 130 bn equity value); Dalmia's recent ~11% block sale at a
~43-45% discount was entirely its own portfolio decision.
• Management said it was not a distressed sale, noting the block was completed in less than ~10 minutes and bought by long-
term institutional investors, and views the stock as undervalued.
• Since the acquisition, the environment changed: group sanctions restrictions prevent business in Russia, Syria and Iran; INR
depreciated; and geopolitical uncertainty and intense competition (three-digit number of alumina players in cement) shifted the
market to a buyer's market, leading to balance sheet adjustments.
• Cement market share rose from ~3% pre-acquisition to ~43%. Cement brick realisations are about one-third of Bhiwadi plant
products, so lower percentage margins were expected.

• The Dalmia business had ~7% reported EBITDA (~3% excluding one-offs) pre-acquisition and now consistently delivers double-

• EBITDA margin was 11.7% in FY26; FY27 is conservatively guided at ~13%, driven by price increases, operational excellence and

• The company does not give revenue guidance; it guides on volume growth of ~8% (market growth plus 2%) over the medium

Capacity & Competitive Landscape
• Overall capacity utilisation is ~67% on a capacity of ~370-385 KT; optimum utilisation is ~82%. At ~6-8% growth, no capex is
required for the next 3-4 years.
• The most expensive production line is booked for the next two years from October 2026 due to large orders received.
• Industry utilisation was ~68% last year, yet brownfield/greenfield capacity is being added; Calderys' ~240 KT single plant next

Flow Control & Product Mix
• Flow control market share is ~34%, neck and neck with Vesuvius; the company has regained share, especially in mini

integrated plants.
• Flow control contributes ~33-35% of revenue; by revenue, bricks rank first, followed by flow control and mixes/masses.
• Flow control has the highest fixed cost, followed by burnt bricks.
• RHIM is a leader in refractories for electric arc furnaces; green steel is an opportunity, demonstrated by the Tata Ludhiana green
steel contract with carbon credits under 4PRO.
Raw Material & Demand Outlook
• Raw material costs have risen due to INR depreciation (the industry imports from China), higher Chinese magnesia and alumina
costs after China harmonised day and night electricity tariffs, and higher logistics costs from the Middle East war.
• Competitors are not fully passing on cost increases due to new capacity, but RHIM successfully passed on a wartime surcharge in
Q1FY27 for at least a quarter, helped by supply chain resilience while some suppliers declared force majeure.
• Group-level global procurement provides scale benefits; raw material volatility is expected to continue due to currency, energy
and geopolitical factors.
• Steel production slowed in Q1 (partly due to a blast furnace incident at RINL and some demand slowdown), but customers
expect at least ~6% YoY production growth, supported by PLI schemes and safeguard tariffs.
• Steel price increases do not directly drive refractory prices but create momentum for refractory price increases.

RIR Power Electronics Ltd
Outlook: The Odisha silicon carbide (SiC) project will be executed in three phases: epitaxial production starts by Nov-Dec 2026,
packaging follows within a year, and the full fab is due within 1.5-2 years. Commissioning delays have pushed the INR 300
mn/quarter SiC revenue run-rate back by one quarter, so FY27 SiC revenue will be about half the original projection. The legacy
business is projected to grow at a 20-25% CAGR over the next three years.
Odisha SiC Project: The INR 6,180 mn project benefits from a 50% government capex subsidy. It covers end-to-end SiC
semiconductor manufacturing: epitaxial (Epi) coating, chip fabrication, packaging and power modules/systems. The company is
targeting the emerging domestic market for power semiconductors.
Infrastructure: Two Epi reactors have been installed, one 6-inch and one 8-inch. The Epi and packaging operations will run from a
leased flatted factory provided by the Odisha government, and 6 acres of nearby land have been set aside for the future fab.
Capex Deployment: About INR 1,200 mn has been spent so far on clean rooms, Epi reactors and back-end equipment. A further
INR 1,000 mn is allocated to the packaging phase and INR 2,000-4,000 mn to the fab.
Project Timeline: Epitaxial commercial production is expected to start in late November or December 2026. That is about 1-2
months behind schedule because back-end qualification trials and statutory NOCs are still pending. Commercial packaging is
targeted within one year, and the fab within 1.5-2 years.
Bridge Strategy: Until its own fab is running, the company will sell coated Epi wafers to third-party fabricators and buy back the
finished chips to package in-house. This lets it earn revenue before the full facility is ready.
Funding Structure: The company previously raised INR 850 mn of equity as its own contribution. It is negotiating a INR 700 mn
bank term loan, which will be matched by a INR 700 mn government grant, giving INR 1,400 mn to complete Phase 1. The fab will
be funded by a new round of equity and debt, matched equally by government funds. The company currently holds INR 200 mn in
cash and fixed deposits, plus INR 25 mn of undrawn bank lines.
Value Addition Economics: Processing raw SiC wafers into finished devices adds 12-13x value over the cost of the raw wafer. Asset
turnover across the global semiconductor industry ranges from 0.6x to 0.75x.
Niche High-Voltage Focus: The company is deliberately staying out of the low-voltage (<1,200V) mass market, such as standard EV
drivetrains, where Chinese and Taiwanese suppliers compete hard on price. It focuses on 1.2 kV and above, with the main
emphasis on 3.3 kV+ applications in HVDC transmission, heavy industry, data centres and railways. Its global competitors include
ABB, Mitsubishi, Infineon and Hitachi.
Order Pipeline: The company has won an export order from the US for 120 units of 125 mm, 5 kV silicon-based devices for HVDC
applications. It has received preliminary approval for an Army module and expects an initial order for 30-40 units shortly, after
successful lab inspections. Rectifiers for green hydrogen applications already contribute 11% of total sales.
Long-Term Potential: The company would be one of India's first end-to-end SiC power semiconductor manufacturers, aimed at
the high-voltage segment where it faces less competition. That positioning, the 50% capex subsidy and 12-13x value addition give
it a strong strategic position. Execution on timelines and Phase 2 funding remain the key monitorables.

RITES Ltd
Key Outcomes
RITES Limited is targeting double-digit revenue growth for FY27, supported by a record order book of approximately INR 95 bn.
The company aims to maintain a strategic revenue blend favouring high-margin consultancy and leasing over low-margin turnkey
projects to sustain an EBITDA margin of ~20% and a PAT margin of ~15%.
Business Model and Revenue Streams
• RITES operates as a multidisciplinary infrastructure consultancy across various sectors, excluding oil and natural gas.
• Consultancy: The primary revenue driver (50%+ target), covering high-end niche areas like metros, tunnels, and bridges.
• Turnkey: Cost-plus consultancy projects; while they represent ~50% of the current order book, the company targets a long-
term revenue share of 25-30% due to low margins (1-3%).
• Export of Rolling Stock: Exporting locomotives and coaches to Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia. Current orders
include locomotives for Mozambique and coaches for Bangladesh.
• Leasing: High-margin business involving the lease of ~100 locomotives to industrial plants (steel, power, cement).
• Financial Position and Capital Allocation.
• Balance Sheet: The company is debt-free with a low CAPEX model.
• Cash Reserves: Total reserves of ~INR 30 bn, consisting of ~INR 8-8.5 bn in own funds and ~INR 22 bn in client-specific funds.
• CAPEX Plan: Annual outlay is limited to approximately INR 1 bn, primarily for adding locomotives to the fleet.
• Dividends: Maintains a high dividend payout ratio of approximately 95%.
• Market Risks and Challenges.
• Competition: Fierce competition in domestic highway consultancy from small players and international competition in rolling
stock exports from China and Southeast Asian nations.
• Funding: The unavailability of Government of India lines of credit for overseas projects has forced a shift toward global
competitive bidding.
• Human Capital: Acquiring and retaining expert talent is a constant challenge in the consultancy sector, though current
attrition remains low at 2-3%.
• Operational Metrics
• Order Book Composition: As of March 31, 2026, the INR 95 bn order book consists of ~50% turnkey, ~INR 20+ bn consultancy,
and ~INR 18 bn export business.
• Client Base: Indian Railways and related industrial railway networks account for more than 30-35% of the order book.
• Working Capital: Low requirement for consultancy/turnkey due to the "deposit work" model where clients fund execution.
Receivables typically range between INR 8-9 bn.

Safe Enterprises Retail Fixtures Ltd
Safe Enterprises is entering a capacity-led growth phase, with Pune expansion and the Amarnath facility expected to support 25-
30% FY27 growth and INR 4+ bn revenue ambition for FY28. The organised-retail expansion opportunity, high customer wallet

Business evolution: Safe Enterprises has operated since 1936 and has been focused on retail fixtures since 1991, evolving from
conventional store fit-outs to modular, electrified and technology-enabled smart-store solutions.
Core proposition: The company uses a proprietary component-based model, with 3,000+ shop-fitting components developed
through ~5,000 hours of development and ~15,000 hours of R&D, enabling faster and customised store execution.
Capacity remains the bottleneck: Management highlighted that sales, rather than demand, have been the key constraint over the
past three years due to limited manufacturing capacity.
FY27 growth guidance: Management expects 25-30% revenue growth in FY27, supported by incremental capacity at Pune and the.
ramp-up of the Amarnath facility.
Amarnath expansion: The Amarnath facility is targeted to commence production in December, with FY27 primarily being a build-
up year and meaningful contribution expected from FY28.
FY28 ambition: Management is targeting INR 4+ bn revenue in FY28, with capacity expansion, customer additions and business
development being pursued simultaneously.
High customer stickiness: The company typically captures 70-80% wallet share of a customer's store-fixture spend, supported by
proprietary components, consistency across stores and execution capabilities.
Large addressable opportunity: Management estimates the retail-fixture opportunity at ~INR 160 bn by applying a ~20% fixture
share to an estimated INR 800 bn retail-interior-design market.
Organised retail tailwind: Continued formalisation of retail and expansion of organised/value retailers into Tier-2/3/4 cities

Differentiation beyond price: Safe does not compete primarily on price; its proposition is based on design, creativity, proprietary

Manufacturing model: The company follows a "standard engineering with customised skins" approach, keeping components
semi-finished and using different fabrics, laminates, metals and wood finishes for customer-specific applications.
Competitive entry barriers: Management believes the key barrier is not merely manufacturing capacity but the combination of
R&D, proprietary designs, mass production, project management, installation capabilities and long-term customer trust.
New Evolve vertical: Evolve extends the existing component platform into home applications without requiring significant fresh
manufacturing investment, but will require a much broader distribution network.
Evolve strategy: The company plans to scale its franchise network from the current ~5 pilots towards ~50 franchises, with
inorganic opportunities also being evaluated to accelerate distribution. Meaningful Evolve contribution is expected post-FY28.
Jewellery opportunity: Jewellery is emerging as a key target segment as retailers expand aggressively, including lab-grown
diamond brands. The company is already working with a few jewellery players and is pursuing additional opportunities.
Wave/RFID opportunity: RFID-enabled fixtures and self-checkout solutions have successfully completed pilots with customers,
with larger rollouts across 100+ stores under discussion. A POC is also underway in Saudi Arabia.
Technology-led revenue opportunity: Wave could increase revenue per store through RFID, self-checkout, IoT, kiosks and
potentially recurring software revenue, while also creating opportunities across warehouse inventory and omnichannel fulfilment.
RFID adoption: Management expects adoption to be stronger initially among mid-segment and mid-luxury retailers, where
customer experience is important but value-for-money remains critical; value retailers may take longer to adopt due to lower
margins.

Sahaj Solar is a diversified solar EPC and products company, with solar water pumping (PM-KUSUM) historically the largest
contributor, now diversifying into C&I EPC, off-grid/BESS and international projects. FY26 consolidated revenue stood at INR 4.19 bn

diversification, the IDMC partnership, and a hybrid solar-plus-battery mix expected to reach ~50% of revenue. Key monitorables are
receivables collection, PM-KUSUM 2.0 timelines, BESS/IDMC order conversion, Zambia and UAE execution, and margin recovery.
Business Model & Positioning
• Sahaj Solar was incorporated in 2010 as a solar system integrator, commissioning its first panel assembly plant in Surat in 2011.
• The current management took over in 2014, relocating to Ahmedabad and adding a 25 MW plant in 2015 and a 100 MW plant in
2018.
• The business spans solar water pumping (PM-KUSUM), C&I EPC, off-grid battery-storage products and subsidy-linked
installations across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Assam, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh.
• The company has executed projects in Uganda, Malawi and Zambia over six years and continues to explore further Eastern
Africa opportunities.
• Solar water pumping remains the largest segment at 70-75% of turnover, though its share has declined from ~82-85% in FY25 to
~73-74% in FY26 as the company diversifies.
• The company has also begun BESS projects with the Border Security Force (BSF) for solar-plus-battery installations at eastern
and western border outposts.
Financial Performance & Growth Trajectory
• FY26 consolidated revenue stood at INR 4.19 bn with PAT of INR 280 mn+, up ~20% over the prior year.
• Revenue growth had earlier been guided at a 30-33% CAGR but moderated to ~25-28% in FY26 as management prioritised cash-
flow management over new business.
• Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35%, in line with FY26, alongside a 12% EBITDA margin target.
• Margins have been volatile (~10-15%), pressured by rising finance costs and cash-flow stress; management expects
normalisation to 9-10% in H2FY27, when ~75% of the year's business is executed.
Receivables & Working Capital
• Of FY26 revenue, ~INR 3 bn was outstanding as receivables, mainly from solar water pumping, with the largest exposures in
Maharashtra and Gujarat.
• ~90-95% of Gujarat receivables and over 60% of Maharashtra receivables have been collected in the last six months, taking total
collections to over INR 1.7 bn of the INR 3 bn outstanding.

Sanathan Textiles Ltd
The company is entering a strong earnings growth phase as Punjab ramps toward full utilisation and Phase 2 adds further capacity,
while technical textile expansion provides an additional growth lever. Management targets EBITDA of INR 5.3-5.5 bn in FY27, INR
7+ bn in FY28 and >INR 8 bn in FY29, with declining debt supporting cash-flow conversion. Tight industry utilisation, limited near-
term capacity additions, domestic PTA availability and improving export opportunities provide further upside to margins. Key
monitorables remain polyester spreads, raw-material pass-through and execution of the Punjab Phase 2 and MP cotton projects.
Strong growth visibility: FY26 revenue was ~INR 38 bn, while FY27 revenue is targeted at ~INR 57 bn and EBITDA at INR 5.3-5.5 bn;
management is currently on track to surpass the EBITDA target.
Punjab ramp-up: The greenfield Punjab filament yarn facility has reached ~90% utilisation in Q2 and is expected to reach 95-96%
next quarter, broadly matching Silvassa operating levels.
Further capacity addition: Phase 2 at Punjab will increase capacity from 700 TPD to 900 TPD and is targeted for commissioning by
April-May 2027.
Technical textiles expansion: Technical textile yarn capacity has doubled from 9,000 TPA to 18,000 TPA, with the company
expecting eventual incremental revenue of ~INR 1.5-2 bn.
FY28 growth: With Punjab Phase 2 and full utilisation of technical textile capacity, management targets revenue of ~INR 67-68 bn
and EBITDA of INR 7+ bn in FY28.
Cotton expansion: A new cotton yarn facility at PM MITRA Park in MP is expected to commence construction by December 2026,
commission by December 2027 and reach full production by FY29.
FY29 target: With cotton capacity and full ramp-up of existing expansions, management targets revenue of ~INR 73-74 bn and
EBITDA above INR 8 bn.
Punjab cost advantage: The Punjab plant benefits from lower power costs, agri-based heating and automation, with management
targeting EBITDA of INR 14,000-15,000 per tonne versus ~INR 9,000 per tonne at Silvassa.
Logistics advantage: Punjab allows delivery to key northern markets within ~3 hours versus ~7 days transit from western India,
enabling customers to reduce freight and inventory costs while providing Sanathan an estimated INR 1,500-2,000 per tonne
benefit.
Industry utilisation tight: Polyester filament yarn industry utilisation is currently ~80%, close to historical peak levels of 80-83%;
management sees most plants operating near full capacity.
Demand outlook: Domestic polyester filament yarn demand is growing ~6-8% annually, with industry demand potentially rising
from ~4.5 mn tonnes currently to ~5.5 mn tonnes over the next three years.
Limited near-term capacity: No major filament yarn capacity has been announced in India for the next 2.5-3 years, although
management expects some industry players to announce expansions that would take another 2-3 years to come on stream.
Market position: Post completion of both Punjab phases, Sanathan expects to become the third-largest player by capacity, with
an estimated 12-14% market share.
Raw-material tailwind: Upcoming domestic PTA capacity from GAIL and Indian Oil could shift India from a PTA-deficit to surplus
position, potentially reducing landed raw-material costs by ~INR 3,000-4,000 per tonne.
Better cost pass-through: Q1 saw some difficulty passing through volatile crude-linked raw material costs, but management said
most of the cost increase has been passed on in Q2.
Debt reduction: Peak net debt was ~INR 13 bn, but management does not plan to take additional debt for Punjab Phase 2 or the
MP cotton project; peak debt is expected to decline annually.
Export opportunity: UK/EU FTAs are generating inquiries, with the EU agreement expected to provide a stronger boost to direct
and indirect textile exports from next year.
Filament applications: Filament yarn is increasingly replacing cotton across garments and athleisure, while also serving luggage,
seatbelts, home textiles, labels, laces and belts.
Cash-flow inflection: With the major Punjab capex largely behind, management expects operating cash flows to significantly
exceed investing outflows in the coming years as capex intensity declines.

Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global Ltd
The company is targeting 70%+ revenue growth in FY27 to ~INR 14 bn, supported by its executable order book of INR 9.34 bn and

Business Profile & Execution Capabilities

construction, pre-engineered buildings (PEB), electrical, mechanical, plumbing, fire-fighting, utilities, interiors and landscaping.

beverages, auto components, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and steel.
• The company's key differentiation lies in its integrated execution capabilities, in-house design and detailing, civil construction teams,
PEB manufacturing facility and electrical, plumbing, fire-fighting and interior execution capabilities.
• It primarily caters to manufacturing-sector clients and does not undertake high-rise or residential construction projects, allowing it to
maintain a focused industrial EPC business model.

existing clients, including follow-on phases of factory projects.
Financial Performance & Growth Guidance
• Revenue stood at INR 8.23 bn in FY26, following a significant scale-up from INR 860 mn in FY23, INR 2.47 bn in FY24 and INR 3.72 bn in
FY25.

executable order book and anticipated order inflows.

Satin Creditcare Network Ltd
Outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance has been raised from a standalone 20-25% to a consolidated 25-30%, with credit cost
projected at 3.0-3.5%. The FY30 group AUM target has been raised from INR 250 bn to INR 320 bn. The target portfolio mix is 70%
microfinance (unsecured) and 30% non-microfinance (secured), with the secured part split into 17-18% MSME/general NBFC and
12-13% housing finance.
• AUM Composition: Group AUM stands at INR 160 bn. Microfinance (SCNL standalone) accounts for INR 133 bn, about 81%.
The rest comes from Satin Finserv, which serves MSME/NBFC (INR 13.6 bn), and Satin Housing Finance (INR 12.6 bn). The
group also includes a technology consulting subsidiary formed in August 2024 and an alternative investment fund, Satin
Growth Alternatives, formed in August 2025.
• Q1FY27 Performance: AUM grew 22% YoY. ROA was 3.5%, or 4.3% excluding management overlays. SCNL has now been
profitable for 20 consecutive quarters, outperforming peers through the industry downturn.
• Credit Cost & Overlays: Q1 credit cost was 3.0%, or 1.98% excluding the voluntary management overlay. Satin's credit cost
compares well with the sector: 4.6% versus ~12% for the industry in FY25, and 3.8% versus ~8% in FY26. In Q1, the company
built an initial overlay buffer of INR 360 mn, and it plans to expand this permanent buffer to INR 900-1,000 mn.
• Asset Quality: GNPA fell 80 bps QoQ to 2.18%, helped by faster write-offs. PAR 1+ dropped from 5.8% to about 3.0% over four
quarters, of which PAR 90+ is just over 2.0%. PAR 1-90 is held at 0.70-0.80%. Overall PCR is about 115%, and PCR on PAR 90 is
83%, compared with a loss given default of 67-68%.
• Collections: Overall collection efficiency is about 97%, and X-bucket efficiency is above 99.8%. Recoveries from written-off
accounts average INR 350-400 mn a year.
• Satin Finserv (MSME): AUM of INR 13.6 bn is targeted to exceed INR 20 bn by the end of FY27. The product is a secured
individual loan against immovable property, with average ticket sizes of INR 0.15-0.25 mn. Unit economics are a blended yield
of 24-25%, opex of 5-6% and credit cost of 2.0-2.5%, which deliver an ROA of 3.5-4.0%.
• Satin Housing Finance: AUM stands at INR 12.6 bn. Blended yield is 17-18%, made up of about 15% for affordable housing and
about 23% for micro-housing. With opex of 3-4%, the business targets an ROA of about 3%.
• AIF Platform: Satin Growth Alternatives recently made an anchor investment of INR 50 mn and targets AUM of more than INR
10 bn by FY30.
• Branch Expansion: The company opened 392 branches in FY26 and plans to add 60-70 in South India in FY27. A new branch
costs INR 0.2-0.3 mn to set up and breaks even in about three quarters, at roughly 1,000 customers. About 200 recently
opened branches are still sub-optimal and are expected to break even within two quarters. The ideal opex ratio is 6.0%, with
6.5% achievable in the near term.
• Underwriting Discipline: Rejection rates exceed 65% nationally and 80% in the southern expansion states. SCNL is the sole
lender to 45-50% of its borrowers. Sector guardrails cap total borrower indebtedness at INR 0.2 mn. Across the industry, the
share of borrowers with more than three lenders has fallen from 30% before the crisis to 6-7%, while Satin held its own
exposure at 5% even before the regulations came in.
• Funding Costs: Borrowing costs have fallen by more than 90 bps. SCNL raised INR 10 bn under special liquidity schemes at
rates below 10%, and recent bank sanctions came 100 bps cheaper than earlier facilities. The draft regulations capping credit-
life insurance distribution income have no financial impact, because the company earns no distribution or commission income
on policies.
• Industry View: At its peak, the microfinance industry had a loan book of INR 4,300 bn and about 80 mn borrowers. The sector
contracted sharply during the stress period but grew 14% last quarter. Management estimates it is about three quarters away
from full recovery.
• Long-Term Potential: Consistent profitability through the cycle, a credit cost advantage over the sector, a growing overlay
buffer and a falling cost of funds support improving earnings quality. The shift toward 30% secured lending and the higher
FY30 AUM target of INR 320 bn give the group a long growth runway with a less risky portfolio mix.

Sattva Engineering Construction Ltd
Outlook: Sattva Engineering Construction is executing a multi-year expansion, transitioning from a regional partnership firm into a
listed infrastructure contractor. Drawing on 25-30 years of experience in water infrastructure, the company is expanding across
southern and eastern India while diversifying into higher-margin industrial construction and specialised environmental
technologies such as odour control systems (OCS). Supported by standalone qualifications, strategic joint ventures (JVs) and long-
term operation and maintenance (O&M) contracts, management targets a 35-40% CAGR over the next three years while
maintaining a disciplined capital structure.
Foundational Heritage & Operational Focus
Founded in 2005 as a partnership firm and converted into a limited company in September 2025, Sattva operates primarily across
municipal and industrial water treatment ecosystems. The core business spans four major segments including water supply
schemes with household pipeline connections, sewage treatment plants (STPs) integrated with biogas power generation, water
treatment plants (WTPs), and long-term O&M contracts of 7-10 years. Additionally, the company recently restarted its industrial
division to construct turnkey factory buildings, securing an initial ~INR 100 mn order from Bimbo Bakers in August 2026.
Earnings Profile & Return Ratios
FY26 revenue from operations grew 32% YoY to ~INR 1,430 mn. EBITDA margin was 15.4%, down from 17.1% in FY25 due to initial
set-up and ramp-up costs on new WTP projects, while PAT margin was 9.1%. Return metrics remained strong, with ROE of 19.9%
and ROCE of 32.7%. Management has guided to a sustainable long-term EBITDA margin of 15-16% across its operating divisions.
Backlog Visibility & Tender Pipeline
As of 30 June 2026, the company's total order book reached ~INR 5,300 mn (excluding the ~INR 100 mn industrial order bagged in
August 2026), incorporating ~INR 140 mn in recurring O&M contracts. Recent wins feature a major expansion into Karnataka with
~INR 1,080 mn in orders for the Bangalore Water Supply Scheme (covering 120 MLD and 110 MLD STPs), with revenue translation
expected to begin in Q4FY27 following design approvals. Sattva also secured a ~INR 1,000 mn order in Q1 for a 46 MLD STP in
Thirupathi, Tamil Nadu, and is actively participating in ~4 upcoming tenders before December 2026.
Environmental Technology: Odour Control Systems (OCS)
Sattva is currently executing an initial OCS project covering 46 sewage pumping stations in Chennai. Driven by state Pollution
Control Board regulations requiring OCS implementation across 50-60% of new pumping station tenders, management views OCS
as an emerging, medium-term growth vector that carries healthy EBITDA margins comparable to standard STP and WTP projects
(~15-16%).
Top-Line Guidance & Site Pacing
Management has aligned its FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~35% YoY (calibrated from previous AGM expectations of 50-60%)
to account for brief site possession and land handover pacing adjustments. This 35% target serves as a conservative baseline for
FY27, with revenue expected to compound at a 35-40% CAGR over a 3-year horizon. Furthermore, enhanced corporate visibility
post-listing has expanded inquiry volumes and bidding eligibility for larger regional project slates.
Territorial Outreach & Joint Ventures
While consolidating its core presence in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, Sattva holds standalone qualifications for large-scale STP
contracts. To bid for larger multi-state infrastructure projects in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, and Andhra Pradesh, the
company is deploying a JV partnership framework. Leadership is also actively exploring market entry into Patna (Bihar) to evaluate
municipal WTP, STP, and pipeline networking prospects alongside local partners.
Balance Sheet Health & Cash Generation
Working capital metrics continue to normalise, with 95% of pending receivables as of March 2026 successfully collected prior to
June 2026, maintaining the target working capital cycle within 90-100 days. Management aims to achieve positive operating cash
flows for FY27 and plans to cap bank debt by maintaining its existing ~INR 250 mn cash credit limit without incurring additional
borrowings. No further equity dilution or share buyback programmes are currently under evaluation.
Investment Catalyst & Key Monitorables
Primary growth drivers include the execution of the ~INR 5,400 mn order backlog, revenue realisation from Karnataka STP projects
starting Q4FY27, scaling the industrial segment, and rising regulatory adoption of Odour Control Systems. Key monitorables
include the pace of land handovers and site access, maintaining working capital efficiency within 90-100 days, execution timelines
for multi-state JV projects, and sustaining 15-16% EBITDA margins amidst commodity cost variations.

SEAMEC Ltd
Outlook: SEAMEC is positioned for a structural tailwind driven by rising offshore exploration activity and a shrinking global pool of
diving support vessels (DSVs), with only ~60-65 DSVs worldwide and ~9-10 operating in India. Management guides to revenue
growth of 10-12% and bottom-line growth at a 15-18% CAGR over the next four to five years, supported by EBITDA margins of 40-
42% and blended ROCE of 20%+. Fleet expansion is underway, with one vessel being added in October and a second targeted by
financial year-end, though one older vessel may retire next year, largely offsetting near-term additions. Day rates are expected to
strengthen to USD 80,000-85,000 for full-scope contracts, and the company retains significant debt headroom, with net debt
currently negative and net worth of ~INR 15 bn.
Business Overview and Asset Base
SEAMEC is part of the MMG Group, which acquired the company in 2014 from France's Technip. The company owns six specialised
DSVs, manages two DSVs for ONGC and holds one supply vessel. DSVs are critical for offshore oil field maintenance, including
inspection, repair and installation work. The company primarily operates along the Indian coast but has expanded to Saudi Aramco
fields through a two-year charter with Safin, an MDC group company, which concludes around April or May next year. SEAMEC
works closely with ONGC, L&T and GR Infra, among others.
Debt Position and Capital Structure
Gross debt stands at ~INR 2 bn, with net debt negative after accounting for treasury investments. The vessel Anand, costing ~INR 7
bn, will be funded ~INR 3.5 bn through debt and ~INR 3.5 bn through internal accruals. An additional vessel is targeted by the end
of the financial year, potentially adding ~INR 6-7 bn of debt, so debt is expected at ~INR 9-10 bn by year-end. Net worth is ~INR 15
bn, keeping debt-to-equity well within 1x and debt-to-EBITDA at ~3x. Cost of debt is targeted below 8%, given the strong credit
rating and MMG Group relationships. The company uses multiple banking rather than a consortium approach, with project-
specific term loans for each vessel.
Fleet Expansion and Contract Strategy
One vessel is being acquired in October, already running on contract, at a day rate of ~USD 45,000 for a bare vessel charter
without diving scope. A second vessel may be acquired by financial year-end, at day rates of ~USD 80,000-85,000 including diving,
consumables and fuel. Contracts are pursued either as long-term IMR contracts directly with ONGC for 3-5 years, or as EPC
contracts on a seasonal basis from November to May in India. Long-term contracts provide revenue visibility for 2-3 years and are
counted in the order book, while EPC contracts are spot business renewed annually. One older vessel may retire next year, with
the decision taken around May or June based on demand and seaworthiness certification.
Market Dynamics and Demand Drivers
The global DSV population is ~60-65 vessels, with ~9-10 DSVs working in India at any given time, including ONGC-owned and
parent company vessels. Demand is driven by increased offshore exploration activity globally and in India, coupled with limited
vessel availability as older vessels retire without equivalent new builds. These vessels are not built on speculation, given heavy
capital expenditure and long payback periods. Asset prices have moved up with charter rates, though these are negotiated deals
rather than active trading markets. Day rates have grown 5-10% YoY, with full-scope contracts rising from USD 66,000 five years
ago to USD 75,000 two years ago, and an expected USD 80,000-85,000 next year.
Financial Guidance and Returns
Revenue growth guidance is 10-12% over the next four years, with bottom-line growth at a 15-18% CAGR over four to five years.
EBITDA margins are sustainable at 40-42%, with operating leverage improving as newer vessels replace older ones. ROCE is
targeted at 20%+ on a blended basis. The payback period for second-hand vessels is 6-7 years in the current capex cycle,
potentially shrinking to 5 years if day rates continue rising. The company benefits from tonnage taxation, with qualifying vessel
profits taxed at a marginal rate under a 10-year scheme. The net asset value of the fleet is estimated at ~INR 14-15 bn.
Competitive Positioning and Peer Comparison
SEAMEC does not face direct competition, as it owns most of the DSVs in its market. Shipping Corporation and GE Shipping
operate in the lower offshore segment with supply vessels, not competing at the niche DSV level. The company positions itself in
the oil and gas sector rather than as a shipping company, with vessels functioning as main machinery for oil field maintenance.
Unlike typical OSVs traded based on market cycles, DSVs are specialised assets with no active buy-sell market. One small vessel in
the fleet is insignificant to top line and bottom line, with no competition against GE Shipping's similar fleet.
Recent Developments and Outlook
A vessel stranded in the Gulf due to war has returned and resumed charter. A recent EPC contract announced at USD 19.02 mn for
200 days translates to an effective day rate of ~USD 0.1 mn including diving, consumables, and fuel, substantially above domestic
averages. The European subsidiary floated earlier has seen limited progress due to geopolitical situations, with plans to partly
vacate the investment and bring money back to India, involving ~INR 150-180 mn of forex gain adjustments on a prudent basis.
The company remains focused on DSVs while opportunistically exploring aligned activities, with contemplation of building a new
vessel that may be available in three years.

Growth & AUM

CAGR.

• Management expects quarterly AUM growth of around 8-12%, with ~10% QoQ growth considered a reasonable trajectory

• Around 60% of incremental growth is coming from new business, while the remaining 40% is driven by deeper penetration of

• The company added 10+ new anchor corporates YTD, including Microtek, Apar Industries and Bajaj, supporting continued

Supply Chain Finance – Core Franchise
• Supply chain finance will remain the core/hero product for the next 2-3 years, with management targeting 70-75% of business

receivables of the top 1,000 corporates and ~INR 5,000 bn currently financed, indicating substantial headroom for penetration.
• SG Finserve follows a multiple-banking model, typically financing only 10-20% of a dealer's total requirement, positioning itself

• This model results in lower utilisation of sanctioned limits at ~50-60%, but also supports faster collections, with the balance
sheet churning every ~45 days.
Diversification & New Products

this contribution toward ~10% as AUM reaches INR 100 bn, subject to credit performance.
• Digital lending will focus on merchant/business loans rather than retail loans, leveraging transaction and collection data
available through LSP partners such as BharatPe.
• Management intends to test new products conservatively, assess their credit-cost and ROA profile and only then scale them
materially.
Asset Quality & Risk
• Management continues to maintain a nil-NPA portfolio, with collection efficiency remaining above 99%, despite geopolitical,
oil and monsoon-related demand pressures.
• ~99% of collections are received on or before the due date, while overdue accounts generally move back into collection within
30-75 days.

Margins, Cost of Funds & Profitability

• Q1 EBITDA stood at INR 720 mn, up ~26% QoQ, while management indicated a sustainable 4.5-5% ROA as leverage increases
toward 3x.
• Management expects PBT to run at ~INR 3 bn, broadly reflecting the Q1 annualised run-rate.

Share India Securities Ltd
Share India is a 30-year-old, broking-led financial conglomerate, differentiated by a strong in-house backend technology stack and a
large proprietary algo trading engine. The strategic direction is to diversify the profit pool away from prop trading (currently ~50%)
towards broking, led by MTF, and a newly carved-out wealth management business, with prop guided down to 30-35% over three
years. The company guides to high-teens profit growth with gradual ROE expansion, and sees itself as materially less exposed to
market cyclicality than peers.
Business Model and Positioning
The company has been in the industry since 1995 and listed in 2017-18; it is predominantly a broking entity that has diversified into
multiple revenue streams since 2015-16. Its edge is an in-house tech team of 250+ engineers focused on backend, low-latency and
nanosecond technology rather than front end, serving large institutions, AIFs and boutique hedge funds doing derivative trading.
Its exchange turnover market share peaked at 7% in 2018-19 and is currently 3-3.5% overall, with ADTO of ~INR 90 bn last quarter
spread across cash, F&O and commodities.
Proprietary algo trading is ~50% of the profit pool; the balance 50% is broking and allied services (NBFC, investment banking, tech as
a service, insurance broking and wealth management). Algo grows at 8-9%, and other businesses at a 20-25%+ CAGR.
Algo Trading Engine
A pyramid structure of 3,000+ traders on the company payroll (fixed plus bonus) operates within pre-designed algos; no one-sided
or unhedged trades are allowed, and all positions are squared off intraday. The business has been built organically over 13 years
since 2013-14.
The business performs well even when markets do not, giving a very different cycle from cyclical broking; the company expects
performance per employee to rise further with AI, though real impact is a couple of quarters away.
Diversification and Growth Drivers
Share India acquired majority stakes in three tech companies, adding 100+ tech staff: Silverleaf (HFT), AlgoWire (low latency) and
Utrade (retail interface). Employee strength is ~3,700, the investment banking arm has completed 23 IPOs, and the NBFC asset book
is ~INR 2.7 bn, with 68-70 branches.
MTF is the biggest broking growth driver: the book stood at INR 4.65 bn in Q1 and is targeted at INR 10 bn in two years; it was
maintained even in weak markets and built organically. Broking and wealth will take the larger profit share over three years.
Wealth management is being carved out into a separate subsidiary led by a senior industry hire as CEO, with committed capex of
~INR 1.2 bn over three years and board approval for a fundraise (likely equity dilution) drawn on milestones. It is currently housed
under broking, so wealth growth will show up in broking MIS until FY28-FY29.
On the INR 10 bn MTF target: a NIM of 3-5% on borrowed capital (~INR 5 bn) and 15-17% yield on internal capital (~INR 5 bn), plus
an extra 1.5% yield from cross-selling, targeting INR 150-200 mn of incremental profit. MTF contribution flows directly to PBT, with
strong operating leverage.
Segment Economics and Guidance
Allied businesses are high-margin but small: NBFC contributes ~2-2.5% of profit, and insurance broking and tech ~1.5-2%. By 2030,
contributions can rise (IB to mid-to-high single digits, NBFC to the mid-teens), but growth will be led by broking and wealth.
Segment growth: MTF and related businesses at a 25%+ CAGR, IB at 25%+ (cyclical), NBFC at 15-17% (ROE-driven, ~INR 3 bn loan
book), and prop at high single to low double digits, so its profit share falls. Q1 PAT was ~INR 1.25 bn, with a healthy Q2 run-rate;
management declined to guide to an annualised EBITDA of INR 8 bn, as it avoids forward-looking statements.
Balance Sheet and Regulation
Investments of ~INR 3 bn and cash equivalents of ~INR 30 bn are largely FDs pledged with the exchange as margin, effectively
working capital in cash form. Trade payables of ~INR 6 bn are mainly client float deposited onward with the exchange, plus INR 1-1.5
bn of NCDs.
Promoter pledge is given only as collateral comfort to lending institutions, not to extract liquidity. On regulation, most derivative
market headwinds of the last three years are seen as passed; the recent CAS circular signals a more cohesive regulator. Prop is
capital driven, so any top line drop flows with a commensurate cost drop, protecting the bottom line; prop is now an ROE story
rather than a profitability story.
Guidance
The company guided to maintaining the strong Q1 run-rate through the year and high-teens profit growth over three years, with
prop falling from ~50% to 30-35% of profit as broking (MTF-led) and wealth take share, and gradual ROE expansion.

Sheetal Cool Products Ltd
Outlook: Sheetal Cool Products is focused on strengthening its core dairy and ice cream business through deeper distribution,
higher freezer deployment, quick-commerce expansion and product premiumisation. Dairy contributes ~80% of revenue, while
exports and ready-to-eat/ready-to-cook products provide additional growth avenues. The company is also focusing on cost
